title: Magnifica Humanitas: Choosing Humanity in the AI Revolution
location: ON
description:
— A Symposium on Putting Pope Leo’s “AI Encyclical” into Practice 







October 30-31, 2026 (Fri/Sat), 10:30am – 5:00pm 



Father Madden Hall (in Carr Hall, 100 St. Joseph St) 



Free admission / Lunch included: Register now 



How do we maintain our humanity and agency in a world that increasingly revolves around AI? 



From workplaces to social media feeds, from breakthroughs in healthcare research to that question you Googled last night, AI seems to be permeating every aspect of our lives. But as the ways we think, work, live, and act are being rapidly transformed, how do we protect and nurture those parts of our humanity that matter most—our dignity, our agency, our creativity and moral commitments? 



Join us as we discern our stakes in the current AI revolution through the lens of Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo’s “AI encyclical.” Through two days of panels, discussions, and workshops, we will explore how the Pope uses Catholic social teaching to engage with the structural realities of AI, and consider our own practical responses to his call to prioritise human dignity over unrestricted AI development. 



By asking practical questions about AI in light of Magnifica Humanitas, this symposium will help us engage critically and faithfully with changing technologies in our own lives, work, and service to the world. Whether you are new to the conversation and wanting to learn more or are already confronting pressing issues around AI, we welcome you to join us in this timely dialogue on navigating the emerging AI frontier. 



__________ 



Magnifica Humanitas Online Reading Group 



Monday evenings (7-8pm) from Sep. 14-Oct. 19 



UPDATE: sign-ups for the reading group have now closed. 



Are you interested in Pope Leo’s “AI encyclical,” but daunted by the thought of reading it alone? Have you been tempted to ask ChatGPT for a summary? Join us instead for this virtual reading group and explore the encyclical in conversation with others. Over 6 weekly sessions, Dr. Ren Ito will facilitate discussions of each chapter of Magnifica Humanitas. Participants will build an understanding of the encyclical’s key arguments, and will learn to engage with current issues of new technology through the lens of Catholic social teaching. 



Participants will also have the opportunity to present reflections on and takeaways from the encyclical during a session of our October 30-31 Magnifica Humanitas symposium.

title: Cylinder Spectrum & Polygon Plexus
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"Cylinder Spectrum" & "Polygon Plexus" are two visual art exhibitions by Toronto artist Angela Julian (Native Torontonian and OCADU graduate). Both shows are located inside the Sun Gallery at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center. The collected works are a group of large scale colorful abstract paintings done in plaster. They range in size, scale, shape, and number, but they are all tied together through the mediums of plaster and acrylic paint.


On one side of the gallery is the show "Cylinder Spectrum", which is a group of acrylic paintings done on distinctly rounded canvases that were covered in layers of mixed-media and plaster. These are shown both as individual works and presented as a group that makeup a larger installation. The circular nature of the canvases and surfaces links the entire show by their rounded nature. On the opposite side of the gallery is the show "Polygon Plexus" which is a group of hand-made canvases and surfaces that were created to form irregular shapes. These outer shapes are deliberately jagged, pointed, elongated, and heavily textured surfaces, and each painting is covered with a either a geometric or abstract pattern. Both exhibitions demonstrate a variety of different color schemes and embrace vibrant, highly-saturated colors.


The Sun Gallery is the twin space to the Star Gallery on the property, and it is an airy and brilliantly lit space with wide sky-lights that allow for beautiful natural day-light. The gallery space is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably the beautiful wooden beams of its ceilings. These are two very fun shows and run until the end of October, 2026.

Upcoming Events | 918 Bathurst Centre for Culture, Arts, Media and Education https://www.918bathurst.com/events

title: The Face is a Landscape
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"The Face is a Landscape" is a visual arts exhibition by Toronto artist Angela Julian. The large body of art features colorful works done in Portraiture. The show is comprised of drawings and paintings created in a highly-detailed contemporary style. She explores painterly and drawn techniques in both wet and dry mediums. The faces are designed using many layers of blended line-work, impressions, and cross-hatchings. She uses very fine brushes and drawing instruments to achieve these micro-techniques that makeup the broader whole of the picture. The works are located in the Star Gallery and fill up the room from floor to ceiling. The subjects of each portrait are all well-known authors, writers, or philosophers by nature. Angela is penning her first book series in the high-fantasy genre, she has included portraits in the show based on writers that had a direct impact on her as a reader and aspiring author. The exhibition is largely a homage to those writers and thinkers who influenced her.


The Star Gallery is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably its beautiful wooden ceilings. The show runs until the end of October 2026, don't miss it!

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

title: BOOK READING: THE SUN WILL SHINE ON MY TOMORROW, BY SANDEE MACGREGOR
location: Blackhurst Cultural Centre
description:
📚☀️🌅The book "The Sun Will Shine on My Tomorrow,” by Sandee MacGregor, tells the true story of Dorice Lusuli, a young girl in Nairobi, Kenya, who lost both of her parents and was left facing fear, grief, and uncertainty about what would come next. Through the care of her grandmother and the support of a caring village, Baba Nyumbani, she found the food, school fees, and protection she needed, along with a renewed sense of hope for her future.
Sandee Macgregor is a Canadian author based in Southern Ontario. Trained as a teacher, she is the author of two bestselling devotionals as well as two children’s books, "Lucy's Adoption Story" and "Can I Take It to Heaven?"
Meet the author and learn about Dorice's story of resilience growing up as an orphan and about the organization that supported every step of the way.
Free to attend. All are welcome! #ReadDifferently📚

title: Question Everything: Evaluating in an era of bias, spin and social polarization
description:
Part of the Think, Research, Create: Intro to Library Research Series (3 out of 4)
Not all information is created equally—and not all search tools work the same way. This interactive workshop will help you compare popular tools for information discovery from AI to academic search platforms. You’ll learn the differences between misinformation, disinformation, malinformation, AI hallucinations and deepfakes. We’ll show you practical fact-checking tools and strategies to help you figure out what’s real and what’s not. You’ll also practice evaluating sources, including academic ones, so you can choose the most reliable information for your assignments. By the end, you’ll feel more confident navigating the information jungle!

title: Native Plant Series: Collecting Native Seed
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for an engaging workshop where you’ll learn about biodiversity, native plants and how to enhance your garden!
Nature needs your help and it’s as simple as using native plants in your garden! Biodiversity, the variety of all living things necessary to sustain life, is declining because of climate change, habitat loss from increasing urbanization and agricultural practices. Come understand the importance of native plants, how to grow them to welcome pollinators and enhance the beauty of your garden.
 
Session 1: Collecting Native Seed
Discover a simple and rewarding way to grow your garden while supporting plant diversity! Join us for an engaging workshop on ethical seed collecting, where you’ll learn best practices for gathering and caring for seeds. We’ll head out into the Toronto Botanical Garden for a guided session collecting a limited amount of seed, then return indoors to explore seed cleaning and storage techniques. You will keep the seed you collect. To help you get started, the Toronto Master Gardeners will also share a limited selection of seeds collected earlier in the year.
 
Saturday, October 31, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m.
Registration: Public $20, TBG Members $15 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Tina Cesaroni and Pat Concessi
Toronto Master Gardeners Tina and Pat are transitioning their home gardens to more natural environments, which includes adding native plants, shrubs and trees. They collect seed each fall and grow native plants from seed for their own gardens and to share with their communities.
 
About Toronto Master Gardeners
Toronto Master Gardeners (TMG) is a volunteer not-for-profit organization that shares current, science-based horticultural information with the gardening public through various channels, including in person, in print, through the media, and online. Our committed volunteers support and inspire the community, and continually update the sound knowledge required to help them. Learn more and ask your questions Toronto Master Gardeners – Helping Gardeners.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information

For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Survivalist Series: Introduction to Firecraft
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fire-craft-intro-4)**
***Discover the ancient art of safely creating and maintaining fire without lighters or matches!***
For thousands of years, fire has been our greatest ally for warmth, safety, cooking, and survival. But in the wild, fire doesn’t come easy. It takes knowledge, patience, and the right technique.
We are back for the fourth installment of this popular course to teach you the beautiful art of fire. You’ll begin to master the craft with hands-on guidance from our expert firecraft instructor - guide Kyle.
You'll be shown and encouraged to practice:
1\. Ferrocerium rod techniques with multiple tinders
2\. Traditional flint & steel fire lighting
3\. The art of hand\-drill friction fire
This course will give you the foundation to create fire anywhere, anytime.
**Included:** Your own high-quality ferro rod to take home and keep the fire burning wherever you go.
**Who It’s For:** This course is for beginners and intermediate survivalists alike. Bring your curiosity, a willingness to learn, and a love of getting outside. This is an amazing opportunity not only to learn from our expert, but it's a fun, practical lesson at a uniquely low price.
**About this series:** The Survivalist Series is an expert-led set of courses designed to develop applicable and life-saving skills in the outdoors. Keep your eyes peeled for more courses on many other topics coming soon!
**Due to the cost of parking at Bronte Creek, WU transport is recommended for this course.**
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Ancient techniques:** Learn unique firecraft techniques from long ago that do not need matches or a lighter.
**Survivalist skills training:** Develop essential skills to survive and thrive in the wild.
**Fire kit included:** Every participant gets this kit including a ferro rod and variety of tinders.
**Itinerary**
**10:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**11:00** \- Arrive at course location
**11:00 - 16:00** \- Introduction to fire craft course
**16:00 - 17:00** \- Drive back to Toronto
**Event cost: $104+HST. $20 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fire-craft-intro-4)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: 🎃🍂 Halloween Day: The Fall Colours of High Park & Ghost Stories 👻
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🎃🍂 Halloween Day: The Fall Colours of High Park & Ghost Stories 👻

### Fall Colours, Spooky Stories & A Little Halloween Fun

It's Halloween — so why should the ghosts get to have all the fun at night?

Join us for a **Halloween Day walk through High Park**, where we'll enjoy the fall colours while stopping along the way for some of the park's stranger, spookier, and downright weird stories.
High Park has a long history of ghost stories and local legends.

From stories connected to the **War of 1812** — yes, *that* War of 1812 — to tales of mysterious deaths and people who may not have completely left the park behind, there's plenty of history to make an ordinary fall walk a little more interesting.
But don't worry.

**This isn't a terrifying ghost hunt.**

It's Halloween in the middle of the day. 👻☀️
Think **fall colours, creepy stories, a few laughs, and just enough spooky atmosphere to make you look over your shoulder once or twice.**

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 👻 What We'll Do

We'll walk through **High Park**, stopping at different locations along the way while I share stories connected to the park's history and ghostly legends.
Along the way we'll:

* Enjoy the fall colours 🍂
* Explore some of High Park's most interesting locations
* Hear stories of ghosts, legends, and strange events 👻
* Learn a little about the park's history
* Take photos and enjoy the scenery 📸
* Have some Halloween fun along the way 🎃

We'll keep a steady walking pace, with regular stops for storytelling.
The walk will remain **outside throughout** — there is no entry into buildings.

***

## 🎃 Halloween Day — So Let's Have Some Fun

This isn't meant to be a serious paranormal investigation.
It's a **Halloween walk**.

Some stories are creepy. Some are strange. Some might make you wonder whether there's actually something going on.
And some are just a good excuse to tell a spooky story while walking through the fall leaves.

**You don't have to believe in ghosts.**
You just have to enjoy a good story.

***

## 🍁 Fall Weather & Expectations

This is an outdoor walk, so please dress appropriately for the weather.
High Park can be cool and damp in late October, so bring a warm jacket and wear comfortable walking shoes.
We'll be walking at a steady pace, with stops along the way for stories and photos.

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** High Park sign on the west side at Bloor Street West & High Park Avenue
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** **11:00 AM sharp**
I will only wait **5 minutes.**
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🚶 **Pace:** Steady walking pace
🏁 **End Point:** Back where we started

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$10 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This is a **curated, guided storytelling experience**, rather than one of our regular group walks. The route, stories, and history have been researched and developed specifically for this experience.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🧥 Warm fall jacket or layers
📸 Camera or phone
🎃 Halloween spirit
And if you want to wear a costume...
**I'm certainly not going to stop you.** 👻

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This is great for:

* People who love Halloween 🎃
* Anyone who enjoys ghost stories
* Fall-colour enthusiasts 🍂
* History buffs
* People looking for something different to do on Halloween Day
* Anyone who enjoys a good story and a few laughs
* People who want to meet new people while exploring Toronto

You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

**Come for the fall colours.** 🍂
**Stay for the ghost stories.** 👻
**Leave with a new connection — if the ghosts don't get you first.** 🎃

title: Botanical Drypoint Printmaking
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of drypoint printmaking!
In this hands-on workshop, you’ll be creating an edition of 5 original prints using a printmaking technique called drypoint. This medium is similar to etching, but it’s far safer because no dangerous acids are involved. Rembrandt is a well known Old Master who excelled at both drypoint and etching.
 
For botanical subject matter, please bring sketches and line drawings for inspiration and reference. The image needs to measure 4×6 inches; you’ll learn how to incise the image onto a printing plate using a drypoint needle. If you’re stuck for ideas on what to create, there will be pressed leaves available which make lovely subjects. You’ll also learn how to ink the plate and work with an old-fashioned mechanical printing press.
 
Drypoint gets messy, so please wear old clothes or bring an apron. Also, please bring a pair of dishwashing gloves.
 
Saturday, October 31, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $75, TBG Members $65 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature-focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Real Ghosts: A Hallowe'en Exclusive
location: Mimico Centennial, Auditorium
description:
Putting the ‘boo’ in ‘book’, author Peter Roe (
Haunted Town Halls
,
The Complete Paranormal  Investigation Handbook
) will manifest at the Mimico Centennial Library, for an exclusive Hallowe’en visit Saturday, October 31st, at 2:30 pm sharing
The Searcher Group’
s true-life discoveries from the field of ghost investigation.
Over 30 years before reality TV inspired thousands of thrill-seeking groups worldwide,
The Searcher Group
– Canada’s oldest, most reputable and accomplished paranormal research team – celebrates its 47
th
Anniversary in 2026!
Mixing chills, a deep appreciation of Ontario’s vanishing heritage and thought-provoking discussion with a dash of humour, this popular presentation returns discussing tools-of-the-trade, original theory on life-after-life phenomena and rarely-seen ghost photos!
Skeptics and the curious alike are all welcome to attend this judgment-free Hallowe’en event. Bring your own inquiries and experiences to a Q&A following the hour-long talk!
For early attendees eager to secure a seat, a Pre-Show video will start at 2:00 pm, to set the mood.
Copies of
Haunted Town Halls
($20) and/or
The Complete Paranormal Investigation Handbook
($30) will be available for sale and signing with no obligation to purchase. Cash only, please.
*Please Note: Video recordings of this presentation are not permitted, thank you.
About the Presenter
As Assistant Director of The Searcher Group (TSG), Peter Roe also serves as Director of TSG subdivision, Mortal Coil Paranormal (MCP), serving the Greater Toronto Area and southwestern Ontario.
When he is not spearheading investigations and conducting research, he is actively promoting TSG’s pro bono services, publicly presenting field discoveries and advocating against Ontario’s rapidly vanishing heritage.
Peter has appeared in a testimonial capacity over two seasons of the Travel Channel’s Fear the Woods (aka Evil Encounters on T+E Channel), been interviewed by CBC Radio and the Paranormal UK Network, and has earned worldwide notoriety with the release of his first nonfiction publication, Haunted Town Halls (Quagmire Press), in 2018.
Peter is co-author of
The Complete Paranormal Investigation Handbook
with Searcher Group founder Richard Palmisano – released August 18, 2025 through Llewellyn Worldwide.
About The Searcher Group
Founded in 1979 by Richard Palmisano, The Searcher Group (TSG) is Canada’s leading team of investigators, researchers and theorists. The Searcher Group’s mission includes investigating alleged paranormal activity, developing and conducting experiments for the advancement of parapsychology, and researching and developing new technologies and theoretic models.
Boasting an ironclad reputation for safety, confidentiality and credibility over the course of 47 years, TSG has had the privilege of working with government officials and operators of recognized, historic public sites alike, in its ongoing quest to discover and contribute answers to humankind’s most enduring questions pertaining to life-after-life and ghost phenomena.
Applying his 37-year career in law enforcement, security and surveillance in the field, Richard is also the author of five nonfiction publications documenting the team’s most harrowing and informative cases, including
Overshadows
(2003),
Journeys into the Unknown
(2006),
Ghosts
(2009),
Ghosts of the Canadian National Exhibition
(2011) and
Meeting Place of the Dead
(2014), all available through Dundurn Press. He has co-authored an advanced paranormal investigation manual with TSG Assistant Director Peter Roe, titled The Complete Paranormal Investigation Handbook released August 18, 2025 through Llewellyn Worldwide.
Richard and his books have been featured on television, radio and internet podcasts worldwide, including A Haunting (Season 1, Discovery Channel), Northern Mysteries, Portal into the Unknown, CBC Radio, Breakfast Television, Darkness Radio, and Crash Course in Awesome, among many others.
The Searcher Group featured as the cover story of the United Church Observer (now
Broadview
) in October 2016* and soon after appeared in Reader’s Digest (April 2017)

Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🎃 **Halloween Dinner @ The Haunted Keg Mansion 👻**

This year marks our **14th annual Halloween Dinner at The Keg Mansion** — a tradition I started with this group fourteen years ago.

⚠️ **This event fills up every year, and spots are limited to just 30 people. If you want to join us, please make sure you’re committed before signing up.**

If you don’t already know, The Keg Mansion is one of the most haunted buildings in Toronto. Some guests claim to have seen the Lady in the window upstairs, and the women’s washroom is famous for its ghostly encounters. We may not know exactly where we’ll be seated, but the second floor is known to be especially active… if you dare. 👻

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 🍽️ The Keg Mansion

The Keg is a classic steakhouse with a wide range of dishes and price points, so there’s something for everyone. Whether you’re coming for the meal, the company, or the possibility of encountering something from the other side, you’ll be part of one of our longest-running Halloween traditions.

📋 **Menu:**[ Click Here](https://thekeg.com/en/locations/mansion/menu)
💲 **Cost of Meal:** $$$

***

## 👥 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Spot:** I’ll be waiting outside The Keg Mansion wearing my Moose Hat. Please don’t go inside without me.
🕖 **Meetup Time:** 6:45 pm

**I’ll only wait 5 minutes!**

***

## 🎭 Dress Code & Church Street

Every year people ask if they can dress up — the answer is **YES!** Costumes are welcome. 🎃
After dinner, anyone who wants to head to **Church Street for Toronto’s famous Halloween Festival** is welcome to go.

It gets **very crowded**, so I won’t be joining the group or leading everyone through the festival. I’ll help anyone who wants to go together find one another, point you in the right direction, and make sure you know where you’re headed.
From there, you’re on your own to enjoy the madness! 👻

***

## 💵 SAVE YOUR SPOT — PLEASE READ BEFORE RSVPing

**Spots are limited to 24 people.**

To secure your spot, a **$25 e-transfer must be sent to [mathewmaclean@hotmail.com](mailto:mathewmaclean@hotmail.com) within 24 hours of signing up.**
This applies to **everyone**.

It does not matter whether you joined the group yesterday, have been here for fourteen years, or have been a member in good standing for years. **If you are attending this event, you pay the $25 save-your-spot fee. There are no exceptions.**

Here’s how it works:

* **$25 must be paid within 24 hours of signing up.**
* **$20 will be returned to you when you show up.**
* **$5 is the Meetup fee that supports the group.**
* If payment is not received within 24 hours, **your spot may be given to someone else.**
* **There are no refunds for any reason.**

Please do not sign up unless you are **100% committed to attending**. With only 30 spots available, every spot matters.
I’m not going to chase people for payment. If you sign up, you are responsible for sending the $25 within the 24-hour deadline.

⚠️ **Waiting List:** If the event is full and you are placed on the waiting list, **do not send the $25 e-transfer.** Only send payment if I contact you and confirm that a spot has become available. Your spot is not confirmed until I have contacted you and confirmed it.

***

## ⚠️ Important Notes

* Sometimes things happen and I may need to cancel — please watch for updates.
* Please **don’t call the restaurant** — they won’t know anything about this event. Direct all questions to me.
* This group is open to everyone: singles, couples, and anyone looking to be social, make friends, and have fun. We also host movies, walks, hikes, arts & culture outings, and more!

👤 **Organized by Mathew.** For questions, post on the wall or email **[torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com](mailto:torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com)**

Learn Salsa, learn Bachata! Have fun and meet new friends!​ 
Our regular Saturdays become a party on the last Saturday of every month. Experience an unforgettable Salsa & Bachata Party at the Zhulin Hidden Village in Lewisham. 
We kick off the night with Salsa & Bachata lessons. If you’re new to dancing, we recommend joining our beginners’ group. All levels are welcome! No prior experience or dance partner is needed. Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
🎃 Looking for a fun way to meet new people in Toronto this Halloween?

You could walk into a room full of strangers and hope a conversation happens… or you could let us make the first step easy.

Join us for a Halloween Special at Stout Irish Pub, where Fast Friends takes the guesswork out of making new connections.

Through relaxed, professionally hosted conversations, rotations and Halloween-themed connection rounds, you'll meet 20+ people, discover common interests and have plenty of reasons to laugh and chat along the way.

🎃 Costumes are welcome but completely optional — come dressed up, add a little Halloween flair, or simply come as you are.

And the best part? The evening doesn't stop when the hosted rounds do.
Afterwards, stick around at Stout for 50+ board games, drinks and more time to socialise with the people you've just met. 🎲🍻

Book Early & Save: [https://toronto31stoct.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto31stoct.eventbrite.co.uk)
Early Bird: CAD $10 \| Regular: CAD $15 \| Door: CAD $20 cash

Advance tickets help us plan the right space and group size and ensure a well-organised experience for everyone.

🤝 What to Expect
7:00 PM — Welcome & Drinks
Meet your host, Kruttika, grab a drink and settle in.
Coming alone? You're in good company. Many of our guests arrive solo, and our host will help you get comfortable, make introductions and get the evening started.

7:30–8:30 PM — Hosted Fast Friends
This is where the evening really gets going.
You'll have a series of short, guided conversations, moving around the group so you get the chance to meet a variety of people rather than spending the whole evening talking to just one person.
No need to walk up to strangers and figure out what to say — we've created the structure for you.

🎃 Halloween-Themed Connection Rounds
Alongside the regular Fast Friends conversations, we'll add some Halloween-inspired themed rounds with fun prompts and challenges designed to get people laughing, talking and discovering what they have in common.
Expect a few seasonal twists — nothing complicated, just an easy way to make the conversations even more fun.

🎲 8:30 PM onwards — 50+ Board Games & Socialising
Don't feel like heading home after the hosted rounds?
Stay and keep the evening going at Stout.
With 50+ board games available, you can join a game with people you've met, grab another drink, continue a conversation or simply mingle and see where the evening takes you.
You don't need to be a serious gamer — the games are simply another easy way to keep people interacting.

🍻 And if you're staying later, Stout's After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.

title: THE FAMILY CROW: A Murder Mystery
location: Factory Theatre,125 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5V 2R2, Canada
description:
The Family Crow: A Murder Mystery


A MURDER murder mystery - and the 100th performance of an acclaimed Canadian puppet show


Internationally acclaimed puppeteer Adam Francis Proulx returns to Toronto this Halloween for the 100th performance of THE FAMILY CROW: A Murder Mystery at Factory Theatre.


A group of crows is called a murder. So what happens when there is an actual murder amongst a group of crows?


You get a MURDER murder mystery!


Enter Horatio P. Corvus, an increasingly exasperated detective with one hour, five crows, and zero patience. When a murder is committed within a family of crows, Horatio must sort through the evidence, interrogate the suspects and uncover the truth before the killer gets away.


Performed by a singular actor but bringing six characters to life (and death?), The Family Crow is a puppet-fuelled, pun-filled theatrical mystery packed with atmosphere, absurdity and twists. It's a show for anyone who loves a good story, a good pun, and a good old-fashioned whodunit—with a distinctly avian sense of humour.


This special Toronto engagement marks the 100th performance of the show, making Halloween night an especially appropriate time to return to the scene of the crime.


Critics have embraced the show's peculiar combination of puppetry, comedy and mystery. Liz Nicolls of Edmonton called it “weird, cuckoo brilliance” and “a bona fide theatrical caws célèbre,” while Glenn Sumi of NOW Magazine described it as “delightfully atmospheric.” The Saskatoon StarPhoenix declared that audiences would be “crowing about it to all your friends,” while CJSF called it “definitely a must-see.”


The production is directed by Byron Laviolette, a director and dramaturg who has worked with interactive art forms for more than twenty-five years. His work spans clown, puppetry, immersive theatre, audio storytelling and interactive performance. He was the founding Artistic Director of What The Festival, a founding member of Morro and Jasp, and is Resident Director of Pucking Fuppet Co.


About Adam Francis Proulx


Adam Francis Proulx is a Dora-nominated Canadian theatre artist and one of Canada's most sought-after puppeteers. He is best known for his solo shows, including The Family Crow: A Murder Mystery and Baker's Dozen: 12 Angry Puppets, as well as the family musical Emilio's A Million Chameleons, which recently celebrated an Off-Broadway run.


Beyond his own creations, Proulx has appeared in the first Canadian companies of Avenue Q and Disney's Frozen, and has worked across North America. He performs as Fuzz the hamster on the Canadian Screen Award-winning The Fabulous Show with Fay & Fluffy on Family Jr., where he also writes for the series. In 2025, he was a Protégé recipient of the Johanna Metcalf Awards for the Performing Arts.

JUNO & GRAMMY nominated jazz/hip-hop trumpet playing iconoclast BROWNMAN ALI (Jay-z, Missy Elliot, Kanye West, Guru's Jazzmatazz) will once again lead an all-star quartet through his popular annual HALLOWEEN THRILLER concert, this year travelling up from Brooklyn, NY to various venues (and schools) across Southern Ontario. The much lauded BROWNMAN ELECTRYC TRIO + 1 will perform the entire Michael Jackson "Thriller" recording, interpreted and re-worked in the Miles Davis-esque fashion this multiple National Jazz Award winning improviser has become known for. In addition to the quartet performing Thriller from top to bottom, other MJ classics will be featured through the night for this unique Halloween Series jazz party. Costumes and Thriller video dance moves encouraged!

[ TICKETS: http://www.eventbrite.ca/e/2001549304851 ]

This show features as it's "+1" acclaimed keyboardist NICK MACLEAN -- a JUNO Award nominee, a signee to Brownman's Browntasauras Records label & winner of 10 Global Music Awards -- standing alongside 2 of Toronto's most in demand musicians : SEAN DENNIS on 6-string electric bass (called "a once in a generation bass player" by the Head of the Humber College Bass Department when he was a student there), and ADAM MANSFIELD on drums (25-year old drumset phenom), all under the direction of 2x National Jazz Award winning modern jazz trumpet iconoclast BROWNMAN ALI. Please visit http://www.Thriller.Brownman.com for more info on this year's Halloween Thriller Series.

"Delving so deeply into that record always leaves us speechless", states Ali. "Michael birthed so many incredible tunes over the years, but his collaborations with Quincy Jones on Thriller has to be one of the most towering musical achievements in pop music ever. Using that brilliant material every year on Halloween, as jump-offs for what we do makes for a party that's both danceable, but still rooted in exploratory improvising and deep reaching solos. We approach it the way Miles might have."

The BROWNMAN ELECTRYC TRIO has won a National Jazz Award, 3 Toronto Independent Music Awards, a SOCAN music award, a CBC Galaxie Rising Star Award, and an International Independent Music Award for "Jazz-Funk album of the year" for their latest release "Gravitation", which hit number 4 on the iTunes USA jazz charts upon it's release.

Heralded as “Canada’s preeminent Jazz trumpeter” by NYC’s Village Voice, Brownman Ali - born on the small Caribbean island of Trinidad, & schooled in NYC - is a multiple award-winning NYC-schooled protégé to his teacher, Grammy-winning trumpet legend, Randy Brecker. Splitting his time between Toronto and New York, he tirelessly leads 8 unique ensembles of his own including the internationally acclaimed Miles Davis influenced BROWNMAN ELECTRYC TRIO, and the award-winning CRUZAO latin-jazz quintet. All these ensembles record under Brownman's own much lauded BROWNTASAURAS RECORDS label, established in 2009. In high demand in the studio world with over 300 CD appearances to date, Brownman delivers stylistically authentic horn playing over a wide range of styles from bebop to hiphop having worked with the likes of Guru's Jazzmatazz (replacing Donald Byrd in that primordial ensemble), Mos Def, KRS-1, Quincy Jones, Paul Simon, Jay-z, Missy Elliot, Mingus Dynasty Big Band, Gary Bartz, Chucho Valdes & far too many more to name here. He is considered to be one of the most unique and provocative improvising trumpet players in the nation today and is widely regarded as a vanguard for the evolution of Jazz in Canada.

title: Branch Art Exhibit: Storytelling -- works by Adira Rotstein
location: Deer Park, Main Floor
description:
Throughout the month of November, the works of artist Adira Rotstein are on display at
Deer Park branch
.
Adira Rotstein is a Toronto artist, writer and teacher. Her YA novels 'Little Jane Silver' and 'Little Jane and the Nameless Isle' are published by Dundurn. She has experience in sequential art, creating comic books and illustrating stories. She also loves experimenting with the boundaries of stopmotion and hand drawn animation. I am curious about the world in all beauty and absurdity
"Usually, with my artwork I attempt to tell a story. People say I am able to imbue even inanimate objects with a personality, human agency and warmth. People's faces, their motions, their discarded objects at rest tell stories about where they have been, what they have felt and where they are going. Slow down and see what they have to say. Even the smallest among us has a perspective worth learning about and a beauty worth sensing."
This exhibit is part of TPL's
Art Exhibit Space
program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighbourhoods.
The exhibit can be viewed during Deer Park's open hours. Please check the
Deer Park branch
page before your visit.
Free. All are welcome.
Image credit
Artist: Adira Rotstein
Title of Piece: Little Jane Silver frontpiece
Medium: water colour pencil on paper
Size/Dimensions: small (up to 13 cm x 18 cm)

title: Exploring Mount Nemo
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/mt-nemo-fall-26)**
**Mount Nemo is one of the best parts of the Niagara Escarpment and it's only a short drive from the city!**
We'll follow the Bruce Trail for about 7 km along the top of the ridge, through old forest that grows right up to the cliff’s edge. Within a few minutes, while immersed in this UNESCO biosphere reserve, Toronto feels a lot further away than it is.
This isn't a simple stroll but it is accessible for anybody wanting to get into hiking. The ground is broken up in the best way, with rock, roots and the odd scramble, and the route keeps changing character as we go.
November is a good month to do it. The trail is quieter than in peak fall colour season, and depending on the year some leaves may still be hanging on. Most people arrive not knowing anyone, and by the time we're back at the cars you'll likely have a few new trail friends.
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Close to the City:** It's an hour drive from Toronto, which makes this one of the easiest ways to get onto the escarpment.
**Views:** Whatever colour is left in the forest, set against the dark green of the cedars. Bare branches also mean longer sightlines across the valley.
**Meet Your Crew:** A day on the trail with fellow members of the WU crew, and a few new people to plan the next hike with.
**Itinerary**
**10:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele Station
**10:00 - 11:00** \- Drive to trail head
**11:00 - 15:30** \- Hike the trail with a stop for lunch along the way
**15:30 - 16:30** \- Drive back to Toronto
**Event cost: $55+HST. $40 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/mt-nemo-fall-26)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Branch Art Exhibit: My Red Is Not Your Red by Francesco Leka
location: Northern District, 2nd floor Art gallery
description:
Throughout the month of November, the works of artist Francesco Leka are on display at Northern District library.
Francesco Leka is a self-taught Canadian artist from Toronto who balances his artistic practice with his studies in Health Sciences at the University of Ottawa. While pursuing a future career in medicine, he continues to develop his art independently and with dedication.
"In my work, I find in witnessing viewers interpret the densely packed symbolic elements into their own narratives. Conceptually, my works explore the illusions people cling to—nostalgia, order, wealth—and the harsher truths underlying them. Visually, scenes in my oil paintings draw inspiration from the awe of nature, aesthetic qualities of myths, and my own visual interpretations of music."
This exhibit is part of TPL's
Art Exhibit Space
program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighborhoods.
The exhibit can be viewed during Northern District library's opening hours.
Free. All are welcome.

Organized by Professor Ebrahim Ghafar-Zadeh, Undergraduate Program Director in Engineering, the showcase will feature 10 faculty presentations, live demonstrations, laboratory tours, and interactive discussions highlighting research and innovation across electrical engineering.
Participants will explore a wide range of topics, including communications, control systems, optoelectronics, analog and digital electronics, artificial intelligence on chips, power electronics, electric vehicles, wearable and implantable devices, and biomedical engineering.
The event will provide a valuable opportunity for students, particularly first-year engineering students, to discover the breadth of electrical engineering, learn about research and career pathways, interact with faculty members and graduate students, and experience cutting-edge technologies through demonstrations and laboratory visits.
Complimentary lunch and networking opportunities will be provided, allowing attendees to connect with faculty, graduate students, and peers in an informal and welcoming environment.
All first-year engineering students are especially encouraged to attend. Students from other years who are interested in electrical engineering are also welcome.
Registration: Scan the QR code on the event flyer to reserve your spot.
Join us to discover how electrical engineering is shaping a smarter, healthier, and more sustainable future!
Be Inspired. Discover Opportunities. Shape the Future.

title: Silvia Bonoli (Donostia International Physics Center)
location: MP 1318A
description:
Title: Constraining the growth of massive black holes with a population-level multi-messenger approach

Abstract: JWST’s discovery of a large population of active black holes at z > 5, and the evidence from Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs) for a gravitational-wave background likely produced by supermassive black hole binaries, offer new constraints on the growth and evolution of massive black holes. Both observations challenge standard expectations. JWST points to more numerous or more rapidly growing black holes at earlier times than many models predict, while the estimated PTA amplitude seems to require a larger-than-expected population of very massive black holes at low redshift. Meanwhile, tidal disruption events (TDEs) open a window onto the elusive population of intermediate-mass black holes. In this talk, I will present L-GalaxiesBH, a semi-analytic model that follows the formation, growth and dynamics of massive black holes and their host galaxies from the first seeds to the local Universe. I will then show how we jointly confront it with JWST, PTA and TDE data to constrain the model’s parameters and piece together the evolutionary history of massive black holes.

description:

title: It Takes Time: producing theatre with The Howland Company
location: Joe G. Green Theatre, Centre for Film and Theatre @ York University, 4700 Keele Street, Toronto, ON
description:
Join us for wide ranging conversation with The Howland Company ( https://howlandcompanytheatre.com/ ) Founding Members Ruth Goodwin, Cam Laurie and Courtney Ch’ng Lancaster, as they discuss the production history of Casimir and Caroline and the gifts and challenges of running a theatre company with your friends.
Date: Monday November 2, 2026
Time: 6:30 pm
Location: Joseph G. Green Theatre
Free Admission
The Howland Company was founded 13 years ago as a vehicle for ten emerging theatre artists to create work for themselves. Since its inception, the company has produced nearly 20 shows at various sizes and scales included the world premiere of Casimir and Caroline, first collectively workshopped in 2015 before premiering in January 2020.
Most recently The Howland Company co-produced Lucy Kirkwood’s The Welkin with Soulpepper and Crows’ Theatre (nominated for 5 2026 Dora Awards), produced Susanna Fournier’s take rimbaud, a new work first commissioned in 2013 (nominated for 5 2026 Dora Awards), and were selected for the 2026 Best of Fringe with YOU CHOOSE: An Improvised Murder Mystery.
We will also share a special sneak peek screening of THAT WHICH IS HEARD, an intimate documentary short that follows actress Shruti Kothari, whose Dora Award–winning performance in Howland’s Casimir and Caroline captivated audiences in January 2020. Just weeks after the show closed — and only days before the pandemic shut down theatres worldwide — Shruti’s life changed dramatically when she suffered a stroke at the age of 30. Her road to recovery and a return to the stage is chronicled in this documentary short directed by Ken Pham and produced by Ruth Goodwin, Kirthiga Rajanayagam and Shruti Kothari.
PARTICIPATING ARTISTS
Ruth Goodwin is a Toronto-based actor, writer, producer and director. She is best known for her roles on Global TV’s Private Eyes and Netflix’s Wedding Season, alongside appearances on Baroness Von Sketch, Workin’ Moms and Murdoch Mysteries and more. She also recently starred opposite Academy Award Winner Adrien Brody in a Super Bowl commercial ranked among the year’s Top 10 by The New York Times.
Ruth is a founding artist of Toronto’s critically acclaimed Howland Company, where her work has earned her numerous Dora Mavor Moore Award nominations, Best of Fringe Awards and a Toronto Theatre Critics Award. She also received a Canadian Comedy Award nomination for her improvised stage show Entrances and Exits, alongside Colin Mochrie, Andrew Phung and Elizabeth Johnston. She has been named a “Top Artist to Watch” by the Toronto Star and NOW Magazine.
Beyond acting, Ruth spent six years as a Segment Producer for CTV’s Canada AM before producing the short film Stuck, which has amassed over 50 million views on Amazon Prime. She made her film directorial debut with The Strangers’ Case, currently streaming on CBC Gem.
Cameron Laurie is a Toronto based actor and theatre producer. He is a Founder and Artistic Leader of The Howland Company, where he has performed in a number of shows including The Welkin, Heroes of the Fourth Turning, Prodigal, Three Sisters, Punk Rock and Casimir & Caroline, for which he won a Dora Mavor Moore Award for Outstanding Ensemble. Other theatre credits include Saving Graceland, The Trials of Maggie Pollock, The Donnelly’s Trilogy, The Drawer Boy, Our Beautiful Sons (Blyth Festival), A Little Closer (The Vault Creation Lab), The Merchant of Venice (Shakespeare Bash’d).

title: Discussion & Reading of 2001: A Space Odyssey
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi all,

We've been invited to an evening at the Symphony Space Leonard Nimoy Thalia Theater, and I hope you can make it! A panel of actors, thinkers, and writers will discuss Arthur C. Clarke's 1968 classic *2001: A Space Odyssey*. The panel will discuss emergent artificial intelligence, space exploration, and the limits of human power. There will also be a reading from the prolific actor Stephen Lang (Avatar).
.
**Purchase your tickets for this event via the [Symphony Space website](https://www.symphonyspace.org/events/thalia-book-club-arthur-c-clarkes-2001-a-space-odyssey), your rsvp to this Meetup event is not enough.** Use the code *Hal* at checkout to get your ticket at the special discount price of $15. Get your tickets asap, this event will sell out!
.
Our Book Club read *[2001: A Space Odyssey](https://www.meetup.com/thescifibookclub/events/296342688/)* in 2024 and loved it. If you have not had the pleasure, I highly recommend picking it up. The novel was written by Clarke concurrently with Stanley Kubrick's writing of the film. It weaves in and out of what you've seen on screen, crafted by one of the great literary minds of our time. We'll likely discuss 2001 more at our [Open Signal virtual event](https://www.meetup.com/thescifibookclub/events/316438957) on November 12th.

Thanks again to Symphony Space for inviting us to this really interesting event!

Jon & Meghan

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Botanical Leaf Painting Workshop: 4-sessions
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a four-week introduction course and learn the basics of botanical leaf painting!
Learn how to paint a realistic oak leaf using watercolour paint and colour pencil. Participants will learn how to mix and layer colour washes in order to create an image that has depth and feels true to life. Our instructor will guide each stage of the process through group demonstrations and provide individual attention. Attendees will observe and paint from actual pressed oak leaves (we will not be copying photos).
 
Beginners welcome. All art materials will be provided.
 
Tuesdays, November 3 through 24, 1 to 3 p.m. (four sessions)
Public $125, TBG Members $110 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine-inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing, and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

location: Victoria Village
description:
Author, Kath Jonathan presents and discusses the characters, conflicts and family theme of her bestselling novel, “
The Resistance Painter
”. This dual timeline World War II story is set in 1940's Warsaw, Poland and 2010 Toronto, Canada.
The presentation begins with a short reading, then a description of her WWII, dual timeline novel, The Resistance Painter, its main characters, conflicts, themes and questions. More specifically these include the question which haunts the main female characters: How do you live with integrity and compassion in the middle of a war? It’s a question the audience is asked to personally hold in place during the presentation for discussion later. The 1940’s Warsaw narrative centers the young painter, Irena, who joins the Polish resistance army and makes art as a record of war, and later, after a terrible wartime betrayal, continues making art in Toronto as a means of survival.
Drop-In.
The Resistance Painter

title: Let's Make a Graphic Novel! Workshop with Tory Woollcott

description:
Led by the professional cartoonist, Tory Woollcott, this workshop teaches the fundamentals of story outlining and narrative structure as it applies to comics & graphic novels, prose, or even video games! Drop in, limited spots.
Tory Woollcott is a Toronto-based author, illustrator, designer, and educator whose work spans graphic novels, science comics, audio dramas, podcasts, and kids' books. She is the author of Science Comics: The Brain: The Ultimate Thinking Machine (First Second Books), a vibrant and accessible exploration of neuroscience, illustrated by Alex Graudins. Her debut graphic novel, Mirror Mind, is a celebrated autobiography that recounts her experiences growing up with dyslexia. Other notable works include the audio drama Awake with Sparklermonthly, the travel diary Toronto to Tuscany (created in collaboration with Kean Soo), and two successful Kickstarter campaigns: the Tessera Oracle and its follow-up, the Trine Oracle.

title: Civic Meetup #567: Insights from the Tracking (In)justice Project
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom / Metro Hall
description:
Topic: Insights from the Tracking (In)justice Project

Last year, 61 people died in interactions with the police or in incarceration facilities across the country. Historically, we lacked means for systematically tracking even basic details of the circumstances around these deaths, including rudimentary demographic information (who was killed?), geographic (where were they killed?), as well as investigative outcomes (were any officials held responsible?), and journalistic coverage (has there been any reporting about this)? With a team of researchers spanning Carleton, McGill, Queens, UofT, and UBC, we are developing the Tracking (In)Justice project to systematically and transparently catalogue the circumstances around these deaths, drawing on a mix of sources from government releases, news reporting, and meticulous case-by-case fact checking, tracking these critical details from 2000 onwards.

‎

Speaker: Farhan Samir (he/him) (in-person)

Farhan Samir is a Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC) Postdoctoral Fellow in the Computer Science department at the University of Toronto. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia, where his work was supported by an NSERC Doctoral Fellowship, a UBC Public Scholars Initiative award, and the 2024-25 UBC Department of Statistics Award in Data Science. He was formerly a researcher at NVIDIA, Amazon Science, and the Allen Institute for AI.

‎

Agenda:

7:00-7:20 Welcome and Introductions

7:20-7:50 Presentation and Q\&A/discussion

7:50-9:00 Breakout groups

‎

Code of Conduct: https://civictech.ca/about-us

‎

Check in with us on the Civic Tech Toronto Slack: https://link.civictech.ca/chat

About Us:

Our weekly civic meetups bring together Torontonians (designers, coders, urban planners, government staff, mappers, policy-makers, students, communications strategists, community organizers, and more) who share an interest in making Toronto more responsive, prosperous, sustainable, and equitable through design, tech, and data.

Come and be part of it!

title: Protecting Sobriety Through Loss
location: Online, online
description: Queer Death Salon is a virtual community space for all 2SLGBTQIA+ people to come together to discuss death, dying and grief. In her life Jackie Clark has seen the overlapping power of queer and recovery communities. Getting sober after a devastating loss and staying sober through another was one of the hardest things She's ever experienced, and it is only through deep connections with other people and a lot of truth telling that She managed. This session is for 2SLGBTQIA+ people in recovery (however they may define it), struggling with substance use, or supporting friends and family through the same, to connect about how death and grief intersect with addiction and recovery. Participants can expect some framing, a grounding meditation, and some prompts for peer-sharing. Participate as much as you’re comfortable (just listening is okay too)! *A note about language and perspective: I, Jackie, will facilitate with deep care and a concerted effort to use language as inclusively as possible. I also understand that everyone’s experiences with both addiction/substance use disorders and with grief are extremely individual. I am not an expert, but a peer with lived experience. * Please feel free to bring your own experience to the table, and also leave behind any perspectives that do not resonate with or serve you. Jackie Clark (she/they) is a queer person from Battersea, Ontario celebrating six years of sobriety. In her professional life she works for a non-profit and on a farm –part of that work is advocating for and building community among queer and trans farmers. Outside of work she fills her days with fostering animals, running in the woods, and spending time with friends. After the loss of her best friend in 2019, she worked towards harm reduction and then addiction recovery, eventually spending a year facilitating meetings for folks recovering from all types of substance use and behavioral addictions. She believes firmly in the wisdom and power of queer community to hold each other safely as we navigate grief. ‍

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

They bring 9+ years of experience as a Pro Dominant and kink professional, over a decade of professional experience screenwriting and developing content for Hollywood film and television, and a BA in Film with a minor in Literature. Their kink workshops have been sought after across the U.S. and Canada, including at Dark Odyssey, Kinkfest, and Westcoast Bound, with their online classes reaching kinksters worldwide. They have worked with hundreds of clients, organized 70+ community events, led support groups, created erotic immersive theatre productions, and more. They are currently pursuing a master’s-equivalent certification in sex coaching, and their personal relationships all center power exchange, queerness, polyamory, and risk-informed consent. Primal and pet play are two of their deepest passions, and they actively use both their Handler and primal headspaces as a way to explore, affirm, and fuck with their own gender alongside those of their playmates'. Their approach is a concoction of creativity, real-life animal research, and our internalized symbolic templates. They delight in guiding both new and experienced players on their journeys, with a particular focus on self-exploration, deepening intention, and personal growth. title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Xuan Ji (CITA)
description:
Title: How Orbital Eccentricity Erases Snowball Bistability on Earth-like Planets 

Abstract: For the same stellar flux, Earth's climate can be either warm and partly ice-covered, or fully frozen in a "Snowball" state. This bistability comes from ice-albedo feedback: once ice forms, it reflects more sunlight and keeps itself frozen. A stable Snowball episode requires this bistability. Snowball episodes on Earth are linked to rises in atmospheric oxygen and in the complexity of life. I will start from the simplest global-mean energy balance model and show how ice-albedo feedback produces bifurcations and bistability. I will then turn to eccentric orbits. There, 3D global climate model simulations show the bistability disappears at moderate eccentricity. On the blackboard I will add ice thermodynamics to the energy balance model to explain why. This suggests Snowball episodes may be rarer on exoplanets than previously thought.
Host: Soumendra Kishore Roy

EUC Seminar: The spectre of the crowd: Liberal democracy and the fear of the masses with Dr. Hannah Richter
This talk will present key arguments and first findings from ongoing research into the way crowd psychology’s idea of ‘the masses’ has shaped the political imaginary of liberal democracy. At the end of the 19th century, crowd psychologists like Hippolyte Taine, Gabriel Tarde and Gustave Le Bon sought to deduce laws of collective behaviour from the political upheavals of their time. The crowd they presented as the result of their pseudo-scientific investigations was irrational, primitive and readily susceptible to the whisperings of political strongmen. In the following decades, and despite their obvious biases, the political ideas of crowd psychology came to resonate with a diverse group of scholars grappling with fast-paced technological, political and social changes. Amongst them were Joseph Schumpeter, Hannah Arendt and Sigmund Freud. Regardless of whether mass participation is rejected or endorsed, I argue that all three endow the masses with a constitutive, dangerous irrationality that the political community must keep at bay. I will further show how, filtered through the work of José Ortega y Gasset, crowd psychological ideas of mass behaviour shaped the demophobic discourse of the early Mont Pelerin Society meetings, and influenced the economic writings of Friedrich Hayek and Ludwig von Mises. To conclude, I will reflect on the relevance of interrogating the intellectual legacy of crowd psychology’s political ideas in the context of what Cas Mudde has termed the ‘populist zeitgeist,’ in which evaluations of collective political behaviour are ever-present.
Speaker Bio
Hannah Richter is Assistant Professor in Politics at the University of Sussex, UK, where she researches and teaches critical political thought, and Editor-in-Chief of Distinktion: Journal of Social Theory. She is the author of The Politics of Orientation. Deleuze meets Luhmann (SUNY Press, 2023) and Challenging Anthropocene Ontology. Modernity, Ecology and Indigenous Complexities (Bloomsbury, 2024; with E. Randazzo). Her work has been published in academic outlets including the European Journal of Political Theory, the European Journal of Social Theory, Globalizations, International Political Sociology and Political Geography. At the moment, she is working on a project that develops a critical genealogy of how 20th century democratic thinking imagines ‘the masses’.

title: Bring Your Problem: Can AI Help?

description:
