description:
Learn how to create stunning arrangements using natural materials!
Each week a different natural material – wood, branches, foliage, and fruit and vegetables – will take centre stage. These elements have always been included in arrangements, but here we will make them the stars of the show! We will study their forms and shapes, textures, sizes, colouring and characteristics to discover the new and exciting ways they can be used. Join us on this journey of discovery.

Wednesdays November 4, 11, 18, & 25, 6 to 9 p.m.
Public $240, Members $190 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Margaret Taylor
For more than 15 years, Margaret’s passion for flowers has led her to exhibit, judge, demonstrate and teach floral design in Canada and abroad. A recipient of many awards, Margaret’s accolades include two Canada Blooms’ Founder’s Gold Cups for Best in Show. Margaret has also won Best in Show on three occasions at the provincial triennial show and as a result, has been chosen to represent Canada in two world shows. It was her greatest honour to exhibit for Canada both in Boston and in India.
 
Margaret is currently a floral design judge accredited by the Garden Clubs of Ontario, a horticultural judge accredited by the Royal Botanical Gardens and a rose judge accredited by the Canadian Rose Society. Margaret is also a Sogetsu Ikebana teacher and exhibitor. Much lauded for her design acumen by the horticultural community, she is a past president of the Garden Club of Toronto and is a coordinator of floral design studies at Toronto Botanical Garden.

title: The Gravity Grand Prix
location: Malvern, In the DIH
description:
Get ready to design, build, and race! This high-speed engineering challenge invites young adults (competing in teams of 2 ages 18-24) to design the ultimate gravity-powered race car. Using professional 3D modeling software and cutting-edge 3D printing technology, your team will compete to see who can conquer the downhill track the fastest. The core of this challenge is physics: maximizing kinetic energy while minimizing friction. How will you transform potential energy into pure speed?🛠️ The Challenge Rules
The Software: All cars must be fully designed from scratch using OnShape. A brief Introduction to the software will be provided.
The Material Limit: To keep the playing field level, your final race car is strictly limited to a maximum of 30 grams of 3D printed filament and 2 tooth picks.
Free Prototyping: Failure is part of engineering! Teams are encouraged to print, test, and redesign. Prototype prints are completely free throughout the design phase.
The Track: A straight, downhill gravity track built for maximum acceleration.
📅 Timeline & Important Dates
Design & Prototyping Week: Nov 4 to Nov 11— Access the DIH, collaborate with your partner, and test your prototypes.
Race Day: Nov 11 (Exactly one week after design week) — Family and friends are welcome to watch the final showdown!
💡 Key Engineering Focus Areas to take home the trophy, your team will need to think critically about:
Aerodynamics & Friction: How will you reduce air resistance and wheel friction to keep your car gliding?
Weight Distribution: How can you strategically place your 30-gram limit to maximize downward momentum?

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: El día que la IA decidió trabajar en equipo (más JARVIS, menos Skynet)
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
En los últimos meses hemos visto cómo la IA escribe código, genera imágenes o responde preguntas. Pero hay algo mucho más interesante ocurriendo: ¿qué pasa cuando varias IAs empiezan a trabajar juntas como un equipo real?

En esta sesión vamos a llevar esa idea a la práctica montando, desde cero, una factoría de software basada en agentes IA. Cada agente tendrá un rol claro —programador, QA, diseñador, incluso músico— y todos estarán coordinados por un agente orquestador (el “project manager” de toda la vida) que se encargará de repartir tareas, tomar decisiones y mantener el flujo de trabajo.

Lo interesante es que no será teoría: lo veremos en directo. Los agentes se comunicarán entre ellos, pasarán tareas y construirán algo real delante de nosotros. Sin guión y sin red, mostrando cómo funcionan de verdad estos sistemas cuando los pones a trabajar.

Al final tendremos un producto generado por este “enjambre” de agentes, y por el camino habremos visto cómo se diseñan, cómo colaboran y qué problemas reales aparecen cuando intentas llevar esto a la práctica.

title: A Matter of Feeling: Chinese Ceramics Through the Senses
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
A Matter of Feeling: Chinese Ceramics Through the Senses            
                                    
                                
                        
                                                
                                                        Get Tickets                        
                                            
                
                    
    



	

    
         
    




	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Thursday November 5, 2026
12:00 pm – 1:00 pm ET
Online via Zoom 
Part of the Gardiner Signature Lecture Series
The Ann Walker Bell Lecture 
Speaker: Dr. Laura Vigo, Curator of Asian Art and Archaeology, Montreal Museum of Fine Arts 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    The Duran Duran song “A Matter of Feeling” seemed to define an era. Strangely enough, it offers an unexpectedly bittersweet point of departure for a talk that, in its own way, circles back in time. In this online lecture, Dr. Laura Vigo will turn to the origins of the Chinese ceramic collection at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (MMFA) and the enduring feelings these objects have inspired in those who handled them—potters, users, collectors, and curators alike. She will also consider how attending to these sensory encounters might shift the way we engage with them today. The objects’ appeal has never been simply about beauty or romance. Rather, there is a profound sensuality to ceramics: the sensation of touch, the scent of fired clay, the sound of porcelain when gently struck, and, above all, the pleasure of looking closely. 
These perceptual connotations shaped the collecting practices of figures such as Sir William Van Horne and the museum’s remarkably charismatic first volunteer curator, Cleveland Morgan. Their tales, and the objects they left behind, remind us that collecting ceramics has always been about more than acquiring beautiful commodities. It was, and still is, about cultivating the senses and the imagination, and about bridging past and present through the intimate experience of handling and looking.

                    About the Speaker
                    
                
                
                    Laura Vigo
                    
                
                
                    Laura Vigo is Curator of Asian Art and Archaeology at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (MMFA) and an invited curator at the Museum of Asian Art in Turin (MAO), where she co-curated several recent exhibitions and is currently preparing the new galleries dedicated to Chinese material culture. 
At the MMFA, she has developed major exhibitions and collection displays, including the N. Kapany Gallery for Sikh Art, the Asian collections in the Arts of One World wing, and the recent exhibition Tōkaidō: Dreamscapes by Andō Hiroshige. Her previous projects include Egyptian Mummies, Pompeii, and The Warrior Emperor and China’s Terracotta Army, as well as exhibitions exploring Japanese ceramics, artistic diversity, and the museum’s collections. 
Vigo holds a PhD in Chinese Archaeology from SOAS, University of London, and has worked across museums, galleries, and auction houses in Italy, the UK, and Canada. Her interests span from the histories of collecting, the Western construction of Asian art, transcultural narratives, to sensory studies, and digital mediation. She also teaches at the Université de Montréal. 
Her work often brings together museum collections, contemporary artistic practices, and questions about how we encounter objects—and how museums can create new ways of seeing, sensing, and understanding them.

title: Nov 5 - Visual AI Agriculture Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics at the intersection of agriculture and AI.

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 05, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/visual-ai-agriculture-meetup-november-5-2026)**

Talks will include:

**U-Net Framework for Micro-Scale Surface Damage Segmentation in High-Resolution Soybean Seed Imagery**

Accurate detection of surface-level seed damage is critical for soybean seed quality assurance, yet automated micro-scale damage detection in high-resolution imagery remains an open challenge due to extreme spatial variability in damage scale, severe class imbalance across damage types, and the computational demands of processing ultra-high resolution agricultural imagery at scale. This research addresses the semantic segmentation of fine-grained soybean seed surface defects, such as wrinkles, dark spots, and general surface damage, in 6048 × 4024 pixel images where target damages can be as small as 18 × 18 pixels, using an augmented dataset of 77,000 individual seed images.

To overcome the difficulties of micro-scale detection, spatial sparsity, and class confusion, we propose a two-stage training and dual model inference framework built on an optimized U-Net architecture with a ResNet34 encoder. In the first stage, a damage specialist model is trained using weighted loss functions and a class-balanced approach that prioritizes damage classes.

In the second stage, transfer learning is applied to initialize a healthy seed specialist model from Stage 1 weights, with rebalanced class weights and tile probabilities that identify healthy seeds. During inference, a confidence-gated damage filter suppresses low-confidence predictions, and healthy seed labels are assigned only when the specialist model's confidence exceeds that of the damage model.

The two specialist models achieve validation accuracies of 94% and 98.53%, respectively, and the combined inference system successfully detects and localizes all three damage categories across unseen test images under conditions of extreme spatial variability and class imbalance. Qualitative evaluation confirms close alignment of predicted boundaries with ground truth annotations across all damage types, including dark spots.

These results demonstrate that confidence-gated dual model inference can reduce class confusion in imbalanced micro-scale segmentation, advancing the feasibility of fine-grained automated seed quality inspection at the scale.

*About the Speaker*

[Saurav Upadhyaya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sauravupadhyaya/) is an AI/ML researcher with a Master's degree in Computer Science, whose work spans agricultural AI, conversational systems, and public health, consistently translating advanced technology into tangible real-world impact.

**From camera to drone: wildfire detection and integration at the edge**

Wildfires are getting larger and more expensive every year. But caught early, a fire is a small job for a small team; caught late, nothing stops it. The cameras to catch them are already installed, so the work is not necessary more sensors but making the ones we have act.

This talk walks the whole chain: a small vision model running on the camera that flags smoke, an integration layer that scores the alert against terrain, weather and history to decide whether it matters, and a drone dispatched to confirm before anyone commits a crew. We will cover what has to run at the edge and why, how small the model can get before it stops seeing smoke, and what it takes to trust a detection nobody has looked at yet.

*About the Speaker*

[Maxime Carriere](https://voxel51.com/events/www.linkedin.com/in/maxime-carriere-871756161) is co-founder of Kernwerk in Berlin, where he works on compressing AI models to run on cheap embedded hardware.

**5,000 Flights to Answer One Question: Can a Drone Sample as Well as a Human?**

Environmental testing still begins with a person walking onto a site with a shovel. We built a system that turns a plain-language brief into a sampling campaign, flies it, and returns soil, water and vegetation samples with GPS, timestamps and chain of custody intact: 5,000 flights, roughly 9,000 miles and 570 flight hours over a 185-acre site in Roatan, much of it under canopy where GPS degrades and clearances are tight.

I will walk through the vision and planning stack, including multispectral and thermal canopy sensing, terrain and land-cover mapping, and the constraint solver that clears a route against airspace and battery budget before anything leaves the ground. Then the harder problem: evidentiary comparability.

A drone-collected result means nothing to a regulator unless it agrees with a hand-collected split under the same method, so I will show the dual-collection protocol we designed to test exactly that. I will close on why calibrated uncertainty and knowing when a model should refuse to answer matter more than raw accuracy once the output lands in a regulatory filing.

*About the Speaker*

[Rohan Talwadia](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rohantalwadia/) is co-founder and CTO of LabGPT, which automates environmental field sampling using drones and edge analysis, with results returned through ISO/IEC 17025-accredited partner laboratories.

Black Refugees in America (Rutgers University Press) ( https://www.rutgersuniversitypress.org/unwelcome-shores/9781978843073 ), Unwelcome Shores is an ethnographic study of the Liberian refugee community in Staten Island, New York, home to the largest per capita concentration of Liberians in the U.S., that sheds light on the racialization of Black refugees and the racism they have experienced at every step of their migration journey. In this pioneering study, sociologist Bernadette Ludwig explores how Liberians have responded to such racist exclusions, noting how members of this community reject the informal refugee label once they are resettled in the United States. Liberian migrants often view the label as a liability since the larger general public, the media, and the U.S. government tend to regard Black refugees as an economic and social burden unworthy of assistance. Indeed, Black refugees’ humanity is often ignored, Ludwig contends, in favor of overemphasizing presumed barbaric violence, endemic wars, cultural backwardness, and diseases. By detailing the lack of aid and support for Black refugees and describing how Liberian refugees in particular have had to overcome various struggles and barriers in coming to the U.S. and while living here, Unwelcome Shores highlights the overarching role of race and anti-Black racism in American society.


Biography



Bernadette Ludwig, PhD is a Sociologist and the Assistant Dean of the Macricostas School of Arts and Sciences at Western Connecticut State University (WCSU). Prior to joining WCSU, she was a tenured Professor of Sociology and the Director of Civic Engagement at a college in New York.
Her primary research focuses on the intersection of immigration, race, and gender and analyzes how seemingly racially neutral refugee and immigration policies indeed are inherently racist. In addition to her book, Unwelcome Shores: Black Refugees in America  ( https://www.rutgersuniversitypress.org/unwelcome-shores/9781978843073/ )(Rutgers University Press, 2025) she had published widely in journals such as International Migration, African and Black Diaspora: An International Journal, and International Journal of Migration, Health and Social Care, and in edited books.
In another research project, she investigates the significance and meaning of community-engaged learning opportunities for students, in particular those from historically excluded groups which have been published in Michigan Journal of Community Service, Learning Science Education & Civic Engagement, and others. Her co-edited book How to Facilitate Community-Engaged Learning (Edward Elgar Publishing) was published in August 2026.
Before pursuing a PhD in Sociology, Dr. Ludwig worked with refugee and immigrant communities in Atlanta GA. During that time, she was the executive director of two non-profit organizations, including Culture Connect, Inc., which she co-founded. Her years of working in the field with refugees and immigrants continue to inform her research and her teaching.  As a first-generation college graduate and immigrant, she is committed to mentoring students, in particular those from historically excluded groups. Dr. Ludwig also serves as a pro-bono country conditions expert for asylum and deportation claims/hearings.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

title: Author Talk: Robert Moor
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
To truly grasp the wisdom of a tree, you need to begin thinking like one…
One day, years ago, Robert Moor set out to climb a tree near his home in British Columbia. This simple act unwittingly launched him on a decade-long adventure around the world, ranging from Papua to Tanzania. Along the way, he learned the art of “tree-thinking,” which, he discovered, has the power to break open some of humanity’s oldest questions: What is the secret to truly growing old? How do we set down roots in an increasingly chaotic world? Most importantly, how should we—as individuals, as communities, as stewards of the earth—live?
 
Moor’s mind-expanding talk, “How To Think Like A Tree” will reveal the myriad ways trees teach us to “grow wise.” The genius of trees, he argues, is that they deftly combine four entwined processes: branching, pruning, gnarling, and rooting. He shows how this pattern appears well beyond the realm of botany; it occurs also in human brains, in family trees, and in the evolutionary tree of life. His lecture includes colourful anecdotes and multimedia from his travels, including his experiences studying bonsai in Japan, climbing giant sequoias with David Attenborough, and sleeping in a chimpanzee nest in Tanzania. The end result of learning to ’think like a tree,’ Moor argues, is to become more creative, rigorous, and deeply rooted to the living world.
 
Thursday, November 5, 2 to 4 p.m.
Free to attend. Please register beforehand so we know you’re coming!
 
About Robert Moor
Hailed by critics as a “philosopher on foot,” Robert Moor is the bestselling author of On Trails and In Trees. Translated into more than a dozen languages, On Trails garnered the National Outdoor Book Award, the Pacific Northwest Book Award, and the William Saroyan International Prize. Moor’s writing has appeared in The New Yorker, The Atlantic, Harper’s, and many other publications. He lives in Halfmoon Bay, British Columbia.

title: Uplifted by the Sea: The Efik of Calabar in the Atlantic Slave Trade
location: (3rd flr York Lanes, Rm 314)
description:
Date: Thursday, November 5, 2026
Time: 2:00-3:30pm EST
Location: Tubman Resource Room (314 York Lanes)
4700 Keele Street 
Toronto, ON | M3J 1P3 
In-Person Registration: https://research.apps01.yorku.ca/machform/view.php?id=322950
Zoom Registration: https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/fDGGCUPYQHu66fmEakVbUg





Title: Uplifted by the Sea: The Efik of Calabar in the Atlantic Slave Trade
 
Abstract:
The history of the Efik of Calabar illustrates how geography, commerce, and human exploitation shaped an African society’s fortunes and its place in the Atlantic world. From the seventeenth century, the Efik leveraged their strategic maritime location to establish Calabar as a major slave-trading port in the Bight of Biafra, linking British merchants with hinterland communities whose people were sold into Atlantic slavery. This paper examines how maritime access, commercial monopolies, credit networks, and indigenous institutions such as the Ekpe society enabled Efik commercial dominance. It explores the paradox of Efik resistance to the enslavement of their own people alongside their participation in the enslavement of neighbouring communities. It also considers how Atlantic commerce transformed Efik society through European goods, literacy, education, and new expressions of wealth and prestige. Finally, it interrogates the selective remembrance of slavery in contemporary Calabar, particularly the tendency to emphasize European culpability while obscuring indigenous participation. Drawing on primary and secondary sources, the paper argues that Efik prosperity and regional prominence were inseparable from the Atlantic slave economy. Ultimately, the sea uplifted the Efik into extraordinary commercial and political prominence, but their ascent was entangled with the exploitation and suffering of others. Confronting this history offers a more nuanced understanding of African agency, complicity, and responsibility in the Atlantic slave trade.
 
Bio:
David L. Imbua is a Professor of Atlantic History and Diaspora Studies at the University of Calabar, Nigeria, where he serves as Head of the Department of History and International Studies and Deputy Director of the Institute for African and Asian Studies. A distinguished historian of the Atlantic world, slavery, the Cross River region, and Nigerian historiography, he has authored over 100 scholarly publications. His award-winning book, Intercourse and Crosscurrents in the Atlantic World: Calabar-British Experience, 17th–20th Centuries, received the 2015 Lapai Book Prize for Outstanding Historical Text in International History. He has contributed to UNESCO’s General History of Africa and collaborated with Professors Paul E. Lovejoy, Nicholas Radburn, and Randy J. Sparks on the landmark book, The Notorious Massacre at Calabar in 1767. A former valedictorian and overall best graduating student of the University of Calabar’s 2002 graduating class, Professor Imbua currently serves as President of the Historical Society of Nigeria, the country’s first professional association, founded in 1955.
Moderator: Dr. Damilola Adebayo, Department of History, York University.




Damilola Adebayo is an Associate Professor of History and a faculty member in the Graduate Program in Science and Technology Studies (STS). He serves as Vice President of the Canadian Association of African Studies and Associate Editor of History and Technology. An award-winning historian of Anglophone West Africa, particularly Nigeria, his research and teaching lie at the intersection of the history of technology, socioeconomic life, and the role of international organizations in Africa. His work examines the socioeconomic life of Western technologies in African cities since the mid-nineteenth century, with particular attention to the varied contexts in which energy, communication, and transportation technologies were introduced, adopted, appropriated, hybridised, reinvented, or discarded by both elite and everyday users, and to how these technologies have been both a cause and an effect of economic, social, and political change in African societies. His work has earned international recognition, including the Maurice Daumas Prize, awarded by the International Committee for the History of Technology (ICOHTEC) for the best article in the history of technology, and the Bernard S. Finn IEEE History Prize, awarded by the Society for the History of Technology (SHOT) for the best article on the history of electrotechnology. His prize-winning scholarship has appeared in leading historical journals, including Past & Present. He earned a BA in History from the University of Ibadan, an MA in International History from the Geneva Graduate Institute, and a PhD in History from the University of Cambridge, where he was a Cambridge-Africa Scholar and recipient of the IEEE Life Members’ Fellowship in the History of Electrical and Computing Technology. His book project, Power and the People: Electricity and Urban Life in Nineteenth- and Twentieth-Century Nigeria, contributes to broader debates on infrastructure, urbanization, development, state power, modernity, and energy inequality.

title: DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit
location: Bendale, The program will take place in the Auditorium located in the basement. Elevator on site. If you have any questions, please call Bendale Branch at 416-396-8910.
description:
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit  teaches principles of air pressure and pneumatics to kids Ages 6 and up. Each child will get to take home one kit they build.
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit
Engages children in practical activities
Teaches principles of air pressure and pneumatics
Includes all components for easy assembly
Age: 5+
The
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit
is an engaging and educational assembly kit designed specifically for children between the ages of 5 to 12. This kit offers children the opportunity to participate in practical activities, while simultaneously observing the movement of a wooden horse, propelled by the simple push and pull of a syringe. This action illustrates the principles of air pressure and pneumatic systems in a fun and interactive way.
The kit includes all necessary components for the assembly of a pneumatic horse, such as pre-cut wooden pieces for the horse structure, a pair of syringes of different sizes, orange rubber rings that function as grippers, self-tapping screws, metal shafts of varying lengths, a small screwdriver, and a plastic tube. The assembly process does not require any soldering.
Registration Begins  on October 26th 2026 at 10:00 A.M. Spaces are limited this program will take place again in December.
The program will take place in the Auditorium located in the basement. Elevator on site. If you have any questions, please call Bendale Branch at 416-396-8910.

title: 🧠💡❓Trivia Night @ The Frog: A Firkin Pub
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
## 🧠🎉 Trivia Night @ The Frog: A Firkin Pub 🍻

**Think fast, laugh hard, and make new friends!**
We’ll be meeting at **The Frog: A Firkin Pub**, conveniently located just steps from **Yonge–Sheppard Station** — cozy - great food and fun!

### 🕖 About the Event

Trivia starts at **7:00 PM** and runs until around **9:30 P**M— just **ask for Colleen’s group** when you arrive!

Expect a lively mix of **pop culture, history, music, sports, and random fun question.** Whether you come solo or bring a friend, we’ll make sure everyone’s part of a team. 🧩💬

### 💸 Cost & Policy

Everyone must spend at least **$10 (plus tax & tip)** at the pub.

**NEW POLICY:**

* 🆕 *First-timers* must send a **$5 deposit** by e-transfer to **tommills@rogers.com** and message Colleen right away on this page or the sign-up page. you'll be refunded in cashif/when you show up.
* 💌 There will be a **$1 reminder charge** if you don’t send the deposit promptly, for each reminder.
* 👥 You may bring **1 guest**, but please e-transfer **$10** in advance. You’ll be refunded once your guest arrives.

### 🧠 Why You’ll Love It

Trivia night isn’t just about questions — it’s about **connection, laughter, and teamwork**. Come test your wits, cheer on your tablemates, and enjoy the buzz of a pub full of friendly faces. Whether you’re a trivia pro or just in it for the fun, it’s always a great time!

📱 **Don’t forget to join our WhatsApp group** – [CLICK HERE!](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc?mode=ac_t)

### ⚠️ Notes

* Please don’t just “show up” without RSVPing — seating is limited, and teams need to be balanced.
* Occasionally, the organizer may need to rearrange teams if one is *too stacked* (e.g., all the sports or music experts together!).
* Sometimes things happen — events can be canceled or adjusted, so keep an eye out for updates.

📩 **Questions?**
Contact **Colleen**, your organizer, by posting on the event page.

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: WORLD PREMIERE – “The Art of Lockdown”
location: Fox Theatre,2236 Queen St E, Toronto, ON M4E 1G2, Canada
description:
The year is 2020. The world as we know it has changed forever. Artists whose lives and livelihoods depended on bringing people together were faced with a terrifying question:

“What do we do now?”

Introducing The Art of Lockdown, a five-episode documentary series exploring the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the arts and entertainment industry.

Each episode delves into the life and journey of a different artist, revealing how they navigated the uncertainty, challenges, and unprecedented changes brought on by the pandemic. From a one-woman clown show to a black and white murder mystery, every artist has a story to tell!

Join us at Fox Theatre on November 5th at 7:30pm for the world premiere of this compelling new series.

Stick around after the screening to connect with fellow Toronto artists, meet the filmmakers, and take part in a Q&A Session for a behind-the-scenes look at the making of the series.


Tickets: www.tickettailor.com/events/blackalloyproductions/2340506 https://www.tickettailor.com/events/blackalloyproductions/2340506


‘The Art of Lockdown’ is a timely exploration about artistic resilience, creativity, and perseverance in the face of overwhelming odds. It shines a light on the people who create the stories we love and highlights the determination it takes to keep creating, even when the world came to a standstill.

Across five episodes, The Art of Lockdown explores the creativity, resilience, and reinvention of artists navigating an unprecedented moment in history. From experimental filmmaking to personal accounts of an industry in crisis, each episode offers a unique perspective on the pandemic’s impact on the arts.

Episode 1: The Clown

When the Toronto Fringe Festival is cancelled, Katherine transforms her one-woman

show into a short film about a clown navigating the early days of lockdown.

Featuring: Katherine Cappellacci and Laura Cappellacci


Episode 2: Hartley & Sheel

“Have you ever seen Clue?” A sketch comedy duo takes a crack at solving a crime in a

black-and-white murder mystery filmed during lockdown.

Featuring: Hartley Fanson, Sheel Radia, Chris Black, and Anthony Gullace


Episode 3: Respect for Actors

“Our industry was the first to shut down… We lost everything.” As COVID-19 brings

theatre and film productions to a standstill, five actors share their experiences of

navigating uncertainty, reinventing their craft, and adapting to a rapidly changing

industry.

Featuring: Chase Jeffels, Felix Beauchamp, Noor Alimran, Karen Scobie, and Chelsea

Muirhead


Episode 4: Phoenix Rising

Faced with unprecedented challenges, one theatre company refuses to stand still. Discover how its team adapts, innovates, and finds new ways to bring creativity to life.

Featuring: Brandon Nicoletti and Jordan Kenny


Episode 5: The Making Of

Go behind the scenes of The Art of Lockdown for an inside look at the creative process, collaboration, and work that brought this documentary series to life.

Featuring: Can Yüksel, Felipe Gonzalez, Brandon Nicoletti, and Jordan Kenny

Advanced Techniques:

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Forest Bathing at the Garden
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Connect with nature and join us for a guided forest therapy walk!
Rekindle your relationship with nature this fall through a guided outdoor forest bathing walk with certified forest therapy guide Laura Bincik. At a slow pace and in community with other participants and the environment, you will be guided by a series of invitations throughout the experience to awaken your senses and intentionally connect with nature in the present moment.
 
We will gather briefly indoors to prepare for the walk and consider the origin of forest bathing, as well as some of the benefits of the practice. When we venture into the Toronto Botanical Gardens and surrounding ravine, we will cover a loop of approximately 1.5 km on paved pathways, lawns and bare ground, at times encountering uneven terrain, inclines and declines. We will be strolling, standing and sitting (if you wish to). Your comfort and safety are most important!
 
Please note: The surrounding Wilket Creek Ravine faced severe damage due to flooding and has unfortunately remained closed to the public until repairs can be made. The upcoming Forest Bathing Walk will not cross any closed trails into the ravine. 
 
As this program occurs rain or shine, please dress for the weather and wear sturdy, closed-toed footwear. Long pants and shirt sleeves will help to protect against insect bites. You may wish to bring a water bottle, sunhat/glasses, walking poles and/or a folding stool or sitting/kneeling pad.
 
As the walk ends, we will gather and partake in a seasonal tea, snacks and taste honey harvested at Toronto Botanical Garden.
 
In the event of severe weather or environmental conditions, TBG staff will make alternative arrangements to the program.
 
Washrooms are available onsite.
 
The program is suited for adults 18+. All participants must sign a liability waiver at the start of the program.
 
Service pets welcome but we ask that you leave your pets at home during this program.
 
Friday, November 6, 1 to 3 p.m.
Public $35, TBG Members $30 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Laura Bincik
Laura Bincik is a certified forest therapy guide with the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. Following a career that straddled health care and education, Laura discovered that her lifelong sense of awe for the natural world could be enriched and shared with others to enhance wellbeing. Laura feels a connection to the land and the wonder of being in nature from countless hours spent exploring Toronto ravines in all seasons. An active member of Nature and Forest Therapy Canada, Laura follows the growing research on the mental and physical health benefits of forest bathing and is expanding her practice by connecting with local, national and international leaders in the field.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Seminar Series 2026 – 2027 – Dr. Alex Speed (Dalhousie University)
location: 140 Campus Walk
description:
Abstract
The Speed group works at the boundaries of main group and organic chemistry, developing new catalysts, primarily based on phosphorus (III), and phosphorus (II)/(III) cycles, for useful chemical transformations, including asymmetric reduction. This talk will encompass our efforts to functionalize the potent greenhouse gas sulfur hexafluoride (SF6), and the unplanned yet fruitful discovery of carbon-carbon bond forming reactions during these explorations. Beginning with initial reactions of SF6 with stoichiometric quantities of phosphines and phosphides, mechanistic studies into the role of the phosphines revealed an unexpected role for phosphorus compounds in the unusual P(II) oxidation state. A further serendipitous discovery led to the development of new chemistry for the formation of carbon-phosphorus, and ultimately carbon-carbon bonds. These reactions, including intermolecular alkene hydro(hetero)arylation reactions, were made catalytic in phosphorus. The insights gained from this catalysis were then reapplied to the challenging problem of catalytic functionalization of SF6.

title: Language, Epistemology, Metaphysics, and Mind Research Interest Group (Brian Hedden, MIT)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Language, Epistemology, Metaphysics, and Mind Research Interest Group is delighted to welcome as guest speaker Brian Hedden, a professor in the Department of Linguistics and Philosophy at MIT. He works in epistemology and decision theory, as well as related areas of ethics and political philosophy. 
Talk Title
Algorithmic Monoculture 
Talk Abstract
Algorithmic decision-making is replacing idiosyncratic human judgment in domains such as hiring, lending, and college admissions. But what happens if all firms use the same algorithm to make their hiring decisions? Or if all banks use the same algorithm to assess creditworthiness? Or if all colleges use the same algorithm to decide which students to admit? Recently, several philosophers, legal scholars, and computer scientists have raised the alarm about such algorithmic monoculture, in which all decisions across a domain (all hiring in a given sector, say) are made by a single algorithm. They warn of the rise of “algorithmic leviathans” and “outcome homogenization,” which may “institutionalize systemic exclusion and reinscribe social hierarchy.” I argue that their concerns are largely misplaced. I consider four objections to monoculture, having to do with systematic exclusion, information aggregation, exploration of unfamiliar types of candidates, and Goodhart’s law, and find them unpersuasive. Monoculture needn’t be dystopian, and depending on the nature of its lone algorithm, it could even be better than polyculture, in which different decision-makers use different algorithms.

title: Imaginary Expedition
location: Burdock Music Hall,1184 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON M6H 1N2, Canada
description:
Imaginary Expedition is a Toronto-based duo of Victoria Dobbs and Glyph Greenleaf who combine folk songwriting with early music composition techniques and intimate, unamplified performance practice. The ensemble draws people closer, quietly pushing the limits of what can be achieved with only their alto and baritone voices and a classical guitar. Their songs alternate between the lead vocalists, and gravitate toward duets with equal importance on both vocal lines.


The name Imaginary Expedition reflects the experience the duo creates. Their songs spark daydreams and send listeners on journeys through memory, grief, gratitude, and self-reflection. Their lyrics journey through emotional terrain shaped by the vivid changing seasons of the North, with imagery drawn from great lakes, old-growth forests, open prairies, wetlands, shield rock, and luminous skies.


Victoria and Glyph began writing together in August 2024 and performing together regularly in September 2025, after years of separate professional music careers. The duo has developed their live show and generated momentum through intimate listening rooms, festival stages, house concerts, and industry showcases. The duo has appeared at JP Music Festival in Boston (2025), and Toronto’s Winterfolk Blues + Roots Festival and Toronto Folk Festival (2026).


Their debut singles “Winter Lullaby” and “The Ones Who Are Gone” capture the acoustic realism of sitting in a room with the performers, whose voices move in harmony and counterpoint with Glyph’s lap-style classical guitar. The songs, which explore how we carry the memories of those we have lost, have received airplay on folk and indie radio in Canada, the USA, and Australia. With the support of a FACTOR Artist Development grant the duo has begun production of a full-length album in the same live-off-the-floor format.


Doors: 6pm

Concert: 6:30-7:30pm

All ages welcome.

$10-$12 advance / $15 at the door

Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. The Culture and Technology Book club brings readers together every two months to discuss new and classic texts that raise important questions about the way technology transforms our cultural and political lives.
This meeting we'll discuss:
Killed by A Traffic Engineer
(also available as an audiobook)
Civil Engineering professor Wes Marshal takes a hard look at how traffic engineering standards in North America have shaped our streets for the worse. He examines some of the dubious and unscientific assumptions central to traffic engineering such as their fixation on speed. Marshal asks what it might look like to build transportation infrastructure with a more holistic understanding of people's needs.
Register for this program to receive the discussion questions a week in advance of the meeting.

Movie info:

It might be November, but it’s still spooky season for us!

Messiah of Evil (1973) is a surreal, slow-burn horror film about a young woman who travels to the eerie seaside town of Point Dume, California, searching for her missing artist father. She finds his abandoned home and a disturbing diary warning of strange changes overtaking the town. As she investigates, she encounters increasingly bizarre residents, ritualistic behavior, and a growing sense that something ancient and horrifying is approaching. The film blends occult horror, zombies, and dreamlike imagery into an unsettling story of isolation and creeping doom.

This is the perfect movie to help us creep into the darker months.

title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons
location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

title: Refrigerator Stories: A Search for Home
location: Tranzac,292 Brunswick Ave, Toronto, ON M5S 2M7, Canada
description:
(Living Room)

A new solo show by Jos Dirkx, directed by Reena Dutt, with music direction by Sacha Hoedemaker. Nine real-life stories, six original songs: starting in a classroom in Dakar with eleven kids from eleven countries, moving through Toronto, Helsinki, Juba and Athens, and arriving at a Dutch kitchen table where, at 39, Jos decides to step back on stage after all. A show about growing up between cultures, a voice that disappears and comes back, and love turning up when you least expect it. And what’s a refrigerator story? You’ll find out in the theatre.

The 2026 workshop performances will be the first time the complete show is performed for live audiences. In select venues, each performance is followed by a short conversation with the makers. The premiere will take place in 2027.

title: UNHack
location: Room 313, Bergeron Centre, YorkU Keele Campus
description:
UNHack 2026 is a two-day hackathon hosted by YSpace and the Lassonde School of Engineering at York University, bringing together engineering students to tackle real-world challenges inspired by the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Participation does not need a startup idea, previous hackathon experience, or advanced technical skills. Through the programming you’ll be guided through a structured process that takes you from problem → idea → prototype → pitch, with support from mentors, facilitators, and technical experts along the way.
KEY DETAILS
📅 When

Saturday, November 7 – Sunday, November 8, 2026

📍 Where

Bergeron Centre for Engineering Excellence, York University

👥 Who Can Participate
UNHack is open to ANY undergraduate student at York University. You can register:

Individually – we’ll help match you with a team
With a pre-formed team of 3–5 students

💡 What You’ll Do
Over two days, you’ll:
1. Identify a problem
Explore selected UN Sustainable Development Goal challenge tracks and define a focused How Might We (HMW) problem statement.
2. Develop your solution
Generate ideas, understand your users, evaluate existing alternatives, and select a concept to pursue.
3. Build a prototype
Turn your idea into an achievable prototype or MVP with dedicated build time, workshops, technical support, and mentor office hours.
4. Pitch your solution
Develop and practice your pitch before presenting your solution to judges. Top teams will advance to the final round and pitch on the main stage.
🏆 PRIZES & OPPORTUNITIES

Cash prizes for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place teams
Mentorship from industry professionals and technical experts
Hands-on experience with design thinking, prototyping, and pitching
Experience Ventures: The first 60 eligible domestic students may receive. $325 upon successful completion of the hackathon and associated program requirements. Funding is first-come, first-served and subject to eligibility.

title: NEW TRAIL! 🍂 From Scarborough to North York: The Fall Colours Trail Walk 🌈
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🍂 From Scarborough to North York: The Fall Colours Trail Walk 🌈

### A Scenic Fall Adventure Through Trails, Ravines & Toronto History

Toronto has some wonderful natural spaces tucked between its neighbourhoods, and this walk connects two of them into one longer adventure!

We’ll begin in Scarborough, exploring the **Gatineau Corridor Trail**, with its wildflowers, tall grasses, and green spaces where nature is allowed to grow a little more freely. 🍁 From there, we’ll make our way along some city streets before connecting with another trail system and continuing through the surrounding ravines toward the **Rainbow Tunnel**.

The tunnel is an unusual piece of Toronto history, painted in 1971 by teenager B.C. Johnson as a tribute to his friend Sigred, who died in a car accident. Although the artwork has seen better days, we’ll make a quick stop to see it before continuing toward our final destination.

We’ll finish at **Shops at Don Mills**, where anyone who wants to can join us for coffee, a pastry, or something to eat after the walk. ☕🥐
This is a longer outing than some of our regular walks, but we’ll take our time, enjoy the scenery, and have a break along the way.

***

### 🚶‍♂️ What We’ll Do

Along the route, we’ll:

* Explore the Gatineau Corridor Trail and its naturalized green spaces 🌼
* Walk through parks and neighbourhood streets
* Take a break midway through the walk
* Connect with the Moccasin Trail and surrounding ravine paths 🌳
* Stop briefly at the Rainbow Tunnel 🌈
* Continue to Shops at Don Mills
* Finish with an optional coffee or snack with the group ☕

The walk should take approximately **3 hours**, depending on the pace of the group and the conditions along the route.
**Please note:** This is a point-to-point walk. We will not return to our starting location at Dollar Tree. At the end, I’ll help anyone who needs assistance figuring out their transit options.

***

### ☀️ Weather & Expectations

This walk takes place in typical Toronto weather conditions. Please dress appropriately for the forecast and wear comfortable walking shoes.
The route includes a mix of paved streets, trails, and potentially uneven or unpaved surfaces. There will be some distance to cover, so this walk is best suited to people who are comfortable walking for around three hours, with breaks.

This is a social walk, not a race. We’ll keep a steady pace and make time to enjoy the surroundings.

🌦️ **This event happens rain or shine!**

***

### 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Starting Location:** Outside the Dollar Tree near Kennedy Station
🫎 **Look for me wearing my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** 11:00 AM
I will only wait 5 minutes.
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🏁 **End Point:** Shops at Don Mills, North York
🚇 **Transit:** We’ll finish near the Eglinton line. I’ll help anyone who needs directions for getting home by transit.

***

### 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer to [mathewmaclean@hotmail.com](mailto:mathewmaclean@hotmail.com)**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing walks and other events throughout Toronto.

***

### ☕ After the Walk

Once we reach Shops at Don Mills, anyone who wants to continue the outing can join us for coffee, pastries, or a bite to eat.
It's a chance to relax, chat, and get to know one another after our walk. Participation is optional.

***

### 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🥨 A snack
🧥 Weather-appropriate clothing
📱 Your phone or camera for photos

***

### 🌈 Who Is This For?

This walk is great for:

* People who enjoy discovering hidden parts of Toronto
* Anyone interested in local history and unusual landmarks
* Walkers who enjoy exploring trails and ravines
* People looking to meet others and make friends
* Anyone who wants to spend a few hours outdoors enjoying the fall colours

The trails and Rainbow Tunnel are part of the adventure, but **the people you meet along the way are the real experience.**

***

**REMEMBER:** You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **[torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com](mailto:torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com)**

**Come for the trails.**
**Stay for the conversation.**
**Leave with a new connection — and maybe a new friend.** 🍂💛

description: This listing is for a three session Beginner Spinning Course. In this class you will learn how to use a drop spindle to spin starting with woolly fibre and ending with a completed, ready to use yarn. Presented by CRIP Lab, University of Guelph & Tangled Arts + Disabilty

The Special Edition of CRIP Lab with film screenings is here! We have been talking about this since our last two gatherings. Jami Mcfarland and Patricia Ginn would also be joining us. Very excited to see the movies with you all! This event is online only . More details about the event are below, along with the zoom links. Saturday, Nov 7, 1-2:30 p.m. Presented by CRIP Lab, University of Guelph & Tangled Arts + Disabilty Film Screenings from a study led by Jami Mcfarland : 2SLGBTQ+ aging with and into difference(s) Storytellers' names and titles: Patricia Derouin’s “Not Dead Yet” (8 mins) Michael Dion’s “Why Didn’t Anyone Tell Me About Aging” (6 mins, 39 secs) Rev. Marcie Wexler’s “Solitaire Road” (6 mins, 20 secs) Bernie Thompson’s “New Beginnings” (9 mins, 42 secs) Rita OLink’s “I’m Not Going to Run, I’m Not Going to Hide” (8 mins, 9 secs) Don Turner’s “A Long Journey Into Aging” (7 mins, 23 secs) David Drinkwalter’s “My Life in the Lost and Found Department” (6 mins, 36 secs) Dar Hansen’s “Dar’s Story” (6 mins, 48 secs) Jo Brook’s “A Fae-ry Tale” (8 mins, 55 secs) These stories came from a SSHRC-funded study, "(Eng)Aging Crip Rainbow Representations: 2SLGBTQ+ Disabled Older Adults Access the Arts and Create Belonging through Digital Storytelling," which sought to create diverse representations at the nexus of 2SLGBTQ+ aging, disability, and illness. Some storytellers chose to explore disability and illness directly in their stories, while others focused on other parts of their identities in their stories. Jami Mcfarland is the PI of this study, but there are several other academics contributing to it: Carla Rice, Nadine Changfoot, Celeste Pang, and Nicole Dalmer), and an excellent RA (Andrea Keber. Funded by SSHRC, the study was created in collaboration with Re-Vision: The Centre for Art and Social Justice at the University of Guelph. title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Doubles: A Panel Talk About the Film, Diversity & Indo-Caribbean Voices
location: Palmerston, Theatre
description:
Join us for an extraordinary evening with the actors and production team behind the six-time, award-nominated film
Doubles
, where diversity meets imagination, identity meets history and rarely heard Indo-Caribbean voices come together to celebrate the power of storytelling.
The Canadian drama film, Doubles, set in both Trinidad and Toronto, explores the relationship between a son and his estranged father. When tragedy strikes, Dhani, a Doubles stand operator dreaming of owning his own restaurant, must leave Trinidad to find his father, whom he hasn't seen in years. Their reunion brings deeply held feelings to the surface as unexpected revelations change their lives forever.
Presented by the
Canadian Caribbean Indian Cultural Collective (CCICC)
, this panel will feature:
Mark Sirju
, Producer
Errol Sitahal
, Actor portraying Ragbir
Premika Leo
, Actor portraying Skye
Kenneth Mohabir
, comedian, actor, and producer, will moderate the discussion.
The film is approximately 1 hour 29 minutes long, followed by a discussion with the panelists about the importance of Indo-Caribbean representation, behind-the-scenes stories about the film, and an audience Q&A.
Free program. Please register. Doors open at 1:45 pm. At 2:00 pm, seating becomes first-come, first-served until capacity is reached, with light refreshments (while supplies last).
Organization Info:
The
Canadian Caribbean Indian Cultural Collective (CCICC)
is a community organization representing Indians (currently referred to as South Asians) of various ethnicities, regions, and faiths, who are the descendants of the indentured labourers taken by the British to their colonies in the Caribbean and around the world. Their mission is to share their stories of struggle, resilience and contributions across the Caribbean and here in Canada.

title: Introduction to Chainmail Workshop
location: Lillian H. Smith, Bagshaw Room, 1st floor.
description:
Chainmail, the ancient art of linking metal rings together in a chain or mesh weave, has a long history within cultural practices from all over the world. These days you might not need a piece of armour to protect yourself during a swordfight, but you still might want to know how to make some - whether for yourself or to deck out a favourite toy! Or, maybe you want to make some unique jewelry: bracelets, necklaces, or earrings. Why not both?
Registration for both sessions is required:
1st session, Nov 7: Basics! Opening and closing rings, Japanese 1-in-1, 2-in-2, or 3-in-3 chain weave, attaching clasps. Make a bracelet or a short necklace.
2nd session, Nov 21: Pick 1 option - barrel or box chain weave, or 4-1 European mesh weave. Make a bracelet, a short necklace, or a base for a larger piece.
Please note that chainmail requires repetitive hand motions, gripping, and close visual attention to detail.
These sessions are oriented towards beginners but more advanced learners are also welcome.

title: The U of T, Yorkville and Rochdale College (MEGA-TOUR)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

**This is a revised route for 2026 to take in the history of the historic Rochdale College!**

On March 15, 1827, a royal charter was issued by King George IV, for the establishment of King's College. The charter was the result of the efforts of John Strachan, the Anglican Bishop of Toronto, the College's first president.

King's College was a religious institution tied to the Church of England and the Family Compact. In 1849, the newly elected government of Canada voted to rename the College, University of Toronto and broke with the church. Strachan resigned to open Trinity College as a private seminary.

University College was created as a branch of University of Toronto. During the American Civil War, the threat of Union blockade prompted the creation of the University Rifle Corps, which saw action against the Fenians on the Niagara border in 1866.

Founded in 1830 by Joseph Bloor, and William Botsford Jarvis, the Village of Yorkville was muddy York's northern residential suburb.

With historic establishments like The Red Lion Inn, Yorkville Town Hall or even the fierce political radical William Lyon Mackenzie, it was here that notoriety was achieved, in Yorkville itself.

Omnibus horse drawn streetcar service started in 1849 to connect the old St. Lawrence Market in Toronto with Yorkville, and by 1853, the population of the village had reached 1,000 residents.

By the 1870s, Potter's Field, a cemetery stretching west of Yonge Street at Bloor Street was closed, and the remains moved to other area cemeteries. Yorkville was growing fast, and soon Toronto was ready to pull the neighbourhood into its orbit. On February 1, 1883, Yorkville's name changed officially. It was now known as St. Paul's Ward!

This walking tour is for all fitness levels and skills. Please dress for the weather. The extensive walking tour begins at the Queen's Park SUBWAY Station at the **southwest corner** of University Avenue and College Street adjacent to the Tim Horton's at the corner.

The walk ends at the site of Historic Rochdale College at Bloor and Huron!

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person!

title: 🇨🇦Japanese and English Language Exchange  (Page for everyone)
description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events

Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:
Once you enter the "Waiting-list", we will message you for the payment via e-transfer. After your payment is confirmed, you will be moved to the "Going-list"

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

@tjex.ca

Feel free to follow us!

description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
🎬 Let’s Go to the Movies (and Actually Talk… or Not)

Whether you're a film nerd, popcorn enthusiast, or just looking for a chill night out with interesting people — this one's for you.

We’re heading out to see a movie together, then grabbing food or drinks after. If the film's great (or terrible), we’ll probably talk about it forever. If it’s just okay, we’ll talk about it for 10 minutes and move on to everything else — books, dating apps, weird dreams, how Toronto keeps getting more expensive, etc.

The vibe is relaxed, friendly, and not too serious. No film degree needed. No icebreakers. No pressure to “perform.” Just come enjoy the film, connect with some thoughtful people, and see where the night goes Click here to watch trailer!

🎞️ **Movie Title + Trailer:** [\[Click here to watch trailer!\]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Haw_sznA5aQ)

📖 **📖 Plot Summary:** Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, US CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

***

### 🗓️ **Event Details**

📍 **Meetup Time:** 6:00 PM (Final time + theatre announced Tuesday of event week)

* **$11.50** for *CineClub* members
* **$16.00** regular admission

🎫 Buy your ticket here: [https://www.cineplex.com](https://www.cineplex.com)
📍🪑 **Where I will be sitting:**

🍿 **After the Movie:**
Yes, we’re heading out after! It’s not just a movie night — it’s a social night. Let's talk, laugh, and dissect every plot twist.

***

### ✅ **Before You Sign Up**

* Please **buy your ticket first** — seating is limited!
* When signing up, let us know your **seat number** so we can try to group everyone together.
* You can still sign up or just **show up on the day** if you’re not sure you can make it — we’re flexible!

***

### 🎥 **A Quick Word About Movie Etiquette**

We love a great film experience. Please:

* Turn off your phone
* Don’t talk during the movie
* Be respectful of others

Repeat offenders will be removed from the group — we take our cinema seriously (but with snacks).

***

### 👥 **About the Group**

This event is open to everyone — single, not single, shy, social, new in town or a long-time local. We're a group for people who love movies *and* making real connections. We also do walks, hikes, restaurants, arts & culture — come be part of it!
