title: Fast Friends: Meet New People, Make Connections & Play 50+ Board Games | 25–45
description:
Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
Making new friends as an adult can be harder than it seems. You want to meet new people, have good conversations and build genuine connections — but knowing where to start isn't always easy.

🤝 That's where Fast Friends comes in.

Join us at Stout Irish Pub for a professionally hosted social evening designed to make meeting people feel natural and enjoyable. With guided conversations, rotations and fun themed connection rounds, you'll have an easy way to meet a variety of people, discover shared interests and start building new friendships — even if you arrive on your own.

And the evening doesn't end with the hosted rounds! Stay for 50+ board games, drinks, food and Stout's After Dark Specials. 🎲🍻

🎟️ Book Early & Save: [https://toronto7thnov.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto7thnov.eventbrite.co.uk)
You can pay securely online with any debit or credit card through PayPal — no PayPal account required.

Advance tickets are cheaper and help us plan the right space and group size for a comfortable evening.

Early Bird: CAD $10 \| Regular: CAD $15 \| At the Door: CAD $20 cash

🤝 The Evening
7:00 PM — Welcome & Settle In
Meet your host, Kruttika, grab a drink and get comfortable.
Whether you've recently moved to Toronto or have lived here for years, it's a chance to step out, meet some new faces and enjoy a different kind of Saturday evening.
Coming alone? You're very welcome — many guests attend solo, and our host will help you settle in and get connected.

7:30–8:30 PM — Hosted Fast Friends
Meeting people doesn't have to mean approaching a room full of strangers and hoping a conversation takes off.
Our host guides you through short conversations and rotations, so you can meet a variety of people throughout the evening. You don't have to worry about who to approach or what to say next — the structure makes it easier to get involved and discover who you connect with.
✨ Themed Connection Rounds
We'll add interactive prompts and themed conversation challenges to help you discover shared interests, swap stories and find unexpected common ground.
From travel and food to music, hobbies and weekend adventures, these rounds help move conversations beyond the usual small talk.

🎲 8:30 PM onwards — 50+ Board Games & Socialising
Why end the evening just as you're getting to know people?
Stout has more than 50 board games available, giving you an easy way to keep socialising after the hosted rounds. Join a game, meet others around the table, share a few laughs, grab another drink or simply continue a conversation.
You don't need to be a board-game expert. It's all about having fun together and giving new connections more time to grow.

🍻 Stay for Stout's After Dark Specials
If you're planning to stay later, Stout's After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.
It's a great way to extend your evening, relax with the people you've met and enjoy more of Stout's lively pub atmosphere.

❤️ Why Come Along?
✔️ Meet 20+ new people in one evening
✔️ Professionally hosted conversations and rotations
✔️ Interactive themed rounds to spark better conversations
✔️ 50+ board games at Stout 🎲
✔️ Stout's After Dark Specials from 9–11 PM 🍻
✔️ Reserved space for our group
✔️ Relaxed Irish pub atmosphere
✔️ An opportunity to meet members from across our Toronto Meetup communities
✔️ Solo attendees welcome
✔️ Designed for ladies and gents aged 25–45
✔️ Friendship-focused — not a dating event

📍 Why Stout Irish Pub?
Located at 221 Carlton Street, Stout offers a relaxed, welcoming pub atmosphere with food, drinks and an impressive selection of more than 50 board games.
It's a great setting for an evening that starts with hosted conversations and continues with board games, laughter and more time to get to know the people you've met.

👥 Who Is It For?
You don't need to be new to Toronto, belong to an existing group or know anyone attending.
Whether you're looking to build a social circle, meet people beyond work, make friends after moving to the city or simply enjoy a different kind of Saturday night, you're welcome.
Come by yourself or bring a friend. We'll help make the introductions easier.

🌍 About Fast Friends
For over 10 years, Fast Friends has been bringing people together through professionally hosted social events in 30+ cities worldwide.
Our goal is simple: make meeting new people easier, more relaxed and more enjoyable.

Come for the conversations. Stay for the board games. Leave with new connections. ❤️
Come solo. We'll guide the experience. You make the connections. 🤝

title: SPECIMEN: Science Fiction on Stage
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi all,

We've been invited to see an original sci-fi play called SPECIMEN at Axis Theatre Company in Greenwich Village with discounted tickets for just $10!
.
Written and directed by Randall Sharp, SPECIMEN takes place aboard a damaged research spacecraft, where a crew struggles to make sense of their new reality. TheaterScene calls it a "... darkly absurd sci-fi fever dream…" that "...arrives like a transmission from a dying satellite: garbled, abrasive, funny, ugly, unexpectedly moving, and very much alive…"
.
The production is a dark comedy and has an avant-garde, 1970s sci-fi feel. From [their website](https://axiscompany.org/mainstage.php), SPECIMEN "...draws from the tradition of downtown experimental and absurdist theatre, blending visual storytelling, heightened performance, dark humor, and immersive design..."
.
Tickets are usually $40, so this is a big discount to see a new, well-reviewed show.
.

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons
location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: 🍂 Crothers Woods Fall Hike & Ice Cream Treat! 🍦
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
## 🍂 **Crothers Woods Fall Hike & Ice Cream Treat!** 🍦

Toronto doesn’t have many true hiking trails — but Crothers Woods is one of the best! This beautiful wooded trail is especially stunning in the fall, with the leaves turning every shade of red and gold.
We’ll start by walking along **Broadview Avenue to Pottery Road**, heading down the hill to meet the **Don Valley Trail**. From there, we’ll join the **Crothers Woods Trail**, take in the fall colours, stop for a short break, and then walk back.

There are a few light hills — and one big one at the very end (Pottery Road, I’m looking at you!) — but don’t worry, there’s a sweet reward waiting. After all that hard work, we’ll stop for **Dairy Queen ice cream**!
This hike is a bit more challenging than some of our regular walks, but totally worth it for the views (and the ice cream).

**This event happens rain or shine!**

***

### 📍 **Meetup Details**

**Meeting Spot:** Right outside **Broadview Subway Station** — I’ll be the one wearing the **Moose Hat!** 🦌
**Ending Spot:** Broadview Subway Station
**Meetup Fee:** $5 (cash in person or e-transfer to **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**)

***

### 🕒 **Timing**

11:00am and I will only wait 5mins — the hike should take about **2 hours**.
You can leave anytime you like if you need to head back early.

***

### 🥾 **What to Bring**

* Water
* Good walking or hiking shoes
* A snack
* A positive attitude (and maybe room for ice cream!)

***

### ⚠️ **A Quick Note**

Sometimes things come up and I might need to cancel or reschedule. Please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

***

### 👋 **About This Group**

This group is open to **everyone** — whether you’re single or not, new to the city, or just looking to be social and make friends.
We also host **movies, walks, hikes, arts & culture events, and restaurant outings**!
You can RSVP ahead of time **or just show up** if you’re not sure you can make it — we’re flexible like that.

***

title: Landmarks 6: Gladstone Hotel to The Edgewater Hotel Via Gutta Percha
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Toronto is a city that hides its history in plain sight. Beneath the glass towers are layers of stories — grand hotels that vanished overnight, political scandals whispered through stone corridors, theatres that once glittered under gaslight, and laneways where the city first learned how to become a metropolis.

This new Toronto History Walks tour invites the walker to slow down, and see the city differently.

Let's return to a bygone era: late 1930s. Parkdale would already have had a long fascinating history behind it, but you would also be looking at a neighbourhood that was changing with the times. One of the most interesting examples was the Edgewater Hotel, built in 1939 at 14 Roncesvalles Avenue, at The Queensway.

It was built by Fred Hammer and became part of a very busy transportation hub, sitting beside the Sunnyside Bus Terminal. The building has survived, although the Edgewater name eventually disappeared and the hotel went through several incarnations. It is a wonderful reminder that Parkdale's history isn't just Victorian, there is twentieth-century history here as well.

And then we come to the Gladstone Hotel, which is one of those buildings that almost seem to have been watching the neighbourhood change. The hotel we see today dates from 1889 and was designed by Toronto architect George Martell Miller in the Richardsonian Romanesque style. Its location was absolutely perfect for business: it stood across from the Parkdale railway station, and was close to the Exhibition grounds. Travelling salesmen, railway workers, visitors to the CNE and commercial travellers could all find shelter here.

The original owner was Susanna Robinson, who was left a widow with thirteen children before construction of the hotel was completed.
The Gladstone tells us something important about Parkdale itself. For decades it was a working-class gathering place, and as the factories and industries changed, so did the fortunes of the hotel. The great tower once had a cupola that could be seen from a distance, but that disappeared in the 1940s. By the later twentieth century the hotel had fallen on hard times and had developed a much different reputation. Yet it never completely lost its role as a community gathering place.

Eventually it was restored and reinvented, becoming part of the artistic and cultural life of Queen Street West.

And finally, we get to one of the great industrial stories of old Parkdale — the Gutta Percha & Rubber Manufacturing Company. Established here in 1883 on West Lodge Avenue, the factory became one of the largest employers in the neighbourhood and, at its height, the largest rubber manufacturer in Canada. They made all sorts of rubber products — hose, belting, boots, footwear, mats and eventually products connected with the rapidly growing automobile industry.

The factory operated until 1960, when changing technology, synthetic rubber and competition finally brought its long Parkdale story to an end. Three places — the Edgewater, the Gladstone and Gutta Percha — give us three very different Parkdales: the Parkdale of travel and transportation, the Parkdale of hotels and community life, and the Parkdale of factories and working people. Put them together and you begin to see just how fascinating this neighbourhood really is.

This walking tour begins at The Gladstone Hotel at the northeast corner of Queen Street West and Gladstone Avenue, one block east of Dufferin Street. We end at the corner of Queen Street West and Roncesvalles Avenue.

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
The phone is ringing.

The roof is banging.

French downstairs.

English upstairs.

Caught in the middle: five people, one couch, and a landlord calling it an open-concept bedroom.

**Welcome to Far-Flung Peoples**, an award-winning, fast-paced, multilingual dark comedy set inside a crooked house in downtown Toronto, where its residents are squeezed into a living arrangement that would raise questions at City Hall, if City Hall were paying attention.

location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

title: Nov 9 - Agentic Labeling for Specialized Visual Data
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 09, 2026
9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/when-prompting-beats-training-agentic-labeling-for-specialized-visual-data-november-9-2026)**

Frontier multimodal models handle familiar concepts well and struggle on niche ones: sorting drill-core samples into 35 geological classes, or telling adhesion from scarring on a ceramic substrate. Our study across 11 specialized visual datasets in manufacturing inspection, geology, and medical imaging found that a few labeled examples in the prompt can close much of that gap, and it also found where that stops working.

**What you’ll learn:**

* Niche versus hard: how in-context examples supply domain knowledge a model is missing, and how to tell a niche task from a genuinely hard one
* What the study measured: on an industrial defect task, one labeled example per class raised macro-F1 from 34% to 59% with no fine-tuning, while on other tasks trained specialists pulled ahead at 5 to 10 examples per class
* Building a few-shot labeling task: define classes, pick reference examples, preview predictions on a small batch, and refine the instructions
* Finding the crossover point: when to stop prompting a foundation model and train a specialist on bootstrapped labels
* Running it on your own data: attendees get free GPU compute from Nebius to try the workflow after the session

title: Recovery College Co Design Course For Graduate & Mature Students)
location: Online (Zoom)
description:
Are you a graduate or mature student interested in shaping mental health and well‑being programming that reflects your lived experience at York University? This co‑design opportunity is for you.
In collaboration with Ontario Shores Centre for Mental Health Sciences, Student Counselling, Health & Well‑being (SCHW) is expanding our recovery college programming— a series of health and well‑being workshops designed to help students thrive amid the unique pressures of advanced study, research, caregiving, work and life transitions.
What will we do?
You and a small group of fellow graduate and mature students will work alongside SCHW and Ontario Shores to co‑create the next set of recovery college workshops launching in Winter/Spring 2027. Together, you will shape workshop topics, content and learning activities and how sessions are delivered and facilitated.
What will we learn?

Recovery college principles and how education rooted in lived experience supports mental health
Co‑design methods for building impactful student‑centered programming
How to draw on your own experiences navigating academic and life‑stage pressures as a source of expertise
How to collaborate as part of a design team to create accessible, empowering mental health workshops

Program Details
This 5‑week co‑design series runs virtually on Mondays from 1:15 to 2:15 PM, from November 9 to December 7. Participation is open to all graduate and mature students.
Honorarium
In appreciation for your support, participants will receive $25 loaded directly to their YU card for each session attended in full (up to $125 for completing all five sessions).
Note: Co‑Design sessions run for one hour. To receive the honorarium for a session, you must attend the full session. If you are unable to attend the full hour or experience technical difficulties, please contact Holly Stacey directly at hstacey@yorku.ca ( mailto:hstacey@yorku.ca ).
Registration
Space is limited (maximum 12 participants) and offered on a first‑come, first‑served basis. Registration is open to mature undergraduate students, graduate students and School of Continuing Studies students. description:

Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.

In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).

description:
When you're the whole company, the admin never ends: emails, scheduling, proposals, follow-ups. What if you could design a system to handle the busywork?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,

title: Changing the Narrative: Toronto’s Indigenous – Settler History
location: Toronto Reference Library, 1st Floor, Beeton Hall
description:
Learn more about Toronto's multifaceted Indigenous history, which has often been ignored or minimized due to the telling of the region's history only from settler perspectives. Join us for a panel discussion about a public history project that worked with five local First Nations to create a more accurate and inclusive story of the region's past, and is transforming the way settlement of 19th century Ontario is represented at The Village at Black Creek (formerly Black Creek Pioneer Village).
Changing the Narrative: Reconnecting Settler and Indigenous Histories at Black Creek Pioneer Village was a collaborative project of York University historians, The Village at Black Creek, Jumblies Theatre, and the Mississaugas of the Credit, Chippewas of Rama, Six Nations of the Grand River, Chippewas of Georgina Island, and Mississaugas of Scugog Island First Nations.
This panel discussion will share research highlights, reflect on the process of collaboration, and explore how the project is expanding and enriching storytelling at one of the region’s prime living history museums.
The project’s findings have also been published in Where Histories Meet: Indigenous and Settler Encounters in the Toronto Area, by Victoria Freeman. The book explores this history from multiple perspectives in an accessible and richly illustrated format and includes excerpts from interviews with twenty Indigenous elders and knowledge keepers. It was nominated for a
2026 City of Toronto Book Award
and is the winner of the
2026 Heritage Toronto Book Award.
Panel members include:
Victoria      Freeman
, historical researcher and author of
Where Histories Meet:      Indigenous and Settler Encounters in the Toronto Area
.
Jennifer      Bonnell
, professor in the Department of History at York University and the      lead of the Changing the Narrative Project.
Allison      White
, curator at The Village at Black Creek (Toronto and Region      Conservation Authority).
Darin      Wybenga
, heritage interpreter for the Mississaugas of the Credit First      Nation, and member of the Research Committee for the Changing the      Narrative project.
Lauri      Hoeg
, Anishinaabe artist and cultural advisor from the Chippewas of      Georgina Island First Nation, and member of the Research Committee for the      Changing the Narrative project.
The panel discussion will last approximately 60 minutes, followed by a Q&A with audience members. No registration required.
source: Toronto Public Library — Adults, Show Up Toronto

title: Hank Idsinga: The High Road
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents retired homicide detective and author Hank Idsinga in conversation with Wendy Gillis at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
In his bestselling memoir
The High Road: Confessions of a Homicide Cop
, Idsinga takes readers behind the crime scene tape and into the mean streets of Toronto's most notorious murders. Teaming up with partners including future police chief Mark Saunders, Idsinga built a reputation for excellent recall and sharp instinct, finding motive and method faster than most. As the public face of that investigation, Idsinga remained strong and compassionate before the cameras, even as the police force faced fierce criticism over its handling of the case.
How do homicide detectives carry the weight of the cases they never solve? What does real accountability within policing actually look like, and why does it matter? And what can three decades on the front lines of Toronto's worst crimes teach us about justice, institutional trust, and the human cost of violence?
Join veteran crime reporter Wendy Gillis in conversation with Hank Idsinga for a gripping, candid evening inside the world of Canada's most storied homicide unit.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Your Health Matters: Diabetes Myths and Facts
description:
Living with diabetes or prediabetes can come with a lot of information about what to eat, what to avoid, and how to manage your blood sugar. With so much advice out there, it can be difficult to separate fact from fiction or know where to focus.
Join Catherine Cai, Registered Dietitian and Certified Diabetes Educator, for a practical and interactive session that separates fact from fiction and explores realistic ways to better understand and manage diabetes and prediabetes.
What to Expect
Understanding Blood Sugar:
Learn what your levels mean and how an A1C test provides a picture of your average levels over time.
Diabetes Myths and Facts:
Explore common myths      and misconceptions about diabetes and separate fact from fiction.
Lifestyle and Blood Sugar:
Learn how sleep,      stress and other lifestyle factors can affect blood sugar.
Building Balanced Meals:
Learn practical ways      to build balanced, diabetes-friendly meals.
Balance, Not Perfection:
Explore how balance      and consistency can support diabetes management without striving for      perfection.
About the Presenter
Catherine Cai is a Registered Dietitian and Certified Diabetes Educator at Crosstown Family Health Team. She provides practical information and guidance to help people better understand nutrition and support their health.

title: Writing Place Workshop with Marc Nair
location: Toronto Reference Library, Third-Floor, Discussion Room
description:
​This writing workshop revolves around writing place, where participants will write poems or flash fiction about a place that is near and dear to them. Participants take an observational narrative approach to writing about place, employing selected poetry and flash fiction techniques. They will take turns sharing their work while the facilitator, poet Marc Nair, offers on-the-spot feedback.
This event will feature a
90 minute Workshop:
Introduction - facilitator (Marc) will invite participants to name their favorite place and expand on why it is so significant for them.
Facilitator will begin by sharing a couple of poems that are rooted in a sense of place, exploring how the poems are written in order to offer concrete suggestions for participants.
Participants then engage in a free writing exercise to generate content about a particular place. Facilitator will then invite some participants to share and suggest how to shape the content using a 'seed' idea or image from the free writing.
Facilitator will also talk about flash fiction (100-200 word) stories as an alternative to the poem. Facilitator will share some examples.
Participants will write their own poem or flash fiction over the next twenty minutes.
They will take turns sharing their work while the facilitator offers on the spot feedback
Marc Nair is an artist, educator and cultural entrepreneur from Singapore who is currently based in Toronto, Canada.
Registration is required.

title: Author Talk featuring Dan Jones
location: Church of the Holy Trinity
description:
[at Church of the Holy Trinity]
Join Ben McNally Books, in partnership with Penguin Canada, for a special conversation with bestselling historian, novelist, and podcaster Dan Jones.
Dan will be discussing his new book
Castles: A Fortified History of the World
.
Doors will open at 6 p.m., the conversation will begin at 6:30. An audience Q & A will follow, and Dan will be happy to sign copies of his book at the end of the evening.
Two ticket options are available: General admission, and Book + Ticket. Book + Ticket includes a copy of Dan Jones' latest history,
Castles: A Fortified History of the World.
Please note:
neither ticket option will require a physical ticket, and you will not be charged for delivery if you choose any of the delivery options.
About the Book
From New York Times bestselling historian Dan Jones, a grand and sweeping history of the world, told through over three thousand years of iconic fortifications.
Castles have been built to defend humanity for millennia—from the walls of Troy in the Bronze Age and the desert bastion of Krak des Chevaliers in Syria; to Windsor Castle and the Tower of London; to Himeji in Japan and Fort Sumter in Charleston, South Carolina. They have inspired terror and passion, foiled conquering forces, and been deployed as the ultimate expression of wealth, status, and supremacy.
In
Castles
, Jones leads readers on a journey through the many eras of castle-building and across continents as each stronghold tells a unique story of power, politics, and survival, revealing the shifting tides of warfare, the rise and fall of empires, the resilience of people under siege, and the flourishing of new ideas.
Blending rich storytelling, deep research, and beautiful original illustrations,
Castles
is an epic story of why humans build fortifications and how they powerfully capture our imagination. With Jones's trademark scholarship and flair, he shows how defiance, endurance, and ambition have been carved into the landscapes we've inherited.
About the Author
Dan Jones is the
New York Times
bestselling author of
Henry V
,
Powers and Thrones
,
Crusaders
,
The Templars
,
The Plantagenets
,
Wars of the Roses
, and
Magna Carta
, as well as the
Essex Dogs
trilogy of novels.
He is the host of the podcast
This Is History: A Dynasty to Die For
and has produced, written, and presented dozens of TV shows, including the popular Netflix series Secrets of
Great British Castles
. As of 2025, he is a member of the board of trustees of Historic Royal Palaces, an organization dedicated to managing and maintaining the unoccupied palaces of England.

title: Discussing Treaties with Rick Monture
location: Spadina Road
description:
Join Professor Rick Monture for a discussion about pre-contact peace agreements between Indigenous nations, treaties between Indigenous peoples and Europeans, and the various "numbered" treaties in Canada. Learn about the philosophies behind the Dish With One Spoon wampum and its significance today, as well as the 1784 Haldimand Proclamation as it pertains to First Nations in Southern Ontario. Come discover why treaties are a vital part of the movement towards Truth and Reconciliation!
No registration required.
Bio:
Rick Monture is a member of the Mohawk nation, Turtle clan, from Six Nations of the Grand River Territory.  He is a Professor in the Department of English & Cultural Studies and Indigenous Studies at McMaster University where he teaches classes on Indigenous literature, Haudenosaunee history, traditional narratives, and Bob Dylan.  He is also a Community Research Fellow with Six Nations Polytechnic and the Deyohahage / Indigenous Knowledge Centre based at Six Nations and is an active member of the language revitalization movement in his community.  In partnership with the Woodland Cultural Centre in Brantford, Rick currently holds a Social Science and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC) award for a project that examines the events that led to the overthrow of the traditional Haudenosaunee government, by Ottawa, to implement an elected council system in 1924.  His book,
We Share our Matters: Two Centuries of Writing and Resistance at Six Nations of the Grand River
, was published in 2014 and is an examination of the Grand River Haudenosaunee’s assertions of sovereignty and social justice through letters, political activism, literature, and film. Rick lives at Six Nations with his family.

title: The Way We Were: Seniors’ Memories of Life in the Junction
location: Annette Street, Auditorium
description:
Get a glimpse of the Junction in past decades through the memories and family stories of people who were there. Back Lane Studios, based in Roncesvalles, presents a selection of short videos from Mapping Our Memories, a project collecting place-based stories from older people in video and written formats. You'll learn about:
Sheila McIlraith's talented mother, a lively young woman who served as public health nurse at Annette and Runnymede public schools, drove her own car in the 1920s and was choir master and organist at High Park Baptist Church. But she gave all that up when she got married in her late 30s.
Local grocer Doug Breakwell, whose store was at the corner of Annette and Indian Grove Cres. He helped out Lorne Clayton's mother many times when she couldn't pay for groceries. But the tables turned. In the 1950s, when small stores were losing out to supermarkets, Lorne was able to help Doug out.
Lois Broad, who made our most popular video
Growing up in the Junction,
had many vivid memories to share, from the Minnies swimming pools at the corner of Quebec Ave. and Bloor, to High Park Avenue United Church, where her parents were the first couple to be married.
We'll screen a curated selection of short documentaries, learn about Mapping Our Memories, and meet some of the people behind the stories during a Q&A.
Light refreshments will be served.  Drop-in. No registration required.

title: ABCD Reads Body Language by Meg Howrey
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***[Body Language](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4801989)*** by Meg Howrey.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/6325601387675648) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"Sloane, a former actress now working as a therapist, is determined to find a meaningful way through menopause, away from marketing schemes, possibly with the aid of psychedelics. Her sister Laurel is managing her own growing rage and restlessness while engaging in work at an environmental non-profit and raising teenagers. Nanette, the youngest, has answered a long-delayed religious calling and is living as a Novice in a convent. All three lives will be further disrupted when Sloane receives a call summoning her to their mother’s house, Laurel discovers possible evidence of her husband’s infidelity, and Nanette finds herself in the middle of a media frenzy after a spontaneous act of public prayer.
Soon, all three are reunited under their mother’s roof, and no one can seem to agree about anything beyond the Barbara has dementia, as did her mother and sister before her. Will it be an opportunity for the closed door of their very private mother’s inner life to crack open? A lesson in care; a shared responsibility that will be the making of this family, divided by large age gaps, parental divorce, and temperament? Or will a stunning revelation upend not only their mother’s remaining time, but divide the sisters permanently?
With razor-sharp prose and undeniable humor, acclaimed author Meg Howrey brings an American family in the midst of a painful crisis to unforgettable life, interrogating memory and emotional inheritance, the right of a woman’s autonomy, and the indelible bonds even the most disparate of sisters can share." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/244709885-body-language))

"Howrey is a reliably beautiful stylist, and her slyly funny prose and blade-sharp insights into human behavior really should put her in the same conversation as writers like Ann Patchett and Barbara Kingsolver. Though this novel hits some familiar beats, Howrey manages to haul in plenty of shimmering pearls on the perils and joys of womanhood—whatever that means.
A comfort meal of a novel: poignant and prismatic." (from [Kirkus](https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/meg-howrey/body-language-4/))

title: Civic Meetup #568: Hack the Count: Turning Window Sensors into Street Safety Evidence
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom / Metro Hall
description:
Topic: Hack the Count: Turning Window Sensors into Street Safety Evidence

When Ontario removed roughly 700 automated speed enforcement cameras from school and community safety zones in 2025, neighbourhoods lost one of their few sources of hard evidence about speeding. What happens when residents start collecting that evidence themselves?

This talk introduces CIVIC (Community-centred Infrastructures for Visible and Inclusive Cities), an urban living lab in London, Ontario. Residents host low-cost, privacy-by-design Telraam traffic sensors and noise monitors in their own windows. These sensors count cars, cyclists and pedestrians and estimate speeds, all without storing images. Professor Carrie Mitchell will walk through how the network was built, what the data shows, and how residents and city staff are using it to make the case for traffic calming. She’ll also cover what’s hard: data gaps, privacy trade-offs, and keeping a volunteer sensor network running. Finally, she’ll ask what it would take to scale community-owned street data across Ontario, and where civic technologists can help.

‎

Speaker: Carrie Mitchell (in-person)

Carrie Mitchell is an Associate Professor in the School of Planning at the University of Waterloo, where she studies urban climate resilience, community-based planning, and, more recently, road safety governance. She is the founder of CIVIC (OurCIVICFutures.ca), an urban living lab funded by Waterloo’s Global Futures Fund that is deploying privacy-by-design traffic and noise sensors with residents and community partners. Before joining Waterloo, she spent five years at Canada’s International Development Research Centre (IDRC) managing urban environment and climate research across Asia. She lives in London, Ontario.

‎

7:20-7:50 Presentation and Q\&A/discussion

title: Hot Docs & Soulpepper Present: Everybody to Kenmure Street
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
When the government came for their neighbours, an entire community stood in the way.

A new monthly series in partnership with Hot Docs, bringing visionary documentary filmmaking from around the world to Toronto’s East End.

From executive producer Emma Thompson comes an inspiring and profoundly moving portrait of what everyday citizens are capable of in the face of injustice. In May 2021, a U.K. Home Office dawn raid triggered one of the most spontaneous and successful acts of civil resistance in recent memory. In Scotland’s most diverse neighbourhood, hundreds of residents rush to the streets to stop the deportation of their neighbours. The morning in Glasgow, the first day of Eid, started as any other. But when neighbors heard through community message networks that two local men were snatched up for deportation, hundreds of people left their daily lives to rush down to Kenmure Street and put their bodies on the line. Though mostly strangers and with almost no planning, this extremely diverse group organized themselves, taking on essential roles to allow the collective to achieve their goal: protecting their own from government forces going after the most vulnerable among them. Everybody to Kenmure Street reminds us of the power that is always inherent in the people.

“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

title: Nov 11 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Time, Date and Location**

Nov 11, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-november-11-2026)**

**Agentic RAG: Beyond Retrieve-and-Generate**

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the default pattern for grounding large language models in external knowledge, but most implementations still follow a rigid retrieve-once, generate-once pipeline — one that struggles with multi-hop questions, ambiguous queries, and knowing when its own retrieved context is insufficient. This talk introduces Agentic RAG, where retrieval is treated as an action within an agent's reasoning loop rather than a fixed upstream step.

We'll examine query decomposition and routing for breaking complex questions into targeted sub-queries, self-reflective and corrective retrieval loops that let an agent judge and re-query its own results, and tool-orchestration patterns (via MCP) that let retrieval sit alongside other agent actions like database lookups and API calls. Using a live architecture — evolving a standard RAG chatbot into an agentic, MCP-connected system — we'll walk through what changes in design, and where these systems introduce new failure modes: grounding drift, latency and cost from repeated retrieval loops, and cases where a simpler RAG pipeline still wins.

Attendees will leave with a practical framework for deciding when the added complexity of agentic RAG is worth it, and a set of design patterns for building it correctly.

*About the Speaker*

[Balaji Venkatasubramaniyar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/balaji-venkatasubramaniyar/) is a Technical Lead at Wisdom Infotech, leading a 15+ person engineering team delivering enterprise solutions. With 13+ years of experience in enterprise software and insurance technology, he specializes in agentic AI systems, RAG architectures, and vector databases.

**GeoAI for the Physical World: Earth Observation, Foundation Models, and Urban Digital Twins**

Earth observation provides a unique form of computer vision for understanding the physical world at city to continental scales. In this talk, I will show how satellite imagery, geospatial data, machine learning, and foundation-model representations can be combined to characterize urban environments and environmental conditions.

I will present UrbanScope Open, an open GeoAI digital-twin prototype integrating Earth observation with 3D buildings, vegetation, land-surface temperature, air quality, noise, population, and other urban data. I will also share lessons from my research using geospatial foundation-model embeddings for environmental prediction across Europe.

The talk will discuss how these approaches can contribute to increasingly multimodal AI systems capable of reasoning about real-world environments.

*About the Speaker*

[Cesar Alvarez](https://voxel51.com/events/cesar.alvarez@uni-a.de) is a researcher at the University of Augsburg working at the intersection of GeoAI, Earth observation, remote sensing, and environmental intelligence. His research applies machine learning, computer vision, and geospatial foundation models to problems including urban environments, climate risk, air quality, and agriculture.

**Can agents get curious?**

Most AI agents are good at answering a question once we tell them exactly what to look for. The harder problem is building agents that can explore a complex dataset autonomously: generating hypotheses, deciding which analyses are worth running, allocating additional compute when evidence is ambiguous, and knowing when they have enough evidence to stop.

In this talk, I’ll show an architecture for autonomous research agents that combines structured knowledge, iterative tool use, and explicit evidence tracking to turn open-ended questions into a sequence of testable investigations. I’ll discuss practical lessons from building and evaluating these systems, including why more test-time compute does not automatically produce better research and how provenance and evaluation can make long-running agents more reliable.

I’ll close with a live example of an agent exploring a dataset, revising its hypotheses, and choosing what to investigate next.

*About the Speaker*

[Srivatsa P](https://www.linkedin.com/in/srivatsa-p) is a member of technical staff at Sigma Computing, where he works on AI agents that reason over complex enterprise data. Previously, he worked on machine learning at Apple and conducted research at the MIT Media Lab; outside of traditional ML, he has also worked on mapping coral reefs through underwater imaging, which sparked an enduring interest in how intelligent systems make sense of messy real-world data.

**Does Cross-Validation Work in Deep Learning?**

Cross-validation is a standard in hyperparameter optimization in classical ML, but is generally considered computationally prohibitive and unnecessary in deep learning. We investigated whether CV produces 1. better DL models 2. better estimates of future performance of said models. We focused on medical image classification as an important deep learning application domain.

Our results show that cross-validation consistently and materially reduces the gap between development and independent testing error for relatively small training datasets (up to about 1000 images). The test performance improvement was generally modest. We discuss the implications for deep-learning practitioners, including whether the increased computational cost of cross-validation is justified.

*About the Speaker*

[Ljubomir Buturovic](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ljubomir-buturovic-798156/) is an AI scientist and biotech executive with extensive experience in clinical diagnostics, including work at Inflammatix and Pathwork Diagnostics. His current research focuses on deep-learning image classification, infectious disease adjudication using LLMs, and development of AI models for helping critically ill patients.

title: 3D Design with Onshape
location: Flemingdon Park, Upstairs Program Room
description:
Learn how to create parametric designs using cloud based software Onshape.
This hands-on workshop introduces participants to the fundamentals of 3D design using Onshape, a cloud-based CAD software. Whether you're an aspiring engineer, designer, or hobbyist, this session provides the tools and knowledge to start creating your own 3D models.
What You’ll Learn:
Getting Started:
Overview of Onshape's interface, navigation tools, and cloud-based collaboration features.
Core Design Principles:
Understanding 3D modeling basics, including sketches, extrusions, and revolutions.
Hands-On Practice:
Creating simple 3D parts, assembling components, and exploring design modifications.
Best Practices:
Tips for efficient modeling, managing design iterations, and exporting models for 3D printing or other applications.
This program is ideal for beginners with no prior experience in CAD software, as well as those looking to explore Onshape's capabilities.
Registration will start 2 weeks before this class. Computers will be provided.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Nov 11 - Toronto Physical AI Workshop and Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join us at the University of Toronto on November 11 for the Toronto Physical AI Workshop and Meetup, co-presented by Nebius and Voxel51.

Seats are limited, **[Pre-registration is mandatory.](https://voxel51.com/events/toronto-physical-ai-workshop-and-meetup-november-11-2026)**

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 11, 2026
5:30 PM - 8:30 PM
The Conference Centre at U of T
Giovanni Room (2nd Floor)
89 Chestnut St.
Toronto, ON M5G 1R1

**Meetup Agenda**
*5:30–6:30 PM*

* Networking, food, drinks, and lightning talks

**Workshop Agenda**
This hands-on session uses DROID, a real-world robotics dataset loaded into FiftyOne as a native multimodal MCAP recording, and YOLO11n, fine-tuned live during the session.

*6:30–7:30 PM*

* Welcome + framing: from raw robot logs to a trained detector
* Explore a real DROID robotics recording in FiftyOne's native multimodal MCAP viewer: camera, proprioception, and language on one synced timeline, no ROS install required
* Curate: extract and browse frames from the recording, filter and deduplicate
* Compute embeddings on the curated frames; explore via similarity search and embeddings visualization (via Nebius Serverless AI Jobs)

*7:30–8:00 PM*

* Auto-label: open-vocabulary detection to generate bounding boxes for the robot gripper and target objects
* Train: fine-tune a YOLO11n detector on the auto-labeled frames (via Nebius Serverless AI Jobs)
* Evaluate results and close the loop: view predictions back on the original MCAP timeline

*8:00–8:30 PM*

* What else Nebius offers: Token Factory walkthrough — chat/vision models, fine-tuning, credits

title: The Writings of David Thompson on His Travels in North America
location: North York Central Library, Room 1, 2nd floor
description:
The Writings of David Thompson
This presentation examines the historical Writings of David Thompson. Between 1784 and 1812, David Thompson (1770-1857) explored and traded over a vast expanse of western North America. Later in life, the surveyor and fur trader wrote what he called his
Travels
, a spectacular geographical and spirited intellectual journey of the Canadian experience. His story tells of a remarkable life in the fur trade but it also captures hid reflections on the land and the indigenous peoples of western North America.
Presented by Bill Moreau, editor of the three-volume work,
The Writings of David Thompson
.
Registration is encouraged but not necessary.

title: Wednesday Night Movie: 1945 (2017)
location: Don Mills, Auditorium
description:
Join us for a viewing of our Wednesday Night Movie
: 1945
(2017)
Directed by
: Ferenc Torok
Starring
: Peter Rudolf, Bence Tasnadi, Tamas Szabo Kimmel
1 hrs 31 minutes
Rated G
12 August 1945, 11 AM. Two mysterious strangers dressed in black appear at the railway station of a Hungarian village. title: 'Hunger' at the Alumnae Theatre (Nov 11 to Nov 22)
location: Alumnae Theatre,70 Berkeley St, Toronto, ON M5A 2W5, Canada
description:
ALUMNAE THEATRE OPENS ALL-CANADIAN, ALL-FEMALE PLAYWRIGHT SEASON WITH MEGHAN GREELEY’S HUNGER

Alumnae Theatre is proud to launch its 2026/2027 season, centred around the theme Stories of Survival, with Newfoundland playwright Meghan Greeley’s riveting drama, Hunger. Directed by Sarini Kumarasinghe and produced by Kimberley Ann Croscup, the production runs from November 11 to November 22, 2026, in the Studio Theatre.

Hunger marks the opening production in a milestone season for Alumnae Theatre, featuring a lineup written entirely by Canadian female playwrights.

Set in an isolated farmhouse during an unspecified period of war, Hunger explores survival, currency, and the fragile nature of morality. In the midst of a violent conflict, Johanna and Max attempt an act of heroics by hiding three refugees in a tiny alcove behind their walls. As space and food dwindle and the war outside reaches a deafening climax, the couple and their secret guests are pushed to their absolute limits.

First premiered by Newfoundland’s White Rooster Theatre in 2019 before embarking on a provincial tour, Greeley’s play earned widespread critical acclaim upon its publication by Breakwater Books, where it was named a finalist for the prestigious BMO Winterset Award. Praised by literary reviewers for its "askew dialogue and cutaway violence" reminiscent of the haunting, surrealist works of Caryl Churchill, Hunger delivers a tense, dark examination of human nature under extreme duress.

"We’re thrilled to begin our season with a play that so fiercely challenges our understanding of human endurance and compassion," says the production team. "Greeley's voice sets a fitting tone for a season dedicated to extraordinary stories of survival written by some of Canada’s most compelling female theatre artists."

The cast is led by Yolande Williams and Ryan Giesen (as Johanna and Max) with Kimberly Van Vo, Arya Ashoori, and Irene Kalogridis (as Rivka, Isaac, and Helen) filling out this ensemble of striking local talent.

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

title: Unsettling the Public Record: Decolonial Research Methods for Troubling Times
description:
As censorship and retaliation become growing concerns, turning to public records and events as sources of ethnographic data raises important ethical questions. Guided by Black feminist critiques of archival violence, Alexandra will examine how the very idea of what is considered “public” can reproduce harm and shape the people and communities represented within public records.
The session will explore the situated ethical obligations that emerge when conducting ethnographic research in and through publics, and consider how research practices can not only unsettle the public record, but contribute to building more just worlds in troubling times.
Participants are welcome to attend all three sessions. Zoom details will be shared with registered participants ahead of each workshop.

title: Common Hour: Celebrating the Canadian League of Composers: John Burge, Piano
location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall, 112 Accolade East Building, York University
description:
In celebration of the Canadian League of Composers 75th Anniversary in 2026, composer and pianist, John Burge presents a solo piano recital of music composed by many of the CLC past presidents. Starting with music by founding President, John Weinzweig, the program proceeds chronologically to current president, Tyler Versluis. The concert opens with a musical land acknowledgement, “Trillium,” composed by Indigenous-Canadian composer and CLC member, Beverley McKiver, and concludes with a rousing collective singing of O Canada. This all-Canadian concert promises to be an event of historical, cultural and artistic significance.
Thursday, November 12, 2026
12:30 – 1:30 p.m. 
Tribute Communities Recital Hall
FREE
Composer and pianist, John Burge ( https://sdm.queensu.ca/people/burge-john ), taught at Queen’s University, Kingston, Ontario, for 38 years before retiring as a Professor Emeritus in 2025. Many of Burge’s orchestral works, such as Snowdrift, The Canadian Shield and Rocky Mountain Overture, have been performed by orchestras across Canada and internationally. His string orchestra work, Flanders Fields Reflections, as recorded by Sinfonia Toronto, received the 2009 Juno Award for the Best Canadian Classical Composition. In 2014 he was inducted into the Royal Society of Canada for his achievements as a composer and support of the Arts in Canada. Having completed his Associate Diploma from the Royal Conservatory of Toronto in Piano Performance while still in high school, John Burge has continued to perform throughout his career, usually in presentations of his own music. Over the years, his piano music has been included in a number of conservatory music syllabi and he is in high demand as a music festival adjudicator. A passionate advocate for Canadian music, he served on the executive committee of the Canadian League of Composers from 1993-2007 (including eight years as President) and on the SOCAN Foundation board of directors from 2009-2025, as well as on the boards of several arts organizations in the Kingston area.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Low Income Retirement Planning
location: Queen/Saulter
description:
November is Financial Literacy Month
Learn about government benefits, tax credits, and strategies to help protect your retirement income. Presented by John Stapleton from Open Policy Ontario.
These sessions are designed for seniors with low income and those who advise them.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
One-on-one support is available at select branches. Meet with Financial Empowerment staff for free financial counselling. Book your free appointment today. Speak with branch staff or visit
tpl.ca/financial-empowerment
for more information.

title: Investment and Real Estate Committee Meeting - November 12, 2026
Penguins: The Adventures of Pimba and family
location: Beaches, Program Room
description:
Discover more about penguin biology, ecology, and migration in this presentation of a collection of photographs taken during an MSc research exchange at the Punta Tombo Penguin Reserve in Patagonia, Argentina.
The photographs are accompanied by the story of Pimba, a penguin who migrates with her family from Patagonia to Brazil by following ocean currents. Through Pimba’s journey, children are introduced to the penguin life cycle in an engaging and accessible way, using real scientific research brought to life through storytelling and images.

title: From Agentic Development to Automated Delivery
description:
Toronto Enterprise DevOps User Group
How do you move from actively guiding AI agents to having them carry work through your team’s development process?

Join us for a practical session on agentic workflows in GitHub. We’ll show how people and agents clarify requirements, plan changes, and capture project knowledge, then use those shared skills and context to automate tasks such as assessing issues and reviewing pull requests.

Through demos, we’ll explore how these steps can connect into a workflow that takes a small bug from report to proposed fix, helping teams move faster and reduce bottlenecks. Along the way, we’ll show how engineers can inspect the agent’s work, step in when it needs refinement, and retain control over what merges.

*Come at 5:30 PM to grab some pizza and network. The presentation kicks off at 6:00 PM!*

title: Food Justice in Toronto: Panel Discussion
location: Malvern, Community Room
description:
Join an expert-led discussion on food justice in your community. Learn about Toronto's food system, the issues that affect our food access, and strategies to address food insecurity and inequity. The panel will be followed by a facilitated group discussion reflecting on engagement with local food systems and practices.
Panelists include:
Shath Ramesh
(she/they) is a community organizer and the Urban Agriculture Coordinator at Malvern Family Resource Centre, where they manage the Malvern Urban Farmers' Market. They hold a Masters in sustainability studies from Trent University and are passionate about food justice, climate action and advocacy.
Jade Guthrie
(she/her) is a queer, mixed-race educator, facilitator, and community organizer. As the Manager of Community Learning and Engagement at FoodShare Toronto, jade is committed to social change work rooted in justice, liberation, and joy and approaches this work with tenderness, curiosity, and reciprocity. Beyond 9-5, jade is an organizer with Justicia for Migrant Workers, a board member at Food Secure Canada, and sits on the City of Toronto’s Black Food Sovereignty Action Plan Advisory Circle.

Essential
Prompting Skills

Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.

Théâtre français de Toronto
s'associent pour créer un club de lecture théâtre. Ce rendez-vous mensuel est l'occasion de discuter et d'explorer des scènes mythiques ayant marqué le monde du théâtre. Avec
Georges Som
, médiateur culturel, nous essayerons de comprendre les enjeux de ces scènes, de découvrir leurs sens et de partager nos sentiments sur leurs auteurs et autrices. Papa doit manger
de Marie Ndiyae.  Papa est parti depuis si longtemps que personne n'espère plus son retour. Mais voilà que Papa revient, voilà que Papa exige de rentrer, sûr de son bon droit, dans la vie qu'il a fuie dix ans auparavant. Qui aime encore Papa? Qui peut prétendre avoir besoin de lui? Il a les apparences de la richesse et d'une jeunesse improbable. Il resplendit d'un éclat peu commun à Courbevoie. Surtout, il sait ce qu'on lui doit, même si ce n'est pas justifié, et qu'on l'aime encore, qu'on l'aimera toujours.

title: Imagining a Turtle Named Franklin by Brenda Clark
location: Lillian H. Smith, Lower Level- Auditorium
description:
Photo credit: Lee Higginson.
Join the Osborne Collection of Early Children's Books for our 19th Annual Sybille Pantazzi Memorial Lecture: Imagining a Turtle Named Franklin by Brenda Clark.
Award winning picture book illustrator, Brenda Clark is the original illustrator of the beloved Franklin the Turtle book series, by author Paulette Bourgeois. In this lecture, she will share how she became an artist and how Franklin was created. Brenda’s illustrations have played a key role in Franklin’s worldwide popularity, leading to the inspiration of the animated TV series, merchandise, spin-off books, a children’s garden on Toronto Island and a Canadian postage stamp. She will walk us through the process of designing and painting the art and explain how it takes some amazing teamwork to meet the challenges of Franklin’s success.
For the past 40 years, Brenda Clark has delighted children as the illustrator of the hugely successful Franklin the Turtle children’s book series. Over 70 million Franklin books have been sold in more than 30 languages worldwide, making it the single most successful picture book series in the history of Canadian publishing. In 2011, the archives of Brenda Clark were donated to the Osborne Collection of Early Children’s Books, and recognized by the Canadian Cultural Property Export Review Board as cultural property for its “Outstanding Significance and National Importance”. In 2014, Brenda was named a Member of the Order of Canada. She lives in Port Hope, Ontario.
Book signings will take place before the lecture from 5:00-6:00 pm on the 4th floor in the Osborne Collection.
Franklin in the Dark
