Having trouble logging in? Please make sure you’re using your PPY York U login. When you select SSO (Single Sign-On), you should be prompted to sign in with your PPY credentials. If you use a different login, you may not be able to access the system.

title: Benefits and Credits for Adults 65 Years & Older
location: Don Mills, Auditorium
description:
This presentation by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) provides an overview of the income sources, benefits, credits, and tax measures available to seniors. It explains retirement income programs such as Old Age Security (OAS), the Canada Pension Plan (CPP), and private pensions, and highlights the importance of filing a tax return every year to receive benefit payments and maintain eligibility for programs.
The presentation also covers key tax credits and deductions available to seniors, including the Age Amount, Pension Income Amount, Medical Expense Tax Credit, Home Accessibility Tax Credit, Disability Tax Credit, and pension income splitting. In addition, it shares information on free tax-filing assistance.
Drop in.  No registration required.

title: Get Things Done with AI: Build Your Own Productivity System
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home.

title: Clayming Love
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
Clayming Love            
                                
    



    
         
    




	

	


			
Events
	







	

	

	


				







	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Monday November 23, 2026
6:00 pm – 8:00 pm
 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    For ages 18+ 
Are you ready? Are you open? Are you willing? 
“The awareness in our hands is alive and continuous. The feeling of our lives will be awake in our fingers. We befriend the clay. The clay befriends us.” — M.C. Richards 
The sense of touch cannot happen anywhere but the here and now. Touch is immediate. Through exploration with clay we will recognize how we can be stuck because we have not looked deeply enough into the nature of our experience. 
Guided by a Zen Buddhist practitioner and registered art therapist, engage in clay exercises designed to call attention to habits of belief, judgments, and the stories we tell ourselves. With self-compassion, we will create possibilities to loosen their hold on us by working with the malleability of clay. 
At the end of the workshop we return the clay to its original form, letting go of what was created and ready to begin anew. 
This workshop welcomes everyone, whether you are new to or familiar with clay, breath, and presence.

Gardiner Friends may only purchase adult clay classes at the discounted rate for membership card holders. 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
                       
            
                
                    Instructor
                    
                
                
                    Suzanne Thomson, Zen Buddhist practitioner and registered art therapist
                    
                
                
                    Suzanne Thomson is ceramic artist, registered psychotherapist, and art therapist with over 30 years of experience integrating these practices to facilitate healing, community building and social transformation work. As a practitioner of Zen Buddhism with training in contemplative arts, sensorimotor psychotherapy, narrative therapy, and trauma-informed approaches she offers psychotherapy, clinical supervision, and has taught at the Toronto Art Therapy Institute and the University of Toronto. Transformation by Fire: Women Overcoming Violence Through Clay, a 10-year retrospective at the Gardiner Museum facilitated by Suzanne, won the 2013 OMA Award of Excellence in Exhibitions. It is a direct reflection of Suzanne’s deep commitment to working collaboratively to address social justice issues through the arts.

title: Bee-ing a Pollinator Protector: Plan Now for a Buzzing Spring Garden
location: Riverdale
description:
Saving the bees is an environmental cause that resonates deeply with Canadians.  While most of us might not be thinking about bees this time of year, our actions during the colder months can still support these pollinators, particularly native bees, which are crucial and threatened by climate change, habitat loss, and other pressures.
In honour of the late bee scientist Sheila Colla, this presentation will offer practical tips on planting and maintaining gardens that provide beautifully blooming habitat for pollinators, with a particular focus on how native plants support wild bees.
Presented by
Lorraine Johnson
, who co-authored
A Garden for the Rusty-Patched Bumblebee
with Sheila Colla, as part of TPL's environmental program series,
Our Fragile Planet

title: Everyday Courage, Everyday Resilience: Finding your resilient flow in times of change and complexity
description:
Join us for an interactive discussion with Career Coach in Residence Sangeetha Dikshit and guest speaker, Abirambika Ravivarman. Resilience is more than bouncing back, it's our capacity to navigate change, uncertainty, and challenges with greater awareness, adaptability, and purpose. In this interactive session, participants will explore the concept of Resilient Flow and how our beliefs, habits, and ways of making sense of the world influence how we respond under pressure.
Sangeetha Dikshit
, one of TPL's four Career Coaches in Residence. Sangeetha is a Career and Leadership Coach empowering individuals to navigate career transitions, develop in-demand skills, and achieve professional success.
Abirambika Ravivarman
is a Human-Centric Leadership and Systems Coach and the founder of Human Systems at Work. Her work goes beyond individual behaviour to focus on the deeper relational dynamics that shape team performance and culture. In today’s AI-augmented workplace, she emphasizes the importance of strengthening the Human Edge—the presence-based and relational capabilities that enable leaders and teams to thrive in complexity.

In this workshop, participants will be guided by artist Farooq Zia through step-by-step instructions using drawing tools and watercolour paint to create their own geometric pattern and complex design art pieces.

title: National Housing Day: A Film Screening and Panel Discussion of Seeking Shelter
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall (1st floor)
description:
On November 24
th
, join Homeless Connect Toronto at the Toronto Reference Library for a special premiere screening and community conversation celebrating the launch of Seeking Shelter, a documentary series by filmmaker Nadine Valcin.
As Canada continues to grapple with a growing housing crisis, Seeking Shelter shines a light on the people, organizations, and grassroots movements creating innovative and inclusive solutions to housing instability. Through stories of resilience, collaboration, and community action, the series explores what becomes possible when people come together to reimagine housing.
This special event will feature premiere screenings of:
Episode 2: Communal Land for the Common Good :
Toronto’s Parkdale Neighbourhood Land Trust is sowing the seeds for innovative housing and communal growth.
And
Episode 3: Co-ops and the Power of Community:
Since the 1970s, a Toronto co-operative has modelled a collaborative and people-first approach to housing.
Following the screenings, filmmaker Nadine Valcin will moderate a panel discussion with housing subject-matter experts, exploring the themes raised in the films and the future of community-driven housing solutions. Audience members will also have an opportunity to participate in a Q&A and contribute reflections to a collaborative poll.
Doors open: 6pm
The episodes are provided courtesy of the National Film Board of Canada.

title: Your Health Matters: Breast Cancer Screening and Early Detection
description:
Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers affecting women, but early detection can significantly improve outcomes. Understanding your risk, knowing when to get screened, and recognizing potential warning signs are important steps in protecting your health.
What to Expect:
Understanding Breast Cancer:
Learn about breast cancer, who may be at risk, and ways to help reduce your risk.
Screening and Early Detection:
Understand who should be screened, why early detection matters, and what to expect during the screening process.
Recognizing Warning Signs:
Learn about potential signs and symptoms of breast cancer and the role of breast self-examination and assessment.
Accessing Care and Support:
Learn about the Ontario Breast Screening Program and resources available to support people living with breast cancer.
This session will be led by staff from LAMP Community Health Centre, who will provide practical information and guidance to help you better understand breast cancer screening and the resources available to support your health.
This program is presented by Toronto Public Library in collaboration with the West Toronto Ontario Health Team (OHT), a network of over 40 local health and social service providers working together to improve the health and well-being of communities in West Toronto.

title: ABCD Reads Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***Yesteryear*** by Caro Claire Burke.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/4849281772290048) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"A traditional American woman, a beautiful wife and mother who sells her pioneer lifestyle of raw milk and farm-fresh eggs to her millions of social media followers, suddenly awakens cold, filthy, and terrified in the brutal reality of 1855—where she must unravel whether this living nightmare is an elaborate hoax, a twisted reality show, or something far more sinister." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/yesteryear/))

"The chasm between social media and reality runs deep and dark in Caro Claire Burke’s debut novel, “Yesteryear,” which crawls into the psyche of a tradwife influencer so maddening and mesmerizing that Anne Hathaway has already signed on to play her in the movie adaptation.
“Sometimes it actually made me sick,” Natalie Heller Mills narrates, “how perfect my life was, and how good I was at living it.” Note her use of the past tense." (from [New York Times Book Review](https://archive.ph/WHSQ6#selection-753.0-764.0))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Jeff Chang: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents award-winning author Jeff Chang in conversation with Vinh Nguyen at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon, celebrating what would have been Bruce Lee's birthday.
More than half a century after his death, Bruce Lee remains as towering a figure as ever, the man who popularized martial arts in the West, became a bridge between Eastern and Western culture, and was poised to conquer Hollywood when he died suddenly at age thirty-two. But in the decades since, his legend has eclipsed the man. Forgotten is the immigrant, the fighter, the seeker, the teacher, the father grappling with exile and belonging in a country that questioned his right to simply exist.
In his epic new cultural biography
Water Mirror Echo: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
, acclaimed author Jeff Chang recovers the man behind the icon. Drawing on in-depth interviews with Lee's closest intimates, thousands of newly available personal documents, and dozens of rare photographs from the family archive, Chang traces Lee's remarkable journey: a charismatic child star turned delinquent teen fighter in Hong Kong, exiled alone to America, who transformed personal struggle into a philosophy of movement and being. Chang reveals how Lee's rise didn't just create a Hollywood legend, it helped birth something even more enduring: the very concept of Asian America.
Join Jeff Chang for a special evening honouring Bruce Lee's birthday, offering a stirringly human portrait of the icon, the immigrant, and the movement he unknowingly ignited.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

A small-town police chief conceals an explosive secret. A pair of ruthless drug dealers leave a bloody trail in their wake as they make their way from Los Angeles to Arkansas. title: Vibe Coding: Make Your Own Interactive Story with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if you could write a story where the reader chooses what happens, like a branching adventure, a mystery, or a game, and have AI build it with you?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll learn "vibe-coding": using an AI coding assistant to build your own interactive story or simple game. You'll design the branches, describe the rules in plain language, test for the tricky edge cases (what if the player picks the weird option?), and end up with a single file you can share with anyone. Just a story you want to tell. This is the playful sibling of the practical vibe-coding workshop.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

description: Inside the mind of the human pet... and how to play with it! US / International Attendees: This event is priced in CAD. At checkout, you will see the CAD price, but your bank will automatically convert it to your local currency. See tickets for estimated USD conversions! You may be surprised to learn how much of pet play and headspace can be explained by surprisingly common psychological concepts that fit into your daily life (or the daily lives of your average vanilla friend). His past research, as well as several ongoing research projects also revolve around pet play experiences, headspace, and different roles within pet play communities. title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Disruptors & Dilemmas — Surviving the smoke: The new reality of wildfires
location: Online
description:
Register now!   
Wildfires are no longer distant events unfolding deep in remote forests. As fires grow more frequent and intense, their impacts are increasingly felt in our cities, communities and the air we breathe. How do wildfires reshape the future of our forests, cities and climate? 
Join University of Toronto experts for an engaging discussion on the science, technology and human realities of wildfires. Explore how robotics and aerial monitoring are changing the way fires are tracked, why wildfire smoke poses growing challenges for urban centres and how communities can adapt in a world where fire is both a natural part of the landscape and an escalating public concern. 
From public health and environmental justice to urban planning and climate resilience, discover how the decisions we make today will shape our ability to live with fire tomorrow. 
This is a Disruptors and Dilemmas speaker series event.This event is co-hosted by: University of Toronto Faculty of Applied Science and Engineering, Temerty Faculty of Medicine and University of Toronto Mississauga.

title: Recovery College- Balance & Build Week 6: Managing Academic Stress & Exam Anxiety
description:
All it takes is one below average or even just average mark to get inside your head and begin doubting yourself and your ability to succeed in your program. title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

Learn about government benefits, tax credits, and strategies to help protect your retirement income. Presented by John Stapleton from Open Policy Ontario.

Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.

title: Coding with Python II
location: Cliffcrest, Meeting Room
description:
Python is an open source programming language that is used for creating web applications, web content, mathematics and system scripting. In this second Python session we will leverage everything we learned about loops and blocks in part one to create our very own functions. We'll take a look at how to approach function design, how to allow users to enter data into functions through arguments, and how to get our functions to return results. We will also introduce some new data structures which, unlike variables, can hold more than one piece of data at a time.
This class is for beginners but assumes you have a basic understanding of Python or have attended Coding with Python I.
Registration will start 2 weeks before this class. Computers will be provided.

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.

title: Alderwood Book Club: Clara at the Door With a Revolver
location: Alderwood
description:
In November we will be discussing the non-fiction book
Clara at the Door With a Revolver
by Carolyn Whitzman.
“In the autumnal darkness of October 6, 1894, an unseen figure rang the doorbell at the Parkdale home of a well-to-do Toronto family and then shot eighteen-year-old Frank Westwood in his doorway, murdering him in cold blood.
Six weeks later, Clara Ford, a Black tailor and single mother, was arrested. Known for her impeccable work ethic and her resolute personality - and for her predilection for wearing men’s attire – she confessed to the murder.
But as the details of her arrest and her complex connection to the Westwood family emerged, Clara recanted, testifying that she had been coerced by police into a false confession.”

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:

Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions

title: Journée pédagogique: Explorum - Bombes à bain
location: S. Walter Stewart, Auditorium
description:
L’expérience des bombes à bain est une expérience simple qui illustre une des réactions chimiques les plus communes : la neutralisation acidobasique qui forme un sel et de l'eau. Cette activité relaxante permet aux enfants de faire leur propre bombe à bain et de comprendre que cette réaction produit du gaz (des bulles) ; ils apprennent que l’acide contient du cations H+ et que la base contient des anions OH- qui réagissent ensemble pour former du sel et de l'eau. Chaque participant combine ses ingrédients et confectionne sa propre bombe à bain qu’il emporte avec lui emballée dans un petit sac en cellophane.
The bath bomb experience is a simple activity that illustrates one of the most common chemical reactions: acid-base neutralization, which forms a salt and water. This relaxing activity allows children to create their own bath bomb and understand that this reaction produces gas (bubbles). They learn that the acid contains H+ ions and the base contains OH- ions, which react together to form salt and water. Each participant combines their ingredients and crafts their own bath bomb to take home, packaged in a small cellophane bag.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

title: Robotics Institute Seminar: Steven Waslander, “TankerVision: Turning Firefighting Flights into a Wildfire Behaviour Dataset”
location: Bahen Centre for Information Technology, Room 1190, or on Zoom, 40 St George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5S 2E4, Canada
description:
Join in-person (BA1190) or online (Zoom) 
TankerVision: Turning Firefighting Flights into a Wildfire Behaviour Dataset
Abstract
Models of wildfire rate of spread, intensity and spotting still rely mostly on small experimental burns from decades ago. Fires are hardest to observe exactly when it matters most, during rapid, intense spread. Satellites are too coarse in space and time, and drones and research aircraft are kept out of fire airspace. The only platforms reliably overhead during a major run are the aircraft fighting the fire. 
TankerVision turns these operational flights into a continuous, automated source of fire behaviour data. Working with Conair Aerial Firefighting, the BC Wildfire Service and Alberta Wildfire, we developed a self-contained imaging unit for the bird-dog aircraft that direct airtanker operations. It records georeferenced colour and thermal infrared imagery whenever the aircraft is near a fire, with no action required from the crew. A prototype flew roughly 50 missions over 30 fires from Kamloops in 2025. 
With support from DRDC and NRCan, three upgraded aircraft flew fires across five provinces and territories in 2026. An automated pipeline segments fire and smoke, reconstructs georeferenced 3D fire fronts and derives rate-of-spread observations from successive passes. The result is the first large multi-pass, multi-fire dataset of active wildfire behaviour, a foundation for data-driven fire prediction models, with an initial public release planned for December 2026. 
About Steven Waslander
Prof. Steven Waslander is a leading authority on autonomous vehicles, including multirotor drones and autonomous driving vehicles.  He received his B.Sc.E.in 1998 from Queen’s University, his M.S. in 2002 and his Ph.D. in 2007, both from Stanford University in Aeronautics and Astronautics, where as a graduate student he created the Stanford Testbed of Autonomous Rotorcraft for Multi-Agent Control (STARMAC), the world’s most capable outdoor multi-vehicle quadrotor platform at the time. He was recruited to Waterloo from Stanford in 2008, where he founded and directed the Waterloo Autonomous Vehicle Laboratory (WAVELab), extending the state of the art in autonomous drones and autonomous driving through advances in localization and mapping, object detection and tracking, integrated planning and control methods and multi-robot coordination. His work on autonomous vehicles has resulted in the Autonomoose, the first autonomous vehicle created at a Canadian University to drive on public roads. In 2018, he joined the University of Toronto Institute for Aerospace Studies (UTIAS), and founded the Toronto Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (TRAILab). Starting in July of 2026, he became the director of the University of Toronto Robotics Institute. 
Join in-person (BA1190) or online (Zoom)

title: The Myth of “Samshu”: Smell, Race, and the Making of Chinatown in North America, 1880s–1920s
location: North York Central Library, Room 101
description:
What did Chinatown smell like to outsiders a century ago? How could an unfamiliar distilled drink
become a symbol of racial and cultural difference? Between the 1880s and the 1920s, Chinese
immigrant communities in North America encountered growing scrutiny of their businesses,
customs, and everyday lives. Among the objects attracting attention was “samshu,” a term found in
English-language descriptions of Chinese distilled spirits. Its reputation became entangled with
accounts of Chinatown, unfamiliar odours, drinking practices, illicit alcohol, and anxieties about
immigration.
This lecture investigates how descriptions of samshu circulated within the cultural imagination of
North American society. Moving among sensory impressions, racialized representations, and the
history of bootlegging and alcohol regulation, it asks how ordinary experiences of smell and taste
could become markers of inclusion and exclusion. The lecture also asks audiences to distinguish
claims made about Chinese communities from the more complicated realities of their lives. In doing
so, it explores how historical encounters produce durable ideas about “us” and “them.”
Presenter: Dr. Jackson Yue Bin Guo | Sessional Lecturer II, Global Asia Studies / History,
University of Toronto Scarborough | Founder, Aprilum Lyceum
Jackson Yue Bin Guo received his Ph.D. in History from the University of Toronto in 2023. He
researches food and drink, law, sensory experience, material culture, and everyday life in late
imperial and modern China. His current book manuscript, Governing Intoxication: Alcohol and the
Convergence of Sensory Life in Late Imperial and Modern China, explores the social, cultural, and
regulatory histories of distilled alcohol. His scholarship has appeared in Global Food History and
the Asian Journal of Law and Society. He is the founder of Aprilum Lyceum.
No registration required.

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

When Kai nearly injures himself during a bench press, Tyler steps in and offers to be his spotter. The two men form an unlikely connection that sparks conversations about body image, modern dating, and the way gay men see each other.

title: Holiday Succulent Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us this holiday season and create a one-of-a-kind succulent!
Celebrate the festive season with a delightful holiday-inspired succulent arranging workshop! In this creative and relaxing session, you’ll design a beautiful succulent arrangement in a charming birch-lined tin planter—perfect for adding a touch of natural elegance to your holiday décor or gifting to someone special.
 
Guided by a succulent expert, you’ll learn tips and tricks for arranging succulents with a seasonal flair, including techniques for layering textures, balancing colours, and incorporating winter-inspired accents.
 
All materials are provided, including a birch-lined tin planter, premium succulents, specialty soil, and care instruction cards to ensure your arrangement stays vibrant through the holiday season and beyond.
 
Join us for this festive workshop and leave with a stunning centrepiece that captures the warmth and beauty of the holidays!
 
Saturday, November 28, 10 to 11 a.m.
Public $55, TBG Members $50 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Canadian Succulents
Molly is the owner and operator of the small business Canadian Succulents. Canadian Succulents creates floral arrangements using entirely succulents and cacti plants. They not only arrange and design all of the creations, but also grow all the plants that can be found in them as well. They operate out of a greenhouse just northeast of the city, where they grow over 300 varieties of succulents and cacti. They grow and create these designs for wedding centrepieces and favours, corporate events and gifting, and hotel and office greenery.

title: Pressed Flower Candle Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a morning of hands-on pressed flower candle making!
Discover the simple, satisfying craft of flower pressing and transform a plain pillar candle into a one-of-a-kind keepsake. Using warm palette knives to gently melt pressed flowers directly into the wax, you’ll learn a technique that’s part botanical art, part patience. Choose from a variety of pressed flowers to design your own arrangement. Beginners welcome.
 
Each attendee will receive one 6″ white pillar candle, a full selection of pressed flowers to choose from, and step-by-step guidance on using heated palette knives safely to melt your design into the wax.
 
Saturday, November 28, 10 to 11:30 a.m.
Public $65, TBG Members $60 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Epiphanie Belanger
Epiphanie Belanger is the founder of HobbyHub, a community-driven platform designed to help people try new hobbies in a relaxed environment. What started as a personal curiosity for creative pursuits quickly turned into a mission to make hobbies more accessible, social, and fun for beginners.
 
Through curated workshops and experiences, Epiphanie brings people together to explore hands-on creative skills in a welcoming, low-pressure environment. Epiphanie is passionate about helping people rediscover play, slow down, and connect (both with their creativity and with others) one hobby at a time.

title: Christmas in Old York! 1833 (RETURN FOR 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

**If you plan on attending, please get your tickets for this event early as this tour has run for the last 3 years, and does sell out rather quickly.**

So what was it like in York in 1833 at Christmas time?

The prices of various food items and gifts on display, the gas lights creating a glow as the snow begins, places to gather, places to get a drink, like the Steamboat Hotel on Front Street, or maybe one might decide to take their best girl or guy on a stagecoach trip to High Park to watch kids speed down the hills on their skids.

What were the traditions in old York? Maybe the residents went down to the lake and watched the nighttime fishermen spear fish for Christmas dinner. Let's take a trip around old York and see what it was like back in 1833, three months before we changed our name to Toronto in 1834.

Or take a holiday trip to Kingston or Montreal to buy gifts directly from New York or London stores, fancy hats for the ladies and cigars for the men. Books and wooden toys for the kids. What about that goose in the little grocery store on King Street West of Jarvis? Candies from Britain, real home made gingerbread in the store windows.

On Christmas Eve everyone walked to St. James Cathedral for the ringing of the bells, singing, and skating over the frozen Toronto Bay to the Peninsula.

This tour explores old York. This walking tour is for all walking levels. The tour begins and ends at St. James Cathedral on King Street East at Church Street. A great way to kick off the season.

This tour has a ticketed price of $15.00.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Painting Botanical Cast Ornaments from Garden Blooms
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Learn how to create your own plant-based pigments and paint one-of-a-kind botanical cast ornaments!
Want to give a holiday gift that is not mass produced in a factory? Looking for a calming experience that beats the hustle and bustle? Join botanical artist Rebecca Fortin for an afternoon of natural paint-making and ornament painting.
 
Under Rebecca’s guidance, you’ll explore how to create colour pigments from local botanicals, such as goldenrod, nettle, berries, and more.
 
Test your plant-based pigments on watercolour paper, including creating a holiday card. Participants will choose two plaster miniature botanical casts to paint and take home or gift for the holiday season. These ornaments are created by Rebecca, each made using impressions of live botanicals. This workshop features botanical casts made with flowers directly from Toronto Botanical Garden, capturing the garden’s beauty in artwork that lasts long after the blossoms fade.
 
All materials will be provided. No prior experience required.
 
This workshop is intended for ages 16+. Mature youth aged 12+ are welcome, but must be accompanied and supervised by an adult.
 
Please note: Please wear practical clothes and footwear that you don’t mind getting a little messy. As with all handmade processes using real plants: results will vary, pigments may shift in colour over time, and each piece will have perfect imperfections that contribute to its unique character.
 
Saturday, November 28, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $115, TBG Members $110 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Rebecca Fortin
Rebecca Fortin is a visual artist based in rural Whitby, Ontario, where she creates botanical artwork rooted in the textures, colours, and quiet beauty of the plants around her. After a 20-year career in public health administration, Rebecca pivoted to focus on her art practice, completing the Drawing and Painting program at the Haliburton School of Art + Design in 2022. She now works full-time as an artist, bringing together her background in community health promotion with her passion for connecting people to nature through art.
 
Rebecca’s work has been shown across Ontario and is held in private and corporate collections in Canada and internationally. Her hands-on workshops invite participants to explore botanicals and natural art materials — offering memorable, calming experiences and the opportunity to create beautiful, one-of-a-kind pieces to take home.
 
Follow Rebecca on Instagram.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Lost Libraries of the Ancient World (LECTURES - 5TH ANNIVERSARY 2ND DATE)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

**A second date has been added as there are 9 on the waitlist for the Saturday October 24 lecture! If you are planning to take in this lecture, get your spots early. See you then!**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2026/2027. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join me, and uncover the world and keep active, warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life. The first Lecture on the Go was **Walking North America** and that was in October of 2021. Hard to believe it's been 5 years of lectures. So I wanted to do something special to celebrate 5 years of exploration.

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

Let's get started.

What if some of humanity's greatest discoveries were made thousands of years ago, and then lost forever?

What if entire histories, scientific breakthroughs, literary masterpieces, and eyewitness accounts of the ancient world once existed, only to disappear into the flames of war, and the collapse of civilizations?

Join me for a fascinating journey into the world's lost libraries, from the legendary Library of Alexandria to the vanished collections of ancient empires whose treasures may be lost forever.

At the heart, stands the Library of Alexandria, the most famous library in history. Founded over two thousand years ago, it sought to gather all the knowledge of the known world. Scholars from across the Mediterranean came to study astronomy, mathematics, geography, medicine, philosophy, and literature. Yet one of history's greatest mysteries remains: what happened to this remarkable institution, and what priceless knowledge disappeared with it?

Was it destroyed in a single catastrophe, or did it slowly fade away over centuries from neglect?

Beyond Alexandria, we will explore a forgotten world of lost libraries and vanished collections stretching from Mesopotamia and ancient Egypt to medieval Europe, Baghdad, and China. Discover the remarkable stories of librarians, scholars, explorers, and rulers who dedicated their lives to preserving knowledge.

We will encounter lost books, missing histories, ancient scientific works, and literary treasures that survive today only as fragments.
This lecture is an exploration of one of history's most compelling questions: What have we forgotten?

And how libraries shaped civilization and why their loss continues to fascinate us centuries later. Whether you are a lover of history, literature, archaeology, or simply enjoy a good mystery, this special Lecture on the Go will leave you wondering. What secrets of the past may still lie hidden, just waiting to be rediscovered? Fascinating indeed!

Upcoming topics in the 2026 series:

\*Philosophy 1: Great Minds of the Western World: Goethe to Kant! - (2027)
\*Philosophy 2: Great Minds of the Eastern
World: Chuang Tzu to Dalai Lama - (2027)
Legacy of Triangle: How a New York Factory Scandal changed North America - (September 2027)

So book your plans now!

This event is for all levels and walkers, there are a few steps here and there to navigate, but mostly on one level. This event in a non-walking event.

The lecture begins on the steps of Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Bay Street and Queen Street West, and
has a ticket price of $20.00 per person, but **free with the yearly membership pass**.

**Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events

Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:
Once you enter the "Waiting-list", we will message you for the payment via e-transfer. After your payment is confirmed, you will be moved to the "Going-list"

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

description:
OCAD University Senate Meeting

The next regular meeting of the OCAD University Senate is scheduled to take place on Monday, November 30, 2026 from 3:15 pm – 5:30 pm EDT. The Senate is responsible for the establishment and regulation of academic policy, standards and procedures at OCAD University. The Senate and its many committees are in charge of all matters pertaining to OCAD U academic resources, academic programming, academic strategic planning, student affairs and any other such matters relating to academic issues. More information can be found on the OCAD U Senate webpage . If you would like to attend as a guest, or if you have any questions, please contact David Wagschal, Quality Assurance Officer & Associate Senate Secretary at dwagschal@ocadu.ca . Please note: Requests to attend public meetings must be made at least one business day in advance of the meeting .

title: Python Essentials 1 Learning Circle
location: Brookbanks, Lower Level Auditorium
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact
networkingacademy@tpl.ca

title: AI for Small Business and Entrepreneurs
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
You've got the business idea. Now come the thousand questions: who's my customer, what's the market, how do I pitch this?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll use AI as a research and planning partner for small business. We'll practice together on a sample business, turning rough ideas into business plans, digging into markets, drafting customer-discovery questions, and building useful low-maintenance automation. The most valuable thing you'll get is usually a better question to be tested in the real world. Whether you're starting or growing, you'll leave with an experiment you can run on your own business this week.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.

“The truth is that we are one body moving through time together.” — Richard Wagamese 
Are you centered? Open to the energy of joy? Open to moving as one? 
We are all connected. Our DNA remembers this connection through clay. In our cells, we hold the memory of all creation. Guided by a Zen Buddhist practitioner and registered art therapist, explore simple physical practices with clay designed to bring you into the moment while deepening and expanding awareness that we are all connected. 
At the end of the workshop we return the clay to its original form, letting go of what was created and ready to begin anew. 
This workshop welcomes everyone, whether you are new to or familiar with clay, breath, and presence.

                    Suzanne Thomson, Zen Buddhist practitioner and registered art therapist
                    
                
                
                    Suzanne Thomson is ceramic artist, registered psychotherapist, and art therapist with over 30 years of experience integrating these practices to facilitate healing, community building and social transformation work. As a practitioner of Zen Buddhism with training in contemplative arts, sensorimotor psychotherapy, narrative therapy, and trauma-informed approaches she offers psychotherapy, clinical supervision, and has taught at the Toronto Art Therapy Institute and the University of Toronto. Transformation by Fire: Women Overcoming Violence Through Clay, a 10-year retrospective at the Gardiner Museum facilitated by Suzanne, won the 2013 OMA Award of Excellence in Exhibitions. It is a direct reflection of Suzanne’s deep commitment to working collaboratively to address social justice issues through the arts.

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

location: Online Zoom Webinar @ Online Zoom Webinar
description:
The Faculty of Graduate Studies is hosting a session entitled From Research to Real-World Impact: An Introduction to Knowledge Mobilization for Graduate Student Scholars. Join us!
Research creates knowledge, but impact happens when knowledge is shared, understood, and used. This interactive session introduces graduate students to the fundamentals of Knowledge Mobilization (KMb) and explores how to move research beyond traditional academic audiences. Topics will include how to identify key audiences, develop effective knowledge-sharing strategies, build meaningful partnerships, and communicate research in ways that support social, community, policy, and professional impact. Whether you are just beginning your research journey or preparing for future careers inside or outside academia, this session will provide practical tools to help amplify the reach and relevance of your work.

title: Access to Housing
location: Albert Campbell, Learning Centre on the Second Floor
description:
Are you looking for subsidized housing in Toronto?
This session will cover:
- An overview of the RGI application process
- Eligibility requirements
- Steps for submitting and updating applications
- Information on priority access
- The choice-based cycle housing offer process and the Single Offer Rule
- Financial assistance programs to help the tenants/home owners

Presented by The Housing Help Centre (THHC), a registered non-profit agency whose mandate is to help people access and maintain affordable and safe market rent accommodation.
Please arrive a few minutes early.

title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
location: Palmerston, Meeting Room
description:
Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space!
A
learning circle
is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment.
Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field.
In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to:
transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel
query data from a relational database using SQL
improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau
We will meet weekly,
in-person,
every Tuesday afternoon, September 15 - December 8, 2-3:30 PM (12 sessions).
Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis.
Learners who complete the course will be able to:
earn a digital badge
download a certificate of completion

title: Python Essentials 1 and 2 Learning Circle
location: York Woods
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Learners who successfully complete both courses will earn a digital badge and certificate of completion.
Python Essentials 1
is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. The course covers essential programming topics such as data types, variables, control flow, functions, and exceptions.
Python Essentials 2
is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming, including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing and object-oriented programming (OOP).

title: After School Club: Make a Kaleidoscope with Explorum
description:
What is a kaleidoscope? An optical illusion? Magic? Art? In fact, it's a bit of all that. It's an instrument developed over 200 years ago that uses the reflection of light on mirrors to create enchanting repetitive patterns. In this workshop, children will make their own kaleidoscope and are introduced to the terms reflection and refraction of light while being captivated by the physics of the shimmering patterns on reflective surfaces.
Recommended materials:
paper (thick card stock), scissors, aluminum foil, markers, glue stick, BBQ skewer, tape, (optional: sparkles)
Zoom URL to access the online program will be emailed to registrants ahead of program date.
This online program is suitable for children ages 6-12. Younger children may require assistance from caregivers. It is recommended that parents or caregivers are present during this live program. Questions about online programs? Please email us at programproposals@tpl.ca.

title: Run Your One-Person Business with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
When you're the whole company, the admin never ends: emails, scheduling, proposals, follow-ups. What if you could design a system to handle the busywork?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll learn to design an administrative system for a one-person business with AI as your assistant: intake pipelines, email drafting, client communication, and scheduling. Learn to map work into four piles: what's rules-based, what AI drafts, what needs your judgment, and what should never be automated. You'll build reusable templates and leave with a clearer plan for how AI could help your business.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.
About the AI Tools Used in This Program
This program includes activities that use agentic AI tools (listed below) on library laptops.
You do not need to create your own account for this program.
Participants are encouraged to follow the Resident’s guidance throughout sessions, which include best practices on using AI.

title: A Short History of Library Architecture in Toronto and Beyond
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, 1st floor
description:
Christopher Hume, the architecture critic and urban issues columnist of the Toronto Star, presents a short history of library architecture. He will be commenting on the structures and social relevance of monumental libraries from Paris, Boston, New York, with a focus on Toronto Public Libraries from around the city.
Hume is the recipient of 2009 The National Newspaper Award for journalism in architecture and urban affairs. His illustrious career at the Toronto Star earned him a President’s Award for Architectural Journalism from the Royal Architectural Institute of Canada. Hume's book, William James’ Toronto Views, won a Toronto Heritage Award in 2000 and in 2004 he received a Landscape Ontario award.

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Tiny Titans: Insects Up Close | Book Launch & Panel Talk with Author & Photographer Dara Ojo
location: North York Central Library, Room 101 - 1st floor
description:
Discover the hidden world of arthropods through stunning macro photography — a visual journey celebrating their beauty, complexity, and essential role in our ecosystems.
Meet
Dara Ojo
, an award-winning macro photographer and conservation storyteller whose work brings the hidden world of arthropods into vivid relief. Ojo's book,
Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem
reveals the fascinating lives of insects, spiders, and other small creatures that quietly sustain life on Earth. Captured across Canada, Mexico, Costa Rica, and beyond, Dara Ojo’s photography highlights the intricate details and diversity of these often-overlooked species.
Ojo will be leading the conversation with:
Antonia Guidotti
,
a Collections Technician with a focus on Insects & Arachnids at the Royal Ontario Museum.
Lorraine Johnson
, author and native plant and ecological gardening advocate, bridging the connection between insects, plants, habitat and practical conservation action.
Dr. Sandra Rehan
, professor at York University and principal investigator of the Rehan Lab with a focus on wild bees, pollinator biology and conservation. Rehan's research explores the biology, behaviour and evolution of bees, with a particular interest in understanding and protecting native pollinators.
Dr. Laura Timms
, Senior Specialist of Natural Heritage Management at Credit Valley Conservation and Adjunct Professor with the Daniels Faculty’s Institute of Forestry and Conservation.
Join in this evening to celebrate macro photography and the intricate beauty and ecological importance of insects and spiders, creatures that quietly anchor global biodiversity, pollination, and climate resilience.
Free program. Register for a reminder.
***Doors open at 5:30 pm. At 6:00 pm, seating becomes first-come, first-served until capacity is reached.***
5:30 pm:
Doors open. Mingle and chat with fellow nature and environmental enthusiasts!
6:00 pm:
Presentation begins. Enjoy a highly visual presentation combining photography, science, conservation and storytelling, taking the audience behind the scenes of six years documenting tiny worlds across five continents and exploring why these overlooked species matter. A light, informal conversation with guest speakers will explore why arthropods are so essential to our ecosystems, with a discussion of challenges impacting local species, and how science, photography and art can work together to help people notice, understand and care about the natural world. An audience Q&A follows this discussion.
7:30 pm:
Book signing with books available for purchase.
***
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​
Questions? Please contact North York Central Library - Business, Science & Technology Department.
***
Place a hold or borrow from Toronto Public Library:
Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem
(book) - Dara Ojo
A Garden for the Rusty-patched Bumblebee
(book) - Lorraine Johnson

description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.
