The Dining Room : Exploring the Design of Twelve Iconic Rooms in Search of the Perfect Dining Experience.​
​(Random House, 2026).
Explore the stories behind twelve iconic dining rooms in homes around the world—from a Japanese samurai house to Claude Monet's brilliant yellow dining room to Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul to Jackie Kennedy’s White House—and travel through time in pursuit of the ultimate design.​
The Dining Room is an englightening and joyous celebration of history, culture and the art of dning. Presenter John Ota's charming observations of the surprising impact of dining rooms on our lives and the cherised moments we share within them will delight armchair travellers, history fanatics and interior design enthusiasts alike.

Develop and exercise the skills you need to be an active participant in everyday democracy in this fun, interactive session. Democracy Fitness expands traditional ideas of what democracy is by exploring how people participate in civic life, build understanding and work together.

title: Learning Things You Love with AI
location: North York Central Library, eLearning Lab
description:
Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. A tutor explains things in the way you understand, asks you questions, and helps you choose what to learn next. Learn how to turn your goal into a specific, doable learning experiment: options not answers, with a practice that survives a bad day. Decide ahead of time how you'll know it's working: revise, or stop without guilt. You'll leave with a plan you actually want to try, and a sense for what AI should never decide for you.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Art of Darkness: Edgar Allan Poe's Life & Work
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Professor Emily Ogden shares her intimate inquiry into the shadowy life and compelling work of the definitive author of the macabre.
Since Edgar Allan Poe’s mysterious death in 1849, his stories and poems have captivated millions of readers around the world. Nearly two centuries later, why do we continue to descend into the darkness of his imagination—and of the genres, from horror to crime, that he pioneered?
In Darkness Becomes Bright, Ogden plumbs the darkness within Poe and enters it alongside him. She interweaves stories from his mysterious and tragic life with those of his most famous readers and translators, showing us how Poe’s vision echoes across the generations, allowing us to make peace with our own flawed humanity.
Emily Ogden speaks with author and critic Naben Ruthnum about the brief life and immortal art of Edgar Allan Poe.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Vietnam & Cambodia with Angkor Wat! Ancient Kingdoms of Southeast Asia!!
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
A Meetup trip in December . . . what can be a better gift for the holidays?! Join our travelers group on a captivating 14-day journey through the heart of Southeast Asia as we explore the vibrant cultures and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam & Cambodia (Dec 04-18, 2026)

As with all our tailor-made Meetup trips, our expert guides will lead us off the beaten path to uncover the authentic charm of each destination, while comfortable accommodations and delicious local cuisine ensure a truly immersive travel experience. Embark on an unforgettable journey through the vibrant cities and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam, finishing with the wonders of Cambodia.

We begin in Hanoi, where history and culture come alive, then sail the emerald waters of Halong Bay. Step back in time among the imperial treasures of Hue, wander the lantern-lit streets of charming Hoi An, and feel the dynamic energy of Ho Chi Minh City. We conclude your adventure at the awe-inspiring temples of Siem Reap, home to the legendary Angkor Wat.

TRIP HIGHLIGHTS:

* **Hanoi**; explore Ho Chi Minh sites, Temple of Literature, Old Quarter cyclo ride & water puppet show
* Visit rural **craft villages**: conical hat & incense making, home-hosted lunch, village walk
* **Ha Long Bay cruise**: limestone islands, floating villages, cave visit, Tai Chi & sunset views
* **Hue**: Perfume River boat ride, Thien Mu Pagoda, Khai Dinh’s Tomb & Imperial Citadel
* Scenic **Hai Van Pass train** to Danang; explore Dragon Bridge, Cham Museum, Marble Mountain

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

GTA Hiking & Stuff
**\*\*\*\*\*\* Christmas Edition \*\*\*\*\*\***
Wear your Santa Hat!

Make sure you join us for this special Christmas & Santa Hat hike as we celebrate the season and winter hiking. We have a few other things you can take part in:

This year we are supporting SOCKs once again. You can bring cash or feel free to e-transfer $ to [ralfraser@gmail.com](ralfraser@gmail.com). Be sure to let me know you're sending me $.

title: THE LIFE AND TIMES OF JANE FRANKLIN  (LECTURES)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

**Toronto History Walks is currently working on bringing Lectures on the Go to a permanent home for 2027. I will continue to update this site for information as to the venue. But for now we will still meet on the steps of Old City Hall until further notice.**

**This is the last Lecture on the Go for 2026!**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2027. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join us and learn about the world and keep active and warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life.

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

Jane Franklin was a prominent 19th-century British woman known for her remarkable energy, and influence, in exploration and colonial affairs during the Victorian era.

She is best remembered as the wife of John Franklin, the Royal Navy officer who led the ill-fated Franklin Expedition. After her husband disappeared in the Arctic in 1847, Jane Franklin became one of the most determined figures in the search for him. She funded expeditions, and lobbied the British government. She mobilized public attention for decades in an effort to uncover his fate and learn the truth.

But she wasn’t only defined by that search. Jane Franklin was also a widely travelled and intellectually curious woman who visited places like Tasmania (then Van Diemen’s Land), Greece, the Middle East, and Russia.

She also supported education, and science, often working behind the scenes to influence institutions like the Royal Geographical Society. You could say she became a kind of unofficial power broker in British exploration.

In this lecture, we’ll explore the life and times of Jane Franklin. in the new biography series of timely women and men who made the world.

Upcoming topics in the 2027 series:

\*Philosophy 1: Great Minds of the Western World: Goethe to Kant! - (January 2027)
\*Philosophy 2: Great Minds of the Eastern
World: Chuang Tzu to Dalai Lama - (January 2027)
Legacy of Triangle: How a New York Factory Scandal changed North America - (February 2027)
The History of Masculinity from the Industrial Revolution to the 21st Century! (March 2027)

**So book your plans now!**

This event is for all levels and walkers, there are a few steps here and there to navigate, but mostly on one level. This event in a non-walking event.

title: AI for Us: Shaping AI in Toronto
location: North York Central Library, Room 2/3
description:
Toronto is one of the biggest AI cities in the world. But what do the people here actually think about it and how do we want to shape its development and use?
A panel of experts, alongside our Innovator-in-Residence
Ryan Kelln
, who know AI from very different angles, unite for an open conversation about what AI is doing to this city, and what we want it to do instead. We'll talk about:
The human beings behind the machines: what drives the people who build AI, and what worries them.
Work, money, and meaning: what happens to jobs, creativity, and value when AI lands here.
Who gets to shape it and who's left out (both are our neighbours).
The stories we tell: how art, media, news, and everyday talk shape what we expect, fear, and hope for.
No pitches, no boosterism. Just an honest conversation about the ideas and stories shaping AI in this city, and what we want it to become.
Featuring:
Jerrold McGrath
, Cultural Programmer and Theorist, In the Meantime
Joseph Wilson
, Anthropologist & Author of Humans of AI: Understanding the Humans Behind the Machines
Owais Lightwala

Chrysalis

About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling, which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.

I will try to answer tantalizing questions about its nature, and how it may have helped shape the Universe.

title: Landmarks 6: Gladstone Hotel to The Edgewater Hotel Via Gutta Percha
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Toronto is a city that hides its history in plain sight. Beneath the glass towers are layers of stories — grand hotels that vanished overnight, political scandals whispered through stone corridors, theatres that once glittered under gaslight, and laneways where the city first learned how to become a metropolis.

This new Toronto History Walks tour invites the walker to slow down, and see the city differently.

Let's return to a bygone era: late 1930s. Parkdale would already have had a long fascinating history behind it, but you would also be looking at a neighbourhood that was changing with the times. One of the most interesting examples was the Edgewater Hotel, built in 1939 at 14 Roncesvalles Avenue, at The Queensway.

It was built by Fred Hammer and became part of a very busy transportation hub, sitting beside the Sunnyside Bus Terminal. The building has survived, although the Edgewater name eventually disappeared and the hotel went through several incarnations. It is a wonderful reminder that Parkdale's history isn't just Victorian, there is twentieth-century history here as well.

And then we come to the Gladstone Hotel, which is one of those buildings that almost seem to have been watching the neighbourhood change. The hotel we see today dates from 1889 and was designed by Toronto architect George Martell Miller in the Richardsonian Romanesque style. Its location was absolutely perfect for business: it stood across from the Parkdale railway station, and was close to the Exhibition grounds. Travelling salesmen, railway workers, visitors to the CNE and commercial travellers could all find shelter here.

The original owner was Susanna Robinson, who was left a widow with thirteen children before construction of the hotel was completed.
The Gladstone tells us something important about Parkdale itself. For decades it was a working-class gathering place, and as the factories and industries changed, so did the fortunes of the hotel. The great tower once had a cupola that could be seen from a distance, but that disappeared in the 1940s. By the later twentieth century the hotel had fallen on hard times and had developed a much different reputation. Yet it never completely lost its role as a community gathering place.

Eventually it was restored and reinvented, becoming part of the artistic and cultural life of Queen Street West.

And finally, we get to one of the great industrial stories of old Parkdale — the Gutta Percha & Rubber Manufacturing Company. Established here in 1883 on West Lodge Avenue, the factory became one of the largest employers in the neighbourhood and, at its height, the largest rubber manufacturer in Canada. They made all sorts of rubber products — hose, belting, boots, footwear, mats and eventually products connected with the rapidly growing automobile industry.

The factory operated until 1960, when changing technology, synthetic rubber and competition finally brought its long Parkdale story to an end. Three places — the Edgewater, the Gladstone and Gutta Percha — give us three very different Parkdales: the Parkdale of travel and transportation, the Parkdale of hotels and community life, and the Parkdale of factories and working people. Put them together and you begin to see just how fascinating this neighbourhood really is.

This walking tour begins at The Gladstone Hotel at the northeast corner of Queen Street West and Gladstone Avenue, one block east of Dufferin Street. We end at the corner of Queen Street West and Roncesvalles Avenue.

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Christmas in Old Toronto! 1855 - The Railway Era (NEW FOR 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

**So what was it like in Toronto in 1855 at Christmas time? This tour is different from the first part - Christmas in 1833 York. If you can, try and take both tours, and compare the differences in 22 years of history! Toronto changed significantly between those years.**

Imagine spending Christmas in Toronto in 1855, when the city was still a relatively young place and the streets were a far cry from the Toronto we know today. There would be no electric Christmas lights, no department-store displays, no traffic jams of cars on the DVP. Instead, Toronto was a city of horse-drawn wagons, muddy streets, wood fires, gas lamps, small shops and busy markets. And the railways were on the way to Toronto.

Christmas was becoming increasingly popular as a family celebration, influenced by traditions coming from Britain, Ireland, Europe and the United States. For many, Christmas Day meant attending church, visiting relatives and friends, enjoying a special meal and taking a welcome break from everyday life, even if just for a day.

For children, Christmas could be magical, but it was a much simpler Christmas. Toys were homemade or relatively inexpensive, and a child's Christmas might include a wooden toy, a doll, some sweets, an orange, nuts or perhaps a book. There were no shopping malls or endless advertisements telling people what they needed to buy.

Toronto's shops and markets would nevertheless have been busy in the days before Christmas. The smell of roasting meat, baked goods, spices and coal fires would have filled the air, while church bells and carriages would have been part of the Christmas landscape. And for those who were poor, Christmas could be a very different experience, making charitable giving and church relief particularly important.

But perhaps the most fascinating thing about Christmas in 1855 is how close the holiday still was to the realities of nineteenth-century life. Toronto was a city of immigrants, workers, merchants, labourers, professionals and families living in very different circumstances. Some homes would have been warm and comfortable, while others would have been cold, and crowded. There were no modern hospitals, no antibiotics, no central heating and no easy way of escaping a harsh winter. Yet people celebrated, rich or poor.

They gathered around fireplaces, went to church, shared food, told stories and tried to make Christmas special. So when we walk through Toronto and imagine Christmas in 1855, we're not simply looking at an old-fashioned Christmas, we're stepping into a city where Christmas was beginning to take on many of the traditions we recognize today, but where life itself was more uncertain.

This tour explores old Toronto during the Christmas season of 1855. This walking tour is for all walking levels. The tour begins and ends at St. James Cathedral on King Street East at Church Street. A great way to kick off the season.

This tour has a ticketed price of $15.00.

title: Our Infinite and Inevitable Ends: Author Talk with A.D. Sui
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall (first floor)
description:
In this exciting author talk A.D. Sui will discuss their upcoming novel Our Infinite and Inevitable Ends, a sapphic cli-fi thriller, as well as science fiction's role in today's rapidly politically and technologically changing world. Question and answer period to follow.
This sapphic cli-fi thriller is a love letter to hope in the bleakest of times, combining the multiverse-bending drama of This Is How You Lose the Time War with the cat-and-mouse chase of Killing Eve.
On a near-future Earth devastated by climate change, Dr. Cassandra Barlowe is right where she wants to be: working on an island of floating trash in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, as far away from Dr. Yana Gulsvig as possible. Cas’s research on plastic-dissolving fungi is undervalued and underfunded, thanks to the invention of deleria, a drug that allows glimpses into different timelines. For the average user, it’s a way to view lost loved ones or experience a different life, but it also offers a glimpse into worlds where humanity has solved its many global crises. Now, most science funding is dedicated to trawling these different timelines, searching for a reality with the solution to the climate devastation.
But when Yana — the world’s leading expert on deleria and Cassandra’s ex-lover — is killed in a mysterious explosion in the hub of deleria research, taking the hope of reversing climate change with her, Cas is arrested on charges of domestic terrorism. Cas must delve through timelines to piece together what happened, while watching other versions of herself and Yana live out the life they could have had — happier, more in love. As brutal government agents close in and her addiction to deleria grows, Cas has to make a choice: live in the spiraling branches of reality, seeking closure for Yana’s death until the drug shatters her mind, or live in the now, even if that means embracing her own damaged self and fighting, however hopelessly, for her own future and that of humanity.

His most recent book, Accelerating Expansion: Philosophy and Physics with a Positive Cosmological Constant, explores some of the philosophical consequences of modern cosmology, focusing on the significance of the discovery of the accelerating expansion of the universe for our understanding of time, geometry, and physics.

Meet the Resident:
Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. Zanchetta uses textiles, texts, and hosts community workshops to create intimate works and spaces where we can unfold our curiosities, care and anxieties about what grows beside our feet. She holds a Master of Visual Studies from the University of Toronto (2023) and a BFA from OCAD University (2018).

title: Birds and Our Christmas Traditions
location: Mount Pleasant, Basement program room
description:
Birds are woven into the fabric of Christmas traditions, serving as powerful symbols of hope, renewal, and warmth during the winter months. Their presence during the holidays, whether through festive ornaments, songs, or sightings at feeders, recalls ancient lore that connects birds with messages of love and positivity. By inviting birds into our lives and honoring them through tradition, we not only support these treasured visitors but also embrace the spirit of Christmas—one of generosity, harmony, and the celebration of nature’s enduring beauty. Jim Mackiewicz is the owner of Wild Birds Unlimited and has been helping customers with backyard bird feeding and connecting to nature for 25 years.

title: Instructional Skills Workshop (ISW) (IN-PERSON) – December 9, 10, 11, 2026
location: DB 1014 Victor Philip Dahdaleh Bldg.
description:
This 3-day intensive workshop encourages examination of one’s teaching practices with feedback focused on the learning process rather than on the specific lesson content. The ISW engenders participatory learning and community building that can transfer back into the classroom. Participants work collaboratively in a small group setting of 4-5 participants to further develop their teaching effectiveness as they design and lead three 10-minute lessons. Following each, participants receive reflective verbal, written, and video feedback from the other participants who have been learners.
This certificate is open to all faculty members (research stream, teaching stream, contract).
This certificate is also available for graduate students with at least 3 years of teaching experience. Alternatively, graduate students are invited to complete the Teaching Assistant Certificate in Teaching (TACT) ( https://www.yorku.ca/teachingcommons/certificates/#tact ).
This is a three-day workshop series scheduled for Wednesday December 9, Thursday December 10, and Friday December 11. Each day will run from 9 am to 4:30 pm in DB 1014.
** Please kindly note: this is a 3-day workshop series intended for participants to attend  the entire workshop (all three days from 9am-4:30pm) in-person.
Register using our registration form ( https://teachingcommonsforms.apps01.yorku.ca/forms/view.php?id=1163054 ).

Early one morning, while delivering an order to the local convent, Bill makes a discovery which forces him to confront both his past and the complicit silences of a town controlled by the church. Already a bestseller in France and certain to be read worldwide for generations to come, Small Things Like These is a deeply affecting story of hope, quiet heroism, and empathy from one of our most critically lauded and iconic writers

title: Dec 10 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Dec 10, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-december-10-2026)**

**Your mAP is fine. Your slices are not. Finding the images that actually matter**

A single mAP can look acceptable while one slice is unusable, small objects, occlusion, or a confused class. I will run a pretrained detector on a few hundred public images (COCO-style, not a production crawl), report the headline metric, then break the same run by slice and walk through the worst samples.

The claim is modest: you do not need a million images or a trained-from-scratch model to see what the mean is hiding, and you cannot relabel everything, so the next labeling budget should follow those slices. No employer data and no confidential dashboards.

*About the Speaker*

[Amandeep Jiddewar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amanfj/) is a Machine Learning Engineer at Pinterest, with prior work in U.S. manufacturing analytics (CertainTeed / Saint-Gobain) and marketplace allocation (QuinStreet). Emory Goizueta MSBA (2019), Kaggle Expert. This talk is in his personal capacity and does not represent his current or prior employers.

**Production AI Agents: Tool Use, Evaluation, Guardrails and Observability**

Building an AI agent is easy. Knowing whether it is behaving reliably in production is much harder. This session explores how to evaluate agents that use tools and external systems, including tool-call validation, tracing, observability, failure analysis, guardrails, permissions, and human review.

Attendees will learn practical patterns for understanding not just what an agent answered, but why it acted and whether the action was safe.

*About the Speaker*

[Akshay Talathi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/akshaytalathi/) is a Vice President at Goldman Sachs with over 10 years of experience building large-scale, cloud-native, and distributed systems across financial services and technology. His current focus is GenAI and agentic AI, including production AI agents, MCP, enterprise integrations, guardrails, observability, and reliable AI-driven workflows.

**From Virtual Worlds to Physical AI: Building Simulation Pipelines That Survive the Real World**

Robots are moving beyond perception systems that only detect and classify objects toward systems that must understand a scene, learn behaviors, and act in the physical world. In this talk, I’ll show a practical Physical AI workflow using OpenUSD, BowerBot, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to build a robot’s virtual world, including its body, cameras, sensors, and environment.

We’ll explore how demonstrations and reinforcement learning can teach behaviors in simulation, how vision and sensor data become observations for a robot policy, and what needs to match when transferring that behavior to real hardware. The demo follows a small robot from a simulated environment toward a real-world task, exposing both the power and the limitations of sim-to-real.

The goal is to make the path from pixels to actions concrete for computer vision and machine learning practitioners.

*About the Speaker*

[Arturo Morales Rangel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arturo-morales-rangel) is the founder of Binary Core LLC, a Physical AI engineering company working across simulation, perception, robot learning, and deployment.

**Prompting Video-Language Models in Production: Lessons from Enterprise Video Tagging and Evaluation**

Video-language models can now describe, tag and answer questions about long-form video, but production results depend heavily on prompt design and evaluation. This talk shares field lessons from deploying such models for media, news, streaming and sports organizations, including how to structure prompts for consistent, schema-bound outputs across hours of footage.

On one sports video-tagging project, consolidating the prompt definitions cut estimated processing cost about 3x, and about 90% of the originally reported issues were later resolved through prompting alone. I'll also walk through building evaluation frameworks for video outputs, including for hard domains like egocentric video, and what changes when migrating between model versions.

Attendees will leave with reusable prompt patterns and an evaluation checklist they can apply to their own video pipelines.

*About the Speaker*

[Yash Gugale](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yashgugale/) is a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at TwelveLabs in New York, integrating video foundation models (Marengo for embeddings and search, Pegasus for video-language understanding) for media, news, streaming and sports customers. He previously spent about six years in video streaming engineering at Peloton and Samsung TV Plus, and holds an MS in Computer Graphics Technology from Purdue.

title: Aesthetics Reading Group (Alexandra King, Simon Fraser University)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Aesthetics Reading Group is pleased to welcome as guest speaker Alexandra King, associate professor in the Department of Philosophy at Simon Fraser University. Currently, she is thinking through what aesthetic normativity looks like: the shape it takes, its parallels and interactions with other varieties of normativity (like the moral and epistemic), and whether it can be said to exist at all. Within aesthetics, she is also interested in an assortment of issues, including subtlety, high and low art, aesthetic/artistic agency, and applied arts. She also owns, runs, and regularly writes for the aesthetics and philosophy of art blog Aesthetics for Birds, which aims to make concepts and arguments in academic aesthetics accessible to a wide, public audience.

title: Ghost Stories of Toronto: Modern Phantoms
description:
As Toronto has grown into a major metropolis, its ghost stories have grown along with it. Many of our city's most bone-chilling tales were born out of that rapid evolution — and the sense of unease it has often caused. We'll conclude this series of talks with author Adam Bunch by exploring ghost stories from Toronto's more recent past. We'll take the subway with the spectre believed to haunt the TTC, set sail with the ghost ship of Etobicoke Creek, and meet the demon said to have terrorized one of Canada's most famous folk singers.
About this event's guest:
Adam Bunch
Read More:
The Toronto Book of Love
The Toronto Book of the Dead
About this series:
You can learn a lot about Toronto through its ghost stories. Whether you believe in the supernatural or not, the tales we tell about spirits and spectres illuminate the true history of the city. They're often tied to dramatic stories of death and disaster, to fascinating historic sites, and to pivotal moments that helped shape our communities. In this series of talks by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore Toronto's past through tales of ghosts, séances and hauntings. Whether it's phantom horses from the War of 1812, the strange prime minister who believed in the occult, or the ghost who was arrested by the Toronto Police Morality Squad, these supernatural stories have a lot to teach us about the history of the place we call home.

title: Early Modern Philosophy Research Interest Group (Andreea Mihali, Wilfrid Laurier)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Early Modern Philosophy Research Interest Group is pleased to welcome as its guest speaker Andreea Mihali (Wilfrid Laurier University) who is an expert in critical thinking, informal logic and argumentation theory, modern philosophy (Descartes to Kant) and visual and musical arguments. 
Talk Title
Descartes’ Omissions 
Talk Abstract
In the Meditations Descartes insists that readers closely follow the example and meditating steps set out in this text (AT VII, 10; CSM II, 8). Given this emphasis on the right order of reasons, it is at least prima facie surprising to also find the following remarks in the Second Replies: “Moreover there are many truths which although it is vital to be aware of them – this method [analysis] often scarcely mentions since they are transparently clear to anyone who gives them his attention” (AT VII, 156; CSM II, 110 – emphasis added).  
A careful reading of Descartes’ works shows that such remarks regarding things left out of Descartes’ actual text are far from being unique. This paper aims to classify Descartes’ omissions, to inquire into what these omissions tell us about Descartes’ approach and to make some preliminary remarks about the light these omissions shed on his explicit statements and theses. 
After discussing and backing up with textual evidence seven criteria of classification of omissions (content-relatedness, scope, means of identification, deliberateness, motivation, purpose and who is expected to remedy these omissions), I will apply them to Descartes’ published works. This application will show that Descartes’ account of the progression of his published works in the Preface to the French Principles (progression from the Discourse and the three accompanying Essays, through the Meditations, to the Principles – Latin and French), this progression in effect also tracks omissions and corresponding additions.

title: Film Screening: ᑕᐅᑐᒃᑕᕗᒃ / Tautuktavuk / What We See
location: Malvern, Community Room
description:
Join us to watch ᑕᐅᑐᒃᑕᕗᒃ / Tautuktavuk / What We See in Inuktitut with English Subtitles.
The film screening will include an 82 minute film and a 20 minute pre-recorded Q&A (102 minutes total).
Blurring the line between narrative and non-fiction, Uyarak and her eldest sister Saqpinak, embark on a difficult healing journey after a traumatic event that reminds them of the importance of community, culture, and family.
Feel free to drop in, no registration required. Registering will send you a reminder before the event.
SYNOPSIS: After experiencing a traumatic event in Igloolik (an Inuit hamlet in Foxe Basin, Qikiqtaaluk Region in Nunavut), Uyarak leaves her community and family in Nunavut to live in Montréal. When Covid-19 lockdowns close off the Canadian Arctic from the rest of the world, Uyarak is further separated from her closest friend, eldest sister, Saqpinak. This extreme situation blurs the lines of both the fictional lives of the sisters, and the non-fiction lives of the film’s directors, Lucy Tulugarjuk and Carol Kunnuk, who play the sisters. The film becomes a series of vignettes of heartache and healing – both in the dramatic based-on-true-events narrative, and the lived reality of these characters and creators. Uyarak doesn’t remember much about one terrible night of domestic violence, but Saqpinak does. Through Zoom calls, Uyarak talks about healing from years of trauma and abuse, and how the counselling sessions she goes to, and other cultural reconnections, are helping her heal. At the same time, Saqpinak is raising a family and hosting live shows about her community. Things are difficult at home – Saqpinak herself is experiencing domestic abuse at home but is waiting to talk about this to Uyarak when she can get home. When Covid-19 restrictions ease, Uyarak is finally able to travel home to Igloolik. At home, she embarks on a deeper healing journey visiting with family and elders, in town, and out on the land. Uyarak and Saqpinak share more stories and support one another in their short time together before Uyarak must return to Montréal.
ABOUT THE CO-DIRECTORS: Lucy Tulugarjuk is an award-winning actor, creative performer, and the Executive Director of Nunavut Independent Television Network (NITV). NITV created Canada’s first 24/7 Inuit language television station, Uvagut TV. Lucy is the co-writer, director of Tia and Piujuq, and assistant director for Zacharias Kunuk’s, One Day in the Life of Noah Piugattuk. In addition to her work in film and television, Lucy is a skilled Inuktitut translator. Carol Kunnuk is a filmmaker working in independent television and film with Isuma for over 25 years as a writer, camera operator, production supervisor, assistant director, actor, and editor. Her personal work includes the short, Being Prepared (NFB), and creator/director of the documentary, Attagatuluk. Carol currently directs and produces Welcome to my Qammaq, a weekly live television show broadcasting across Canada on Uvagut TV.

title: Nerikomi with Eiko Maeda | Nov 14 & 15 2026 | Dupont
location: 300 Campbell Avenue, Unit 115 Join us for a two-day workshop with ceramic artist Eiko Maeda, exploring the traditional Japanese technique of Nerikomi. Unlike surface decoration, Nerikomi builds pattern directly into the clay body itself, layering, stacking, and folding differently coloured clays until intricate designs run through the material from edge to edge. Over two days, you'll learn to prepare and condition coloured clays, build your own pattern blocks and work through four distinct pattern designs, each resulting in a finished ceramic piece approximately 15 cm in diameter. Eiko will guide you through every stage, from initial slab to shaped, refined form. This workshop is open to makers at all levels. No prior experience with Nerikomi is required, though some familiarity with hand-building is an asset. ABOUT EIKO MAEDA Eiko Maeda trained in Japanese lacquer at Joshibi University of Art and Design in Tokyo before discovering ceramics after relocating to Canada. She has spent over a decade developing and teaching her Nerikomi practice from her studio in Ontario, and has been recognized by the Ontario Arts Council and the Toronto Outdoor Art Fair. In 2026, her work was exhibited in Taipei, Taiwan. PLEASE NOTE Firing is included in the registration fee. Finished works will be available for pick-up approximately 3–4 weeks after the workshop concludes. You will be notified by email when your pieces are ready. All Specialty tools will be available for usage with the option to purchase your tools at the end of the course., Toronto, ON

title: Série Portraits et autoportraits: Portraits et autoportraits supports d’une esthétique radicale
description:
Les expérimentations plastiques radicales du XXe siècles ne signifièrent en rien la fin des portraits et des autoportraits. Loin de devenir de simples prétextes, le genre fut au contraire renouvelé par les nouvelles solutions formelles issues du Fauvisme et du Cubisme, mais aussi par les arts décoratifs. Les réseaux d’ornements imaginés par Gustav Klimt concoururent ainsi à magnifier ses modèles tout en préservant leur sensibilité. Quant aux aplats de couleur avec lesquels Henri Matisse ou André Derain architecturent leurs autoportraits, ils traduisent leur vie intérieure avec plus d’intensité encore. Autant de recherches qui ouvrent la voie à l’art contemporain.
Cette conférence vous est proposée par Gilles Genty, historien de l’art, en partenariat avec l’
Alliance française de Toronto
.

description:

～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events

Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate

RSVP open: 5:00 PM

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

description:
This class is for beginners who are curious about buying an Android phone or tablet, or who have acquired one and want to install apps. Android phones include those manufactured by Samsung, Google, Motorola, and OnePlus.

In this beginner's class, you will learn about:
- what apps are, and the benefits of using them
- the differences between pre-installed, free, and paid apps
- how to access and use the Google Play Store
- how to evaluate, download and use apps

At the end of the class, you will have a basic understanding of how to install apps on your Android device through the Google Play Store.

Bring your own device: if you have an Android device, feel free to bring it with you and follow along with the exercises.

Prerequisites:  None
Format:  Lecture with hands-on exercises
[90 min]

location: Woodside Square, Program room
description:
Join us on the following Monday afternoons to discuss books in a friendly and social atmosphere: September 14th, October 19th, November 9th, and December 14th.
This month we will be reading
The MANIAC
by Benjamin Labatut.
The MANIAC
is a 2023 novel by Chilean author Benjamin Labatut, and his first in English (compared to his usual Spanish). It is a fictionalized biography of polymath John von Neumann interwoven with tripartite narratives exploring the intersection of human genius, rationality, and artificial intelligence.Told via oral-history style from peers, wives, and colleagues, Labatut attempts to decipher core themes of reason and madness, the edge of progress, and the loss of the sacred. While a spiritual sequel to
When We Cease to Understand the World
,
no prior knowledge of science or technology is needed to appreciate Labatut's polymathic portrait of von Neumann.
Participants can borrow a copy of the book from the Woodside Square branch upon registration.

title: Above the Fire by Michael O'Donnell

Post-Apocalyptic Book Club - Toronto Chapter
It's our last PABC meetup of 2026!

This time we'll be reading *Above the Fire* by Michael O'Donnell. Here's the blurb:

Laboring under a shared loss, a father and son set out on a late-season backpacking trip through the mountains of New Hampshire. They find beauty and solidarity in the outdoors, making friends along the way and falling into the rhythms of an expedition. But when war breaks out during their hike, they are forced to withdraw even further into the backcountry.

Surviving an alpine winter by themselves, father and son must endure the elements, the solitude, and the ever-present danger of outsiders. As their isolation intensifies, their bond with each other grows more fierce. From their mountain refuge they must confront the perils of a changed world until they are forced to decide whether--and how--to rejoin society.

title: Peek Inside an AI Assistant: How It Thinks and Works
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
You've asked an AI chatbot questions. But there's another kind of AI that doesn't just answer: it acts.
In this demo-driven talk with our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, we'll look deeply at always-on personal AI assistants. The assistant can read your files, use your apps, and remember what you've told it, growing more useful over time. The same powers that let it help you can hurt you if something goes wrong. We'll also open up what happens inside: the hidden instructions, the tools it uses, what it remembers and forgets.
Then we'll look at the AI assistant that helped develop this workshop, and how we shaped our workflow together, and why.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

title: ABCD Reads Exit Party by Emily St. John Mandel
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***[Exit Party](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4792123)*** by Emily St. John Mandel (author of ***Station Eleven***).
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/5182568441053184) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"From the bestselling author of Station Eleven, Exit Party is Emily St. John Mandel’s epic new story of crimes committed and loves lost across worlds and decades.
2031\. America is at war with itself\, but for the first time in weeks there is some hope: the Republic of California has been declared\, the curfew in Los Angeles is lifted\, and everyone in the city is going to a party\.
Ari, newly released from prison, arrives with her friend Gloria just as a fragile new era begins. But there are people at the party who shouldn’t be there. Something is very wrong...
Years later, living a different life in Paris, Ari remains haunted by that night. Whatever happened at the party fractured her sense of reality – and may hold the key to a very different world.
Freedom and surveillance, art and survival, love and loss in a broken world: Exit Party is the electrifying new novel from Emily St. John Mandel." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/241683548-exit-party?ac=1&from_search=true&qid=8V5Hrtzu0U&rank=1))

"A novel of doubles, shadow worlds, and fractured timelines as a man disappears from a glittering Los Angeles party, and a woman—a gunrunner, an art collector, an operative of the State—searches for answers." (from [BookMarks.reviews](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/exit-party/))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Sven Beckert: A Global History of Capitalism
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL and Toronto Metropolitan University present historian Sven Beckert in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
As the Laird Bell Professor of History at Harvard University and co-chair of the university's Program on the Study of Capitalism, Sven Beckert has spent his career tracing how a single economic system came to structure nearly every aspect of modern life, how we work, how we think about ourselves and others, and how we organize our politics.
In
Capitalism: A Global History
, Beckert reveals that capitalism was born global, corresponding at no point to an idealized dream of free markets; from the outset, state-backed institutions, imperial expansion, and coercion shaped its dynamics as much as innovation and exchange did. Along the way, capitalism has both expanded political voice for some and violently foreclosed it for others, entangled from its origins with slavery, colonialism, and profound inequality.
How do we distinguish between capitalism's capacity to generate genuine prosperity and its tendency to concentrate power in ways that undermine democratic institutions? What can nearly a thousand years of capitalist history teach us about the conditions under which economic systems support, rather than erode, democratic life? And as we confront what many call a crisis of late-stage capitalism, what possibilities remain for reimagining an economic order more compatible with democratic values?
Join one of the world's foremost historians of capitalism for an essential conversation about the deep entanglement of markets and democracy, and what history suggests about the road ahead.
Question and answer session and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this Event's Guests:
Sven Beckert
Sanjay Ruparelia
Read More:
Capitalism
Empire of Cotton
***
This event is part of our
On Civil Society
series, where we host local and international authors, activists and academics in conversation about the most critical topics of our time. Generously supported by the McConnell Foundation and also by Chris M. Reid.
***
About the series:
On the Frontlines of Democracy
is a public lecture series to analyze the trajectory of democracy in the twenty-first century.
In every region, the prospects of democracy face serious challenges, old and new. Can we protect constitutional rights and renew collective self-rule in an era of popular mistrust, severe partisanship and resurgent nationalism? Can they reduce inequalities of power, wealth and status, defend deep diversity and confront climate change in the new digital age? Can we develop innovative strategies to revitalize civic engagement, empower public institutions and resist autocratic threats? And what can we offer, learn and do to promote the prospects of democracy in our increasingly post-western global order?

title: AI At Home: No Cloud, No Account
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your AI didn't need the internet at all: no subscription, no one recording what you type?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll see AI models running entirely on one computer, with no connection and no data leaving the room. We'll compare a small local model against a powerful cloud model and plain search: what each gets right, what each costs, and what the privacy trade-offs really are. You'll leave with a decision sheet for your own hardware, an installation recipe, and an honest look at what "open" really means when it comes to AI.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

title: The Delicious and Surprising History of The Dining Room: Author Talk with John Ota
location: Deer Park, Room 204
description:
John Ota presents​ and discusses his book
The Dining Room
.
Explore the stories behind twelve iconic dining rooms in homes around the world—from a Japanese samurai house to Claude Monet's brilliant yellow dining room to Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul to Jackie Kennedy’s White House—and travel through time in pursuit of the ultimate design.​
The Dining Room is an enlightening and joyous celebration of history, culture and the art of dining. Presenter John Ota's charming observations of the surprising impact of dining rooms on our lives and the cherished moments we share within them will delight armchair travelers, history fanatics and interior design enthusiasts alike.
John Ota has been involved with architecture and design since 1978, with degrees from Columbia University, the University of Toronto and the University of British Columbia. His bestselling book
The Kitchen
was a 2021 Taste Canada Awards finalist and a 2021 Paris Gourmand Cookbook finalist in the book design category. After working in architecture in Toronto, New York, and Vancouver, and as lead on multiple Ontario Ministry of Culture projects, John now loves to travel the world visiting historic houses, cooking regional food, and meeting people of all backgrounds.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: How Do AIs "Think"? And Why They Get Things Wrong
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
How does a machine actually "think"? Explore the history and latest developments of machine learning.
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, we'll dig into what's really going on inside AI systems: how they decide what matters in your question, where their training data comes from (and who's missing from it), and how hidden instructions can sneak into content and hijack an AI. Develop an intuitive understanding of how AIs "think" without the math. We'll talk about how AIs remember, how they don't and how they are both similar and different to humans. And we'll ask the question underneath it all: is there anyone home inside the machine?
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

title: Club de lecture théâtre avec le Théâtre français de Toronto
location: Toronto Reference Library, Discussion Room, 3e étage
description:
La Bibliothèque publique de Toronto et le
Théâtre français de Toronto
s'associent pour créer un club de lecture théâtre. Ce rendez-vous mensuel est l'occasion de discuter et d'explorer des scènes mythiques ayant marqué le monde du théâtre. Avec
Georges Som
, médiateur culturel, nous essayerons de comprendre les enjeux de ces scènes, de découvrir leurs sens et de partager nos sentiments sur leurs auteurs et autrices. Chacun est le bienvenu au club, qu'il soit néophyte ou amateur de théâtre confirmé. Les seuls prérequis pour participer sont la curiosité et le plaisir d'échanger autour du théâtre !
Au mois de décembre, nous allons discuter un extrait de la pièce
En attendant Godot
de Samuel Beckett. Deux vagabonds, Vladimir et Estragon, se retrouvent sur une route de campagne, près d'un arbre, à la tombée de la nuit. Est-ce bien le jour et l'heure pour attendre Godot. Arrivent Pozzo, un homme autoritaire, le propriétaire des lieux, avec un Knouk, un sous homme tenu en laisse.

title: Shannon Kyles: What Our Buildings Say About Us
location: Bloor/Gladstone
description:
Shannon Kyles discusses the history of architecture in Ontario and what it says about the people who have built this province. Starting with the Indigenous people, going through the first century of European contact, through the 20th century wars, democratic policies that resulted, and finally onto the 21st century speculative housing practice.
Professor Shannon Kyles is the author of ​
The Story of Ontario Architecture
. She has written and published articles on architecture, taught History of Ontario architecture for 42 years at Mohawk College and online for universities, and has served on the board of the Architectural Conservancy of Ontario for 15 years.

title: Internet Horror Classics on Film: Backrooms
description:
In this final instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series Internet Horror Classics on Film, actor Erin Mick and critic Michael LaPointe join host Adam Nayman to discuss Kane Parsons' debut film, Backrooms, which bends the liminal spaces that have haunted the internet for years into a mesmerizing horror film.
About this event's guests:
Erin Mick
is an actor and writer based in Toronto. Her doctoral research centers on contemporary horror cinema, with particular interest in emergent modes of fan/viewer engagement, as well as horror's relationship to and mobilization of notions of trauma and collective memory. Erin also works as an actor, and is a writer of horror fiction.
Michael LaPointe
is a novelist, critic, journalist and producer in Toronto, Canada. He has published a novel with Random House Canada, written for The New Yorker, The Atlantic, and The Paris Review, and produced series for BBC Radio 4. He is a regular contributor to the Times Literary Supplement. His second novel, Ruby Red, will be released in spring 2027.
Adam Nayman
is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. He is a regular contributor to The Ringer, a lecturer at the University of Toronto's Cinema Studies Institute, and he has written on film for The New Yorker and The New York Times.
Read more:
The Creep

How do animals live in extreme cold where temperatures can reach −50°C or lower? Through a combination of physical adaptations, behavioral strategies, specialized senses and remarkable biological processes they are able to thrive. Become a page-turner by joining the Between the Lines Book Club! Here, we embark on a new chapter with every read, diving into a world of endless possibilities. Friday November 16: A Gentleman in Moscow by Amor Towles
Set in Moscow in 1922,
A Gentleman in Moscow
by Amor Towles follows Count Alexander Rostov, a refined Russian aristocrat sentenced by a Bolshevik tribunal to house arrest in the grand Metropol Hotel, where he must spend the rest of his life confined within its walls. As the world outside undergoes dramatic political and social change, the Count gradually transforms his restricted circumstances into a life rich with unexpected friendships, meaningful encounters, and quiet adventures. From navigating the hotel's intricate social world to forming a particularly meaningful bond with a young girl named Nina, Rostov discovers new perspectives on love, loyalty, personal growth, and the passage of time. Elegant, witty, and deeply moving, the novel explores the nature of freedom, the importance of human connection, and the possibility of finding purpose and beauty even when life takes an unexpected turn.

description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events

Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:
Once you enter the "Waiting-list", we will message you for the payment via e-transfer. After your payment is confirmed, you will be moved to the "Going-list"

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

@tjex.ca

title: Mission of Gravity - Hal Clement
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi everybody,

Back for another team investigating an alien planet. This time we have a true classic, Hal Clement's seminal 1954 gritty sci fi novel, *Missions of Gravity*. This one has been on the list for a while and I'm so glad it was on theme enough to get on the survey.

Book of the Month
*Mission of Gravity* \- Hal Clement \(1954\)

From a good review on Skiffy.ca, "Originally serialized in 1953 in the magazine *[Astounding Science Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analog_Science_Fiction_and_Fact)*, the tale was published in book form the following year. Decades later, it was awarded a [Retro Hugo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Award#Retro_Hugos), for excellence in SF’s pioneering era.

*Mission of Gravity* is an archetypal example of what the kids call “hard science fiction”, a subgenre in which the characters within the SF story solve physical problems with physical –largely technological– means. The science tends to be solid, even the speculative science, and the rules are intensely consistent within the boundaries of the story."

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

description:
TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

Toronto Babel is a welcoming, inclusive, and safe space for everyone. title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Festival Select: Sorcerer (William Friedkin, 1977)
location: North York Central Library, Room 101
description:
Join the Society and Recreation department of the North York Central Library for monthly screenings of fiction and non-fiction films that push the boundaries of the medium. This month we are showing William Friedkin's
Sorcerer
(1977).
Synopsis (The Criterion Collection): A hallucinatory journey into the heart of darkness, William Friedkin’s pulse-pounding reimagining of the suspense classic
The Wages of Fear
was dismissed upon its release, only to be recognized decades later as one of the New Hollywood’s boldest auteur statements. In a remote Latin American village, four desperate fugitives—a New Jersey gangster (Roy Scheider), a Mexican assassin (Francisco Rabal), an unscrupulous Parisian businessman (Bruno Cremer), and an Arab terrorist (Amidou)—take on a doomed mission: transporting two trucks full of highly explosive nitroglycerin through the treacherous jungle. Aided by Tangerine Dream’s otherworldly synth score, Friedkin turns each bump in the road into a tour de force of cold-sweat tension—conjuring a hauntingly nihilistic vision of a world ruled by chance and fate.
No registration required.

Get your spook on with this month's scary movie screening of
Black Christmas
(1974), directed by Bob Clark.
A prototype of the American slasher,
Black Christmas
wears its Giallo influences on its sleeve and sets a blueprint for genre films like John Carpenter's
Halloween
(1977). Shot in Toronto, the film follows a group of sorority girls over their winter break as they are harassed by a series of disturbing phone calls.
Black Christmas
has a running time of 1 hour and 37 minutes, and is rated R.
There will be a short introduction to the film followed by the screening, which will be accompanied by closed captions.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.
